entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint: Working Towards 2050 (published 2022 by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore, MPA) and its implementing incentive architecture, the Maritime Singapore Green Initiative (MSGI, refreshed 2024), as a strategic coordinating framework and a set of voluntary, incentive-based programmes -- not a single binding regulation carrying private-party penalties. It exists to give a freight forwarder with Singapore port exposure (ocean transhipment, bunkering, or harbour craft logistics) a single place to see which MSGI programmes carry concession eligibility, deadlines, and monitoring triggers.

FACT: "The Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint: Working Towards 2050 charts ambitious and concrete long-term strategies to build a sustainable Maritime Singapore." Developed by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) in consultation with industry partners. *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint, MPA, 2022. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-decarbonisation-blueprint

*Analytical inference:* the Blueprint itself creates no obligation running to a freight forwarder; its implementing instruments (the MSGI's five programmes, addressed in Section 8) are what carry actionable eligibility criteria and deadlines.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The Blueprint, published in 2022, outlines seven focus areas, which MPA will focus on to support the decarbonisation of the maritime industry: Port terminals; Domestic harbour craft; Future marine fuels, bunkering standards and infrastructure; Singapore Registry of Ships; Efforts at IMO and other international platforms; Research & development and talent; and Carbon awareness, carbon accounting and green financing." *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint, MPA, 2022. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-decarbonisation-blueprint

FACT: "The Maritime Singapore Green Initiative (MSGI) seeks to reduce the environmental impact of shipping and related activities and to promote clean and green shipping in Singapore." *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

FACT: "In 2024, MPA updated various green initiatives and incentives under the MSGI to encourage early adoption of zero and near-zero emission technologies and fuels." MPA will commit another S$50 million to support the implementation of the refreshed MSGI which comprises of five programmes. *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

*Operational implication:* a workspace whose ocean carriers call at the Port of Singapore, or whose contracted harbour craft operate in Singapore waters, is exposed through the commercial consequence of carrier/craft eligibility for MSGI concessions (Section 8), not through a direct duty on the workspace itself.

FACT: "From 1 January 2025 until 31 December 2027, MPA will provide up to 100% port dues concession to ocean-going vessels calling at the Port of Singapore"[, described fully in Section 8]. *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**WINDOW CLOSING** -- FACT: "The application window for the EEG (base tier) is until 31 March 2027." Port-sector operators eligible for co-funding under the Green Port Infrastructure Programme should confirm eligibility and submit before this date. *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

**MONITORING** -- the Green Ship Programme and Green Craft Programme concession windows are open now; workspaces whose contracted ocean carriers or harbour craft operators may qualify for port dues concessions should confirm eligibility against the published criteria before contract renewals.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific carrier's port-call cost savings under these concessions are contractually passed through to the workspace's freight rates is a carrier-specific commercial question outside this brief's scope.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Blueprint and MSGI create obligations and incentives at the vessel-owner, ship-operator, and harbour-craft-operator layer, not at the freight-forwarder or NVOCC layer directly.

**As freight forwarder / NVOCC:** *Analytical inference:* not the direct target of vessel-level obligations (EEDI, CII, fuel-tier criteria) -- those fall on the vessel owner or operator. The workspace is exposed through the commercial consequence: carriers qualifying for MSGI concessions price port calls differently from those that do not.

**As shipper / cargo principal using Singapore harbour craft:** *Analytical inference:* port-side logistics (lightering, ship-to-shore transfer) rely on MPA-licensed harbour craft; the Green Craft Programme's mandate trajectory (Section 8) means the craft operators serving the workspace's cargo are subject to phased fuel and technology criteria.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any carbon-accounting or green-financing reporting duty under the Blueprint's seventh focus area applies to freight forwarders or shippers, as distinct from vessel and port operators, requires legal confirmation against the specific implementing instrument.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "MPA and the International Energy Agency (IEA) signed an MoU on the Energy Transition of the Maritime and Port Industries and announced the partnership at the event." The MoU will enable the sharing of best practices across maritime and energy industries, support the adoption and transition of zero and near-zero emission fuels by these industries through capacity building training programmes, and contribute to relevant fuel-related projects and initiatives such as the IMO-Singapore NextGEN and NextGEN Connect Initiatives. *Source: MPA -- Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping

FACT: "development of the IEA Regional Cooperation Centre to be hosted by Singapore"[, as part of the same MoU]. *Source: MPA -- Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping

*Analytical inference:* the IEA-MPA MoU and the IMO-Singapore NextGEN/NextGEN Connect Initiatives named in it are the authoritative international channels through which Singapore's implementing instruments are expected to evolve; a workspace tracking IMO-aligned scenario planning should monitor both.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The exported forward-events record for this item carries four rows, all describing the same underlying IMO 2023 GHG Strategy checkpoint fact; each is listed below rather than collapsed, per this item's own export.

1. (target year 2030) FACT: "with indicative checkpoints to reach by 2030 (cut GHG emissions by at least 20%, striving for 30%), and 2040 (cut GHG emissions by at least 70%, striving for 80%). The targets are for the entire shipping sector." *Source: MPA -- Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping
2. (target year 2030) Same underlying checkpoint fact, cited above (the export's second row restates it).
3. (target year 2030) Same underlying checkpoint fact, cited above (the export's third row restates it).
4. (target year 2040) Same quoted sentence also states the second checkpoint (cut GHG emissions by at least 70%, striving for 80%), cited above.

FACT: "We are on track to adopt mid-term measures by late 2025 to cut GHG emissions, to reach net zero targets." These mid-term measures, which are currently being discussed by Member States, include a goal-based marine fuel standard, and a pricing mechanism for maritime GHG emissions. *Source: MPA -- Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping

*Analytical inference:* adoption of IMO mid-term measures, if it proceeded on the stated late-2025 schedule, is the single highest-consequence upstream trigger for Singapore's implementing instruments. Re-check window: the IMO MEPC docket, next two sessions.

FACT: "Insights from the EOI submissions will inform the development of the methanol bunkering regulatory framework to ensure the safe and efficient supply of methanol as a marine fuel in Singapore at a commercial scale." *Source: MPA -- Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping

*Analytical inference:* the methanol bunkering regulatory framework is explicitly described as under development, not yet published; given the EOI volume (Section 13), publication is plausible within the current MSGI programme window (through 31 December 2027).

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this framework create direct regulatory obligations on private freight operators?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Blueprint and MSGI are a strategic framework and voluntary incentive programmes. Obligations described in Section 8 attach to vessel owners, ship operators, and harbour craft operators applying for concessions -- not to freight forwarders or NVOCCs directly. Whether a specific Singapore port-call contract passes a compliance condition down to a private operator is a fact-specific question requiring counsel review.

**Q2: Is participation in any MSGI programme mandatory for a workspace's contracted carriers?**

*Analytical inference:* no. Every MSGI programme (GSP, GCP, GPIP/EEG, GETP, GAP) is described in the source pool as voluntary, incentive-based; a carrier or craft operator that does not apply simply forgoes the concession and bears the standard port dues cost.

**Q3: Does the Blueprint's carbon-accounting focus area create a reporting duty on the workspace?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* see Section 4 -- the source pool does not state whether freight forwarders or shippers, as distinct from vessel/port operators, carry any reporting duty under this focus area.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a voluntary incentive architecture, not a binding regulatory instrument. "Substantive requirements" here means each programme's own stated eligibility criteria (the conditions an applicant must meet to receive the stated concession or grant) plus the operational implications those criteria carry for a freight forwarder as a user of the resulting carrier/craft/port-cost structure.*

**1. Green Ship Programme -- SRS vessel criteria.** FACT: "Exceed International Maritime Organization’s (IMO) MARPOL Annex VI Phase 3 Energy Efficiency Design Index (EEDI) requirements by 10% or more; Adopt low-carbon fuelled engine; Adopt zero-carbon coupled with near-zero emissions fuelled engine; Adopt zero-emission fuelled engine/technology; or Achieve Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) Rating A." *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

*Operational implication:* a workspace whose contracted carriers flag SRS-registered vessels meeting any one of these five criteria may see lower registration-fee/tonnage-tax pass-through from that carrier.

**2. Green Ship Programme -- ocean-going vessel port dues concession.** FACT: "From 1 January 2025 until 31 December 2027, MPA will provide up to 100% port dues concession to ocean-going vessels calling at the Port of Singapore" *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

*Operational implication:* qualifying carriers receive up to 100% port dues concession; carriers that do not qualify carry the full port dues cost through at least 31 December 2027.

**3. Green Craft Programme -- newbuild harbour craft port dues concession.** FACT: "For newbuild harbour craft registered from 1 January 2025 until 31 December 2027, MPA will provide up to 100% port dues concession that meet one of the criteria listed below: Use of low-carbon fuels; Use of zero-carbon fuel; or Use of zero-emission fuel/technology." *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

**4. Green Port Programme legacy craft -- continuation waiver.** FACT: "will continue to enjoy the waiver of craft port dues until the end of 5-year validity period, or until 31 December 2027, whichever is earlier, provided that the craft (a) maintains the MPA licence, and (b) successfully demonstrates the use of zero-emission fuel/technology or zero/low carbon fuel throughout the year." *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

*Operational implication:* for workspaces contracting legacy-registered harbour craft, this waiver's continuation is conditional (licence maintenance plus annual demonstrated fuel/technology use), not automatic.

**5. Green Port Infrastructure Programme -- Energy Efficiency Grant tiers.** FACT: "helps businesses transition towards being more energy efficient by co-funding their investments in energy efficient equipment." pre-approved energy efficient equipment up to S$30,000; and an advanced tier to support companies for larger investments that drive greater energy efficiency. *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

**6. Energy Efficiency Grant -- per-company funding cap.** FACT: "Support is capped at S$350,000 per company across base and advanced tiers". *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

**7. Energy Efficiency Grant -- application deadline.** FACT: "The application window for the EEG (base tier) is until 31 March 2027." *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

**8. Green Awareness Programme -- Carbon Management MOU.** FACT: "The Green Awareness Programme is primarily driven by efforts under the Carbon Management Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between MPA, the United Nations Global Compact Network Singapore (GCNS), and various industry associations, including the Association of Regional Ferry Operators (ARFO), the Association of Singapore Marine Industries (ASMI), the Singapore Association of Ship Supplies and Services (SASS), and the Singapore Shipping Association (SSA)." *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

*Analytical inference:* obligation 9 surveyed but excluded from the workspace-adjacent count below -- the Green Energy and Technology Programme (GETP) funds Singapore-based maritime companies' own pilot trials of green technology (FACT: "The GETP aims to encourage Singapore-based maritime companies to develop and / or conduct pilot trials for green technologies that can help vessels meet the 2023 IMO Strategy on Reduction of GHG Emissions from Ships targets." *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative) -- this is a technology-vendor-facing grant, not a criterion affecting a freight forwarder's carrier/craft cost structure, so it is surveyed but not counted as workspace-adjacent.

No source in this pool states a compliance deadline, fine, or penalty running to a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary for non-participation in any MSGI programme; every programme above is voluntary and incentive-based.

No exceptions are stated in Sections covering the Green Ship, Green Craft, Green Port Infrastructure, Green Energy and Technology, and Green Awareness Programmes' eligibility criteria.

No scope limits are stated in Sections covering the Green Ship, Green Craft, Green Port Infrastructure, Green Energy and Technology, and Green Awareness Programmes' eligibility criteria.

Obligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 8.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Applications for GSP, GCP, and EEG concessions are made through MPA's own referenced circulars (Shipping Circular No. 12 of 2024, Port Marine Circulars No. 13 and No. 15 of 2024) and the GoBusiness Singapore website; the full text of these circulars is not in the retrieved source pool.

FACT: "The application window for the EEG (base tier) is until 31 March 2027." Applications for the Energy Efficiency Grant (base tier) are made through the GoBusiness Singapore website. *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether freight forwarders or cargo principals operating through Singapore can become signatories to the Carbon Management MOU, and what reporting duties would attach, requires direct inquiry with MPA and GCNS.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: because this is an incentive architecture rather than a binding regulatory instrument, "operational system requirements" here means the monitoring and documentation infrastructure a workspace should maintain to track carrier/craft eligibility, not a technical system the Blueprint itself mandates.*

**CII rating monitoring.** *Analytical inference:* workspaces whose contracted carriers claim GSP concessions based on CII Rating A need to track that annual metric, since it must be maintained each year of the concession period, not certified once.

**GCP craft demonstration.** FACT: "will continue to enjoy the waiver of craft port dues until the end of 5-year validity period, or until 31 December 2027, whichever is earlier, provided that the craft (a) maintains the MPA licence, and (b) successfully demonstrates the use of zero-emission fuel/technology or zero/low carbon fuel throughout the year." *Source: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative

*Operational implication:* for workspaces that manage or contract MPA-licensed harbour craft, this creates an annual metering and documentation obligation distinct from the initial incentive application.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section as of the export date -- no exemption or edge-case provision was located in the retrieved source pool for the Blueprint's implementing instruments; every eligibility criterion in Section 8 is stated as an affirmative condition, never a carve-out from a broader duty.*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "Over 60 regional and international companies comprising energy companies, fuel suppliers, traders, bunker operators, and storage companies, participated in the EOI in response to MPA's expression of interest for methanol as a marine fuel in Singapore, which received a total of 50 submissions." *Source: MPA -- Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping

FACT: "On aggregate, these projects have the potential to supply over one MTPA of low-carbon methanol by 2030, subject to commercial decisions and global developments." *Source: MPA -- Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping

FACT: "the demand for methanol as a marine fuel in Singapore can potentially exceed one million tons per annum (MTPA) before 2030, subject to the pace of developments of supply chains, infrastructure, and regulations globally." *Source: MPA -- Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping

FACT: "Approximately 40% of them proposed end-to-end solutions covering all three areas." *Source: MPA -- Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024. https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping

*Analytical inference:* the concentration of methanol supply proposals at Singapore positions it as a near-term methanol bunkering hub; for workspaces whose ocean carriers operate methanol-dual-fuel vessels, this is a route-feasibility signal, not yet a binding requirement.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 2022: Blueprint published by MPA; seven focus areas established.
- 2024: MSGI refreshed; S$50 million committed; five programmes established; IEA-MPA MoU signed.
- 1 January 2025: Green Ship Programme and Green Craft Programme concession windows open.
- 31 March 2027: Energy Efficiency Grant (base tier) application window closes.
- 31 December 2027: GSP and GCP concession windows close (unless extended).
- 2030: IMO 2023 GHG Strategy checkpoint (cut GHG emissions by at least 20%, striving for 30%, entire shipping sector).
- 2040: IMO 2023 GHG Strategy checkpoint (cut GHG emissions by at least 70%, striving for 80%).
- 2050: Blueprint headline target -- net-zero, sustainable Maritime Singapore.

*Source for timeline entries: MPA -- Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint, MPA, 2022 (https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-decarbonisation-blueprint); MPA -- Maritime Singapore Green Initiative, MPA, 2024 (https://www.mpa.gov.sg/maritime-singapore/sustainability/maritime-singapore-green-initiative); MPA -- Singapore gears up to meet net-zero needs of shipping, MPA, 17 April 2024 (https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/singapore-gears-up-to-meet-net-zero-needs-of-shipping).*

metadata.why_matters: MSGI concession eligibility (port dues, registration fee, and grant concessions running through 31 December 2027) shapes which carriers and harbour craft serving Singapore-routed cargo carry a cost advantage, and the methanol bunkering framework under development signals near-term fuel-optionality changes for ocean carriers.

Energy Efficiency Grant base tier cap S$30000
Energy Efficiency Grant total per-company cap S$350000
MSGI programme windows 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027
IMO 2023 GHG Strategy checkpoints: 2030 (20-30% cut) and 2040 (70-80% cut)
metadata.cost_mechanism: Up to 100% port dues, registration fee, and tonnage tax concessions for qualifying vessels/craft; up to 70% co-funding for qualifying port-sector energy-efficiency equipment, capped at S$350,000 per company.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks FACT: "Council Decision (EU) 2016/1764 of 29 September 2016" (CELEX 32016D1764), a short, two-Article, EU-internal position-fixing Decision -- not an instrument that itself regulates freight or aviation operators. It exists so a workspace tracking EU-ICAO cooperation instruments has an honest record of what this Decision does and does not do.

FACT: "The position to be taken by the Union within the EU-ICAO Joint Committee, as referred to in Article 7.3(c) of the Memorandum of Cooperation between the European Union and the International Civil Aviation Organization providing a framework for enhanced cooperation (the Memorandum of Cooperation), with regard to the adoption of an annex on Air Traffic Management to the Memorandum of Cooperation, shall be based on the draft Decision of the EU-ICAO Joint Committee, attached to this Decision." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2016/1764, EUR-Lex CELEX 32016D1764. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D1764

*Analytical inference:* this Decision does not itself enact the Air Traffic Management annex; it fixes the Union's own negotiating/voting position ahead of the EU-ICAO Joint Committee's separate adoption decision.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "It is appropriate to establish the position to be taken by the Union within the Joint Committee with regard to the adoption of an annex on Air Traffic Management to the Memorandum of Cooperation," *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2016/1764, EUR-Lex CELEX 32016D1764. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D1764

FACT: "The Memorandum of Cooperation between the European Union and the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) providing a framework for enhanced cooperation" entered into force on 29 March 2012. *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2016/1764, EUR-Lex CELEX 32016D1764. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D1764

*Operational implication:* this Decision creates no direct obligation on freight or aviation-sector operators. Any operational effect on air carriers or air navigation service providers would arise only once the Joint Committee itself adopts the referenced annex and it is implemented through a separate EU or Member State instrument -- neither of which is captured or evidenced in this source pool.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section as of the export date -- this is a two-Article, EU-internal position-fixing Decision with no operator-facing action item; see Section 5 for the one open confirmation question it leaves.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

This Decision governs only the European Union's own conduct within the EU-ICAO Joint Committee; it creates no compliance chain reaching a freight forwarder, carrier, or air navigation operator.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the EU-ICAO Joint Committee has since adopted the referenced Air Traffic Management annex, and if so through what instrument it took effect for operators, is not addressed by this Decision itself and requires confirmation against current EU-ICAO or EASA sources before any operational reliance.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Pursuant to Article 7.3(c) of the Memorandum of Cooperation, the Joint Committee established by Article 7.1 of the Memorandum of Cooperation may adopt annexes to the Memorandum of Cooperation." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2016/1764, EUR-Lex CELEX 32016D1764. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D1764

*Analytical inference:* this recital is the authoritative basis for why the Joint Committee, rather than the EU alone, is the body that will adopt the ATM annex; this Decision's own role is limited to fixing the Union's own position for that separate adoption.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

1. (target date: Memorandum of Cooperation entry into force) FACT: "The Memorandum of Cooperation between the European Union and the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) providing a framework for enhanced cooperation" entered into force on 29 March 2012. *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2016/1764, EUR-Lex CELEX 32016D1764. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D1764 -- carried from the export's forward-events record (first entry).
2. (same target date) Same underlying Memorandum of Cooperation entry-into-force fact, cited above (the export's second forward-event row restates it with a fuller quotation window).

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the EU-ICAO Joint Committee has since adopted the ATM annex referenced by this Decision was not checked in this authoring pass (see Section 4).

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a direct obligation on freight or aviation operators?** *Analytical inference:* no -- it fixes the EU's own negotiating position within an international joint committee; it does not itself enact or implement the ATM annex.

**Q2: Has the EU-ICAO Joint Committee since adopted the annex this Decision addresses?** *Legal Confirmation Required:* not checked in this authoring pass; see Section 4.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a two-Article EU position-fixing Decision governing only the Union's own conduct within an international joint committee -- it creates no shipper-, carrier-, or operator-facing obligation. "Substantive requirements" here means the Decision's own two operative Articles, both surveyed below.*

**1. Article 1 -- the Union's own negotiating position.** FACT: "The position to be taken by the Union within the EU-ICAO Joint Committee, as referred to in Article 7.3(c) of the Memorandum of Cooperation between the European Union and the International Civil Aviation Organization providing a framework for enhanced cooperation (the Memorandum of Cooperation), with regard to the adoption of an annex on Air Traffic Management to the Memorandum of Cooperation, shall be based on the draft Decision of the EU-ICAO Joint Committee, attached to this Decision." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2016/1764, EUR-Lex CELEX 32016D1764. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D1764

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this obligation runs from the Council to the Union's own representatives within the EU-ICAO Joint Committee; it creates no duty running to a private freight forwarder, carrier, or air navigation service provider.

**2. Article 2 -- entry into force.** FACT: "This Decision shall enter into force on the day of its adoption." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2016/1764, EUR-Lex CELEX 32016D1764. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D1764

No source in this 280,380-character captured document states a penalty, fine, or sanctions provision (a full-text search of the captured page for "enalt", "anction", and "nfringement" returned zero matches for all three terms); as a position-fixing Decision governing only the EU's own conduct within an international joint committee, it has no operator-facing compliance regime and no basis for a penalty provision.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2.

No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2.

No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2.

Obligations surveyed: 2; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 0.

Shortfall: both of this Decision's two operative Articles govern only the EU's own internal conduct within the EU-ICAO Joint Committee (Article 1: the Union's negotiating position; Article 2: entry into force) -- neither creates or affects a duty reaching a private freight forwarder, carrier, or air navigation operator, so zero of the two surveyed obligations are workspace-adjacent and zero FACT claims declare this section, despite the 280,380-character captured page (which is dominated by EUR-Lex site chrome, not additional instrument text -- the operative text is two Articles and three recitals in total).

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of the export date -- this Decision addresses no product category.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No content for this section as of the export date -- this Decision creates no registration or reporting obligation on any private party.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No content for this section as of the export date -- this Decision creates no operational system requirement on any private party.*

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section as of the export date -- this Decision imposes no obligation from which an exemption would be needed.*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section as of the export date -- the captured page carries no adjacent research or alternative-instrument content beyond this Decision's own two Articles and three recitals.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 29 March 2012: the Memorandum of Cooperation between the European Union and the International Civil Aviation Organization entered into force.
- 29 September 2016: Council Decision (EU) 2016/1764 adopted and entered into force on the same day.

*Source for timeline entries: Council Decision (EU) 2016/1764, EUR-Lex CELEX 32016D1764, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32016D1764.*

# 15. Sources

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks UN Sustainable Development Goals 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure) and 13 (Climate Action) as a voluntary, non-binding intergovernmental framework, not a regulation. It exists to give a workspace with air (primary), road (secondary), and ocean (tertiary) freight operations a single place to see how the SDGs anchor the downstream binding instruments (CORSIA, ReFuelEU Aviation, IMO CII, EU ETS, EU CO2 heavy-duty vehicle standards, CSRD) that do reach carriers and, indirectly, the workspace.

*Analytical inference:* the SDGs themselves create no legal obligation on private-sector freight operators; every binding compliance obligation referenced in this brief derives from a separate implementing regulation, never from the SDG text itself.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "of the  2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development , with  17 SDGs  at its core, at the  UN Sustainable Development Summit  in September 2015." *Source: UN DESA -- The 17 Goals. https://sdgs.un.org/goals

FACT: "9 Goal 9 Build resilient infrastructure, promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization and foster innovation. 8 Targets" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 9. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal9

FACT: "13 Goal 13 Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts. 5 Targets" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 13. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal13

FACT: "the transport sector will be playing a particularly important role in the achievement of the Paris Agreement, given the fact close to a quarter of energy-related global greenhouse gas emissions come from transport and that these emissions are projected to grow substantially in the years to come." *Source: UN DESA -- Sustainable Transport Topic Page. https://sdgs.un.org/topics/sustainable-transport

The SDGs are not directly enforceable against private companies. *Operational implication:* the workspace is not a regulated party under the SDGs as a framework instrument; it is exposed only indirectly, through carrier-level implementing regulations and client Scope 3 reporting requests.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No mandatory compliance deadline attaches to the SDG framework itself; the item below is a positioning action, not a compliance action.*

**COST ALERT** -- FACT: "Sustainable transport saw the largest rise (96 per cent), followed by clean energy (53 per cent) and buildings and infrastructure (41 per cent)." *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 13. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal13

*Operational implication:* this capital reallocation is accelerating commercial availability of SAF, green maritime fuels, and zero-emission road vehicles while creating fuel-cost surcharge pressure as carriers service debt on low-emission fleet investments; the workspace should review carrier contract terms now for green-fuel surcharge pass-through clauses.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The SDGs impose no compliance chain on private operators directly; the compliance chain is activated through the implementing instruments the SDGs anchor. For air mode, the workspace sits downstream of airline carriers regulated under CORSIA and EU ETS aviation. For road mode, the workspace sits downstream of road fleet operators regulated under EU CO2 heavy-duty vehicle standards. For ocean mode, the workspace sits downstream of vessel operators regulated under IMO CII ratings and EU ETS maritime.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace, acting as a non-vessel/non-aircraft operator intermediary, has direct obligations under any current aviation or maritime emissions instrument, or whether its exposure is purely through carrier cost pass-through, requires counsel review per the specific instrument and jurisdiction.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "9.1.2 Passenger and freight volumes, by mode of transport" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 9. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal9

FACT: "From 2015 to 2023, global maritime freight volumes in terms of goods loaded grew from 10.3 to 11.6 billion tons, with developing countries’ share increasing from 49 to 54 per cent." *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 9. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal9

FACT: "By 2030, upgrade infrastructure and retrofit industries to make them sustainable, with increased resource-use efficiency and greater adoption of clean and environmentally sound technologies and industrial processes, with all countries taking action in accordance with their respective capabilities" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 9. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal9

FACT: "In 2024, global CO2 emissions from fuel combustion and industrial processes reached a record 37.6 gigatons, a 0.8 per cent increase from 2023." *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 9. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal9

FACT: "The number of people affected by disasters surged by more than two thirds, from 1,158 per 100,000 population in the period 2005–2014 to 2,028 in the period 2014–2023" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 13. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal13

FACT: "13.2.2 Total greenhouse gas emissions per year" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 13. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal13

FACT: "Target 13.a Implement the commitment undertaken by developed-country parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change to a goal of mobilizing jointly $100 billion annually by 2020 from all sources to address the needs of developing countries in the context of meaningful mitigation actions and transparency on implementation and fully operationalize the Green Climate Fund through its capitalization as soon as possible" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 13. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal13

FACT: "global climate finance flows reached an annual average of $1.3 trillion in the biennium 2021–2022, a 63 per cent increase from 2019 to 2020, driven by higher investment in key mitigation sectors. Sustainable transport saw the largest rise (96 per cent)" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 13. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal13

FACT: "R oad transport consistently accounts for the vast majority of GHG emissions in the UNECE region" *Source: UNECE -- Climate and Transport Data Story. https://w3.unece.org/Stories/2025/01/tr_sdg_v3/story4.html

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The exported forward-events record for this item carries six rows; the two distinct dated triggers they describe are surfaced below (several rows restate the same underlying fact from different quoted windows).

1. (2020, from Target 13.a) FACT: "Target 13.a Implement the commitment undertaken by developed-country parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change to a goal of mobilizing jointly $100 billion annually by 2020 from all sources to address the needs of developing countries in the context of meaningful mitigation actions and transparency on implementation and fully operationalize the Green Climate Fund through its capitalization as soon as possible" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 13. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal13
2. (2030, from Target 9.4) FACT: "By 2030, upgrade infrastructure and retrofit industries to make them sustainable, with increased resource-use efficiency and greater adoption of clean and environmentally sound technologies and industrial processes, with all countries taking action in accordance with their respective capabilities" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 9. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal9

FACT: "The United Nations Decade of Sustainable Transport was declared by the United Nations General Assembly in 2023 (resolution A/RES/78/148) to start in 2026." *Source: UN DESA -- Sustainable Transport Topic Page. https://sdgs.un.org/topics/sustainable-transport

FACT: "The United Nations Decade of Sustainable Transport 2026 – 2035 was launched at the UN Headquarters on 10 December." *Source: UN DESA -- Sustainable Transport Topic Page. https://sdgs.un.org/topics/sustainable-transport

FACT: "On 10 December 2025, United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (DESA) organized the launch of the UN Decade of Sustainable Transport 2026 – 2035 and its associated Implementation Plan as a special event in the Trusteeship Council Chamber at the UN Headquarters." *Source: UN DESA -- Sustainable Transport Topic Page. https://sdgs.un.org/topics/sustainable-transport

FACT: "2026 May Thu 07 Open Stage Café event at the International Transport Forum Summit 2026" in Leipzig, Germany, linked to the UN Decade of Sustainable Transport. *Source: UN DESA -- Sustainable Transport Topic Page. https://sdgs.un.org/topics/sustainable-transport

FACT: "2026 Jul Tue 07 UN Decade of Sustainable Transport" -- Annual Stocktake. *Source: UN DESA -- Sustainable Transport Topic Page. https://sdgs.un.org/topics/sustainable-transport

*Analytical inference:* the Decade's Implementation Plan sets the policy agenda for SDG 9/13-linked transport regulations through 2035; workspaces should monitor its freight-specific workstreams. Re-check window: the Annual Stocktake event referenced above.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Are the SDGs legally binding on private-sector freight operators?** Decided: no. FACT: "of the  2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development , with  17 SDGs  at its core, at the  UN Sustainable Development Summit  in September 2015." is a Member State commitment, not a regulation imposing obligations on private operators. *Source: UN DESA -- The 17 Goals. https://sdgs.un.org/goals

**Q2: Does SDG 9.4 directly mandate CO2 reduction from freight operators?** Decided: no. The Target 9.4 text quoted in Section 5 sets a target for Member States; the mechanism of private-sector obligation flows through national implementing legislation, not the SDG text itself.

**Q3: Does SDG 13.2's GHG indicator apply to the workspace's emissions?** Decided as a framework matter: no. FACT: "13.2.2 Total greenhouse gas emissions per year" is a national-level indicator; the obligation arises through implementing instruments (CSRD, ISSB, GHG Protocol) that use it as their policy anchor. *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 13. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal13

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace's specific downstream obligations under CSRD Scope 3 reporting, CORSIA cost pass-through, or EU ETS aviation surcharges constitute SDG-aligned compliance commitments that can be represented to clients as such in commercial proposals requires counsel review.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: the SDGs impose no substantive requirements directly on private operators. "Substantive requirements" here means the SDG target statements themselves (the Member-State-level commitments the source pool states), surveyed because each anchors a downstream implementing instrument that DOES reach carriers and, indirectly, the workspace.*

**1. SDG 9.4 -- infrastructure/industry sustainability target.** FACT: "By 2030, upgrade infrastructure and retrofit industries to make them sustainable, with increased resource-use efficiency and greater adoption of clean and environmentally sound technologies and industrial processes, with all countries taking action in accordance with their respective capabilities" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 9. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal9

*Analytical inference:* this target is the upstream policy rationale for CO2 intensity instruments in aviation (CORSIA, ReFuelEU Aviation SAF mandates) and maritime (IMO CII, EU ETS maritime) -- all of which affect the workspace's carrier base as cost pass-throughs.

**2. SDG 13.2 -- national GHG emissions indicator.** FACT: "13.2.2 Total greenhouse gas emissions per year" FACT: "R oad transport consistently accounts for the vast majority of GHG emissions in the UNECE region" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 13, https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal13; UNECE -- Climate and Transport Data Story, https://w3.unece.org/Stories/2025/01/tr_sdg_v3/story4.html

*Analytical inference:* this target is the upstream rationale for Scope 3 reporting obligations under CSRD, the GHG Protocol, and ISO 14083 freight emissions accounting.

**3. SDG 13.a -- $100 billion climate finance mobilization target.** FACT: "Target 13.a Implement the commitment undertaken by developed-country parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change to a goal of mobilizing jointly $100 billion annually by 2020 from all sources to address the needs of developing countries in the context of meaningful mitigation actions and transparency on implementation and fully operationalize the Green Climate Fund through its capitalization as soon as possible" FACT: "global climate finance flows reached an annual average of $1.3 trillion in the biennium 2021–2022, a 63 per cent increase from 2019 to 2020, driven by higher investment in key mitigation sectors. Sustainable transport saw the largest rise (96 per cent)" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 13. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal13

*Operational implication:* the source material does not establish that the $100 billion target caused sustainable transport's 96 per cent climate-finance rise; no causal link is asserted here. The capital growth itself is reshaping supplier access to SAF and green-vessel financing, which affects the workspace's carrier base.

**4. SDG 9.1 -- infrastructure and freight-volume target.** FACT: "9.1.2 Passenger and freight volumes, by mode of transport" FACT: "From 2015 to 2023, global maritime freight volumes in terms of goods loaded grew from 10.3 to 11.6 billion tons, with developing countries’ share increasing from 49 to 54 per cent." *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 9. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal9

*Operational implication:* growing developing-country share of maritime volumes raises port congestion risk on emerging-market routes; FACT: "small island developing States and landlocked developing countries remained marginalized owing to infrastructure and cost barriers." *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 9. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal9 -- a persistent routing constraint for humanitarian cargo to these regions.

No source in this pool states a penalty, fine, or sanctions provision applicable to a private freight operator; the SDGs are a voluntary, non-binding intergovernmental framework, and penalties arise exclusively under separate implementing instruments not captured in this brief.

No exceptions are stated in Sections covering SDG Targets 9.1, 9.4, 13.1, 13.2, and 13.a.

No scope limits are stated in Sections covering SDG Targets 9.1, 9.4, 13.1, 13.2, and 13.a.

Obligations surveyed: 4; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 4.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of the export date -- the SDG framework addresses no product category directly.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The SDGs generate no direct registration or reporting obligation on private-sector freight operators; reporting obligations arise from implementing instruments.

*Analytical inference:* the workspace's most proximate reporting exposure under SDG 13.2 is as a Scope 3 emission source in its clients' corporate sustainability reports, where clients are subject to CSRD or equivalent disclosure requirements.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any specific client contract clause or tender requirement creates a legally enforceable data-provision obligation on the workspace for Scope 3 freight emissions reporting under CSRD-linked supplier questionnaires requires counsel review of those specific contracts.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

**Emissions data infrastructure.** *Analytical inference:* a freight emissions calculation methodology aligned with ISO 14083 or GHG Protocol Category 4, capable of producing tonne-kilometre CO2-equivalent data by shipment, is the foundational system a workspace needs to respond credibly to client Scope 3 data requests.

**Climate-risk routing.** FACT: "The number of people affected by disasters surged by more than two thirds, from 1,158 per 100,000 population in the period 2005–2014 to 2,028 in the period 2014–2023" *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 13. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal13

*Operational implication:* this trend is relevant to route-reliability planning for humanitarian cargo and time-critical live-events, film & TV, and fine-art shipments on routes traversing high-disaster-exposure regions.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The SDGs carry no exemptions applicable to private operators, as they impose no direct obligations on private operators.

*Analytical inference:* humanitarian cargo operations may be required on routes or timelines that preclude low-emission mode selection, creating operational tension between SDG 13.1 (resilience) and SDG 13.2 (mitigation) that no authoritative guidance in this source pool resolves.

FACT: "small island developing States and landlocked developing countries remained marginalized owing to infrastructure and cost barriers." *Source: UN DESA -- Goal 9. https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal9

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "Despite a continuous increase in goods transport performance over time, the energy consumption per unit of goods transported (measured in tonne-kilometres) is decreasing. This trend indicates that the energy efficiency in the transport of goods is improving." *Source: UNECE -- Climate and Transport Data Story. https://w3.unece.org/Stories/2025/01/tr_sdg_v3/story4.html

*Analytical inference:* this trend supports the case that modal efficiency gains (load factor, route optimisation) are delivering real SDG 9.4 progress independent of fuel-switching; for the workspace, consolidation decisions are a verifiable SDG contribution narrative.

*Industry interpretation:* SLOCAT identifies transport's indirect contribution to SDG 13 via "climate change adaptation (Target 13.1)" and "climate change mitigation (Target 13.2)". *Source: SLOCAT -- Transport Targets of the SDGs (tier 4). https://slocat.net/transport-targets-sustainable-development-goals/

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- September 2015: 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development adopted; SDGs 9 and 13 established.
- 2024: EU ETS maritime coverage begins for large vessels.
- 2025: ReFuelEU Aviation SAF blend mandate begins.
- 2025: 2025 SDG Progress Report published.
- 10 December 2025: UN Decade of Sustainable Transport (2026-2035) launched; Implementation Plan released.
- 2026: UN Decade of Sustainable Transport formally begins.
- May 2026: ITF Summit Leipzig; Open Stage event on UN Decade.
- July 2026: UN Decade of Sustainable Transport Annual Stocktake event.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, which amends the existing MRV Maritime Regulation (EU) 2015/757 to bring offshore ships (400 gross tonnage and above) and smaller general cargo ships (400-4,999 GT) into scope, and to add a zero-rating rule for sustainable fuels. It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace that operates, charters, or manages offshore-service or smaller general-cargo tonnage calling at EEA ports a single place to see what monitoring, reporting, and (from 2027) EU ETS obligations now apply, and by when.

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 16 October 2024." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

FACT: The Regulation carries the official citation "L series 2024/3214 27.12.2024" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union" -- since the Regulation was published 27 December 2024, this entry-into-force clause computes to the third day after publication. *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This is a binding EU delegated regulation, not guidance: it amends Annex I and Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2015/757 directly and applies to "companies" (the ISM-defined operator or manager) responsible for in-scope ships, not only to Member States. It applies to the workspace directly whenever the workspace is, or acts for, the ISM company responsible for an offshore ship or a 400-4,999 GT general cargo ship calling at an EEA port.

FACT: "from 1 January 2025, general cargo ships between 400 and 5000 gross tonnage, and offshore ships of 400 gross tonnage and above, fell under the scope of the amended MRV Regulation." *Source: EMSA - MRV Regulation changes page, European Maritime Safety Agency. https://www.emsa.europa.eu/reducing-emissions/mrv-changes.html

*Operational implication:* A workspace should map every vessel it manages or charters against these two new populations (offshore ships >=400 GT; general cargo ships 400-4,999 GT) rather than assuming the pre-2025 >5,000 GT threshold still defines the full in-scope fleet.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**1. Vessel-type assessment.** Assess the type designations of all offshore vessels under the workspace's operational responsibility against the enacted 35-type list.

FACT: "the following ships, other than icebreakers, designed or certified to perform service activities offshore or at offshore installations: (a) anchor handling tug supply vessel; (b) offshore supply ship; (c) crew/supply vessel; (d) pipe carrier; (e) platform supply ship; (f) drilling ship; (g) floating production storage and offloading (FPSO), oil; (h) gas processing vessel; (i) floating storage and offloading (FSO), gas; (j) FSO, oil; (k) accommodation ship; (l) diving support vessel; (m) offshore construction vessel; (n) offshore support vessel; (o) pipe burying vessel; (p) pipe layer; (q) pipe layer crane vessel; (r) production testing vessel; (s) standby safety vessel; (t) trenching support vessel; (u) well stimulation vessel; (v) cable layer; (w) cable repair ship; (x) mining vessel; (y) wind turbine installation vessel; (z) commissioning service operation vessel; (aa) service operation vessel; (ab) work/repair vessel; (ac) research survey vessel; (ad) dredger; (ae) hopper dredger." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether a specific vessel under the workspace's operational or commercial responsibility meets this classification, and whether the workspace entity is the "company" responsible for MRV purposes, requires counsel and classification-society review.

**2. Verified monitoring plan.** Engage an accredited MRV verifier to assess the monitoring plan for each offshore ship making its first EEA port call from 1 January 2025.

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union"; and *Operational implication:* the plan itself, per industry guidance, must already be verifier-assessed before submission to the administering authority. *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

**3. Fuel zero-rating methodology check.** Verify that the workspace's MRV emissions reporting applies the correct CO2 emission-factor derogation for any RFNBO, RCF, or synthetic low-carbon fuel consumed.

FACT: "However, Article 1, point (2), shall apply from 1 January 2024." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

*Operational implication:* because this rule applies retroactively to 1 January 2024, a workspace whose managed vessels consumed any of these fuel types in 2024 should confirm its 2024 reporting used the correct methodology, not the Annex I default factors.

**4. ETS threshold mapping.** Map the gross tonnage of all managed offshore vessels against the 5,000 GT ETS inclusion threshold now, and begin ETS surrender-account planning ahead of 1 January 2027.

FACT: "From 1 January 2027, offshore ships of 5 000 gross tonnage and above are included in the scope of maritime transport activities covered by Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

Unlike a state planning framework, this Regulation's monitoring and reporting duties run directly to the "company" (the ISM-defined operator/manager) responsible for an in-scope ship, not only to a Member State -- so a workspace that is, or acts for, that company carries the obligations in Section 8 directly, not merely as a downstream effect of a government's own duty.

FACT: For the fleet already inside the EU ETS (above 5,000 GT, in scope since 2024), "shipping companies only have to surrender allowances for a portion of their emissions during an initial phase-in period: 2025: for 40% of their emissions reported in 2024; 2026: for 70% of their emissions reported in 2025; 2027 onwards: for 100% of their reported emissions." This is the general ETS maritime phase-in; offshore ships are NOT part of it. *Source: European Commission - Climate Action: Reducing emissions from the shipping sector, DG CLIMA. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-shipping-sector_en

*Industry interpretation (ABS):* "Beginning 1 January 2027, the EU ETS Directive will be expanded to cover offshore vessels exceeding 5,000 GT, which will be required to surrender allowances at company level by 30 September 2028." *Source: ABS Regulatory News No. 02/2025, American Bureau of Shipping. https://ww2.eagle.org/content/dam/eagle/regulatory-news/2025/Application-of-EU-MRV-and-EU-ETS-to-Offshore-Ships.pdf

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any transitional relief is later granted to offshore ships entering ETS scope in 2027 requires confirmation against Commission guidance current at that time.

GAP: Specific penalty provision not available from primary sources as of the export date. The Regulation (EU) 2024/3214 text itself does not recite a penalty provision; enforcement of MRV Maritime obligations is carried out by Member States.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

The corpus for this item mixes binding law (the Regulation itself, Tier 1) with EU-agency and Commission material (EMSA, DG CLIMA, the COM(2025) 109 review report, Tier 2) and classification-society interpretive guidance (DNV, ABS, Tier 4). The Tier 4 material is cited throughout this brief as *Industry interpretation*, never as an independent legal source, because it restates and operationalizes the Tier 1/2 material rather than creating new obligations.

FACT: "Guidance Document No. 1, Updated Version, 18 November 2025." This is background on the wider EU ETS/MRV Maritime guidance corpus, not a document specific to Regulation (EU) 2024/3214 itself; cited here to confirm which guidance-document version is currently operative. *Source: European Commission - Climate Action: Reducing emissions from the shipping sector, DG CLIMA. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-shipping-sector_en

FACT: For context on the parallel company-level ETS reporting track (ships already inside ETS scope, not offshore ships before 2027): "In addition, from 2025, by 31 March of each year, for ships falling within the scope of the ETS Directive , shipping companies must also submit an emissions report at company level (aggregating the data to be reported for ETS purposes at company level)" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

*Analytical inference:* the Tier 2 Commission and EU-agency material controls interpretation of the Regulation's obligations; the Tier 4 classification-society guidance (DNV, ABS) is cited throughout this brief only where it operationalizes those obligations into vessel-level dates and steps, never as a source of new obligations in its own right.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

**1. Commission feasibility report on 400-4,999 GT offshore ships in EU ETS**, due no later than 31 December 2026. FACT: "According to Article 3gg(5) of that Directive, no later than 31 December 2026, the Commission should present a report to the European Parliament and to the Council in which it should examine the feasibility and economic, environmental and social impacts of the inclusion in that Directive of emissions from ships, including offshore ships, below 5 000 gross tonnage but not below 400 gross tonnage." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

**2. Targeted EU ETS revision proposal.** FACT: "On 17 July 2026, the European Commission proposed a targeted revision of the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) to strengthen Europe's industrial competitiveness and support the delivery of the EU's" *Source: European Commission - Climate Action: Reducing emissions from the shipping sector, DG CLIMA. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-shipping-sector_en

*Operational implication:* a workspace with a fleet concentrated below 5,000 GT should treat both the 2026 feasibility report and the 17 July 2026 targeted ETS revision proposal as material inputs to its 2027+ ETS-exposure planning; neither is finalized law as of this brief.

# 7. Threshold Questions

## 1. Which vessel types are "offshore ships" under the amended regulation?

**Status: Decided by the regulation, with a qualification.**

FACT: "the following ships, other than icebreakers, designed or certified to perform service activities offshore or at offshore installations: (a) anchor handling tug supply vessel; (b) offshore supply ship; (c) crew/supply vessel; (d) pipe carrier; (e) platform supply ship; (f) drilling ship; (g) floating production storage and offloading (FPSO), oil; (h) gas processing vessel; (i) floating storage and offloading (FSO), gas; (j) FSO, oil; (k) accommodation ship; (l) diving support vessel; (m) offshore construction vessel; (n) offshore support vessel; (o) pipe burying vessel; (p) pipe layer; (q) pipe layer crane vessel; (r) production testing vessel; (s) standby safety vessel; (t) trenching support vessel; (u) well stimulation vessel; (v) cable layer; (w) cable repair ship; (x) mining vessel; (y) wind turbine installation vessel; (z) commissioning service operation vessel; (aa) service operation vessel; (ab) work/repair vessel; (ac) research survey vessel; (ad) dredger; (ae) hopper dredger." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

*Legal Confirmation Required:* for any vessel type not explicitly named in the list, whether it qualifies turns on statutory certifications and class notations -- a factual and technical determination for each vessel.

## 2. What is the gross-tonnage threshold for MRV obligations?

**Status: Decided -- 400 GT and above.**

FACT: "from 1 January 2025, general cargo ships between 400 and 5000 gross tonnage, and offshore ships of 400 gross tonnage and above, fell under the scope of the amended MRV Regulation." *Source: EMSA - MRV Regulation changes page, European Maritime Safety Agency. https://www.emsa.europa.eu/reducing-emissions/mrv-changes.html

## 3. What is the ETS applicability threshold and timeline for offshore ships?

**Status: Decided for >=5,000 GT; under review for 400-4,999 GT.**

FACT: "From 1 January 2027, offshore ships of 5 000 gross tonnage and above are included in the scope of maritime transport activities covered by Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC" The Commission review for 400-4,999 GT is due by 31 December 2026 (Section 6). *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

## 4. Which CO2 emission-factor methodology applies when using RFNBO, RCF, or synthetic low-carbon fuel?

**Status: Decided -- Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066 as amended applies in place of the Annex I Part A default factors.**

FACT: "The rules in Annex II to Regulation (EU) 2015/757 should be updated to further align them with the rules applicable to other Emissions Trading System (ETS) sectors with regards to fuels eligible for zero-rating under Directive 2003/87/EC, in particular to include the possibility for zero-rating synthetic low-carbon fuels." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

## 5. Penalty/enforcement provision.

GAP: Specific penalty provision not available from primary sources as of the export date. The Regulation (EU) 2024/3214 text itself does not recite a penalty provision; enforcement of MRV Maritime obligations is carried out by Member States.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

## A. GHG Emissions Coverage for Offshore Ships (new Part AA of Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2015/757)

FACT: "Greenhouse gas emissions from offshore ships shall cover greenhouse gas emissions released during voyages from last port of call to a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State to next port of call, as well as within ports of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State by the following ships, other than icebreakers, designed or certified to perform service activities offshore or at offshore installations" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

**Qualification -- icebreaker carve-out:** "the following ships, other than icebreakers, designed or certified to perform service activities offshore or at offshore installations" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

**Qualification -- design/certification condition:** "the following ships, other than icebreakers, designed or certified to perform service activities offshore or at offshore installations" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

## B. Document of Compliance Deadline

FACT: "by 30 June of each year, companies must ensure that all their ships that have performed activities in the previous reporting period and are visiting ports in the European Economic Area carry on board a document of compli" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

*Industry interpretation (ABS):* "By 30 June 2026 and each year, carry onboard a valid Document of Compliance (DoC)." *Source: ABS Regulatory News No. 02/2025, American Bureau of Shipping. https://ww2.eagle.org/content/dam/eagle/regulatory-news/2025/Application-of-EU-MRV-and-EU-ETS-to-Offshore-Ships.pdf

## C. Zero-Rating of Sustainable Fuels (amended Part C, point 1.2, Annex II)

FACT: "The rules in Annex II to Regulation (EU) 2015/757 should be updated to further align them with the rules applicable to other Emissions Trading System (ETS) sectors with regards to fuels eligible for zero-rating under Directive 2003/87/EC, in particular to include the possibility for zero-rating synthetic low-carbon fuels." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

**Qualification -- retroactive application:** FACT: "However, Article 1, point (2), shall apply from 1 January 2024." *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific fuel used by a managed vessel qualifies as RFNBO, RCF, or synthetic low-carbon fuel under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2066 requires fuel documentation review and potentially counsel.

## D. Emissions Report and Company-Level ETS Report Deadlines

FACT: "From 2025, by 31 March of each year, companies must, for each ship under their responsibility , submit an emissions report for the entire reporting period of the previous year, which has been verified as satisfactory by a verifier in accordance with Article 13" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

FACT: "In addition, from 2025, by 31 March of each year, for ships falling within the scope of the ETS Directive , shipping companies must also submit an emissions report at company level (aggregating the data to be reported for ETS purposes at company level)" -- this company-level report does not apply to offshore ships before their 2027 ETS entry (Section 10). *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

*Industry interpretation (ABS):* "By 31 March 2026 and each year, submit to the responsible administering authority, to the ship’s flag State (for ships flying the flag of a Member State) and to the EU Commission a verified emissions report for the entire reporting period of the previous year." *Source: ABS Regulatory News No. 02/2025, American Bureau of Shipping. https://ww2.eagle.org/content/dam/eagle/regulatory-news/2025/Application-of-EU-MRV-and-EU-ETS-to-Offshore-Ships.pdf

*Industry interpretation (ABS):* "By 31 March 2028 and each year, companies shall submit to the administering authority for offshore ships of 5000 GT and above an aggregated report at company level for the emissions of the previous calendar year." *Source: ABS Regulatory News No. 02/2025, American Bureau of Shipping. https://ww2.eagle.org/content/dam/eagle/regulatory-news/2025/Application-of-EU-MRV-and-EU-ETS-to-Offshore-Ships.pdf

## E. ETS Allowance Surrender

FACT: "Once verified, companies must surrender (use) the equivalent number of allowances by 30 September of that year." *Source: EMSA - MRV Regulation changes page, European Maritime Safety Agency (FAQ). https://www.emsa.europa.eu/reducing-emissions/mrv-changes.html

*Industry interpretation (ABS):* "Beginning 1 January 2027, the EU ETS Directive will be expanded to cover offshore vessels exceeding 5,000 GT, which will be required to surrender allowances at company level by 30 September 2028." *Source: ABS Regulatory News No. 02/2025, American Bureau of Shipping. https://ww2.eagle.org/content/dam/eagle/regulatory-news/2025/Application-of-EU-MRV-and-EU-ETS-to-Offshore-Ships.pdf

*Operational implication:* for offshore ships this first becomes relevant for 2027 emissions, with surrender falling in the 2028 cycle (Section 14).

## F. Cross-Reference -- General MRV Exempted Ship Categories

FACT: "MRV exempted categories are defined in Article 2(2) of the MRV maritime Regulation; those are ‘warships, naval auxiliaries, fish-catching or fish-processing ships, wooden ships of a primitive build, ships not propelled by mechanical means, or government ships used for non-commercial purposes’." *Source: European Commission - Report COM(2025) 109 final, European Commission, 18 March 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025DC0109

*Analytical inference:* these exemptions run to the underlying MRV maritime Regulation (EU) 2015/757 as a whole; an offshore ship falling into one of these named categories is exempt from the MRV obligations described above.

## G. Confirmed Scope Boundary

FACT: "from 1 January 2025, general cargo ships between 400 and 5000 gross tonnage, and offshore ships of 400 gross tonnage and above, fell under the scope of the amended MRV Regulation." *Source: EMSA - MRV Regulation changes page, European Maritime Safety Agency. https://www.emsa.europa.eu/reducing-emissions/mrv-changes.html

## H. Per-Voyage Reporting Derogation (underlying MRV maritime Regulation, Article 9(2))

FACT: the underlying MRV maritime Regulation provides that a company "shall be exempt from the obligation to monitor the information" on a per-voyage basis for a ship meeting stated round-trip and short-voyage conditions. *Source: European Commission - Report COM(2025) 109 final, European Commission, 18 March 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025DC0109

Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (Part H, the Article 9(2) per-voyage reporting derogation, and Part A's icebreaker carve-out). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (Part G, the 400 GT / 400-5,000 GT scope boundary).
