# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

## THETIS-MRV Platform Registration

*Industry interpretation (DNV):* companies should "set up a Thetis-MRV account and request attribution to an administering authority." *Source: DNV - The EU defines offshore ships for EU MRV reporting, DNV, 8 November 2024. https://www.dnv.com/news/2024/the-eu-defines-offshore-ships-for-eu-mrv-reporting/

FACT: "Only 29% of the ISM companies 19 and 3% of the shipowners managing smaller vessels are already registered on THETIS-MRV. This suggests that the majority of companies managing smaller vessels would need to set up and familiarise themselves with MRV processes as they are not already reporting under MRV." *Source: European Commission - Report COM(2025) 109 final, European Commission, 18 March 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025DC0109

*Operational implication:* THETIS-MRV onboarding is a prerequisite before monitoring-plan submission and should be completed immediately if not already done.

## Monitoring Plan Submission Timeline

*Industry interpretation (ABS):* "From 1 January 2025, the shipping company must submit the monitoring plan of the offshore ship to its administering authority within three months after the ship's first port of call in a port under the jurisdiction of a Member State." *Source: ABS Regulatory News No. 02/2025, American Bureau of Shipping. https://ww2.eagle.org/content/dam/eagle/regulatory-news/2025/Application-of-EU-MRV-and-EU-ETS-to-Offshore-Ships.pdf

## Annual Emissions Report -- Offshore Ships

FACT: "From 2025, by 31 March of each year, companies must, for each ship under their responsibility , submit an emissions report for the entire reporting period of the previous year, which has been verified as satisfactory by a verifier in accordance with Article 13" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

**Qualification -- CER not required until 2028:** the company-level ETS report described in Section 8, Part D does not apply to offshore ships before their 2027 ETS entry.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

## 1. Per-Voyage Monitoring Infrastructure

**Scope:** all offshore vessels under the workspace's MRV responsibility calling at EEA ports. **Deadline:** monitoring from 1 January 2025; first verified report due 31 March 2026.

FACT: "the majority of companies managing smaller vessels would need to set up and familiarise themselves with MRV processes as they are not already reporting under MRV." *Source: European Commission - Report COM(2025) 109 final, European Commission, 18 March 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025DC0109

FACT: "recurrent annual MRV-related administrative costs per vessel for smaller vessels (estimated at EUR 3 690 per vessel on average)" *Source: European Commission - Report COM(2025) 109 final, European Commission, 18 March 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025DC0109

## 2. Verified Monitoring Plan

**Scope:** each offshore ship individually. **Deadline:** within three months of first EEA port call from 1 January 2025.

*Operational implication:* the monitoring plan must be verifier-assessed before submission -- a prerequisite step, not a concurrent one.

## 3. THETIS-MRV Account and Administering-Authority Attribution

**Scope:** all companies newly entering MRV scope for offshore ships. **Deadline:** before monitoring-plan submission.

FACT: "Only 29% of the ISM companies 19 and 3% of the shipowners managing smaller vessels are already registered on THETIS-MRV. This suggests that the majority of companies managing smaller vessels would need to set up and familiarise themselves with MRV processes as they are not already reporting under MRV." *Source: European Commission - Report COM(2025) 109 final, European Commission, 18 March 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025DC0109

## 4. ETS Allowance Infrastructure (vessels >=5,000 GT) -- Planning Phase Now

**Scope:** offshore ships of 5,000 GT and above. **Deadline:** infrastructure required before 1 January 2027; first surrender falls in 2028.

FACT: "A company that is only responsible for offshore vessels (and not responsible for other ship types) does not need to open a Maritime Operator Holding Account, as the EU ETS does not apply to these ships before 2027." *Source: DNV - The EU defines offshore ships for EU MRV reporting, DNV, 8 November 2024. https://www.dnv.com/news/2024/the-eu-defines-offshore-ships-for-eu-mrv-reporting/

*Operational implication:* given offshore ships only enter ETS scope in 2027, Maritime Operator Holding Account planning should begin now rather than in 2026.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

## Icebreaker Exclusion

FACT: "the following ships, other than icebreakers, designed or certified to perform service activities offshore or at offshore installations" *Source: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214, European Commission, 16 October 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32024R3214

## General MRV Exempted Categories

FACT: "MRV exempted categories are defined in Article 2(2) of the MRV maritime Regulation; those are ‘warships, naval auxiliaries, fish-catching or fish-processing ships, wooden ships of a primitive build, ships not propelled by mechanical means, or government ships used for non-commercial purposes’." *Source: European Commission - Report COM(2025) 109 final, European Commission, 18 March 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025DC0109

## Offshore Ships Below 5,000 GT -- ETS Exemption (For Now)

FACT: "A company that is only responsible for offshore vessels (and not responsible for other ship types) does not need to open a Maritime Operator Holding Account, as the EU ETS does not apply to these ships before 2027." *Source: DNV - The EU defines offshore ships for EU MRV reporting, DNV, 8 November 2024. https://www.dnv.com/news/2024/the-eu-defines-offshore-ships-for-eu-mrv-reporting/

*Analytical inference:* this exemption from the ETS Maritime Operator Holding Account requirement applies only until 2027 for >=5,000 GT vessels; the 400-4,999 GT population remains under review for potential future ETS inclusion per the 2026 review deadline (Section 6).

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

## Commission MRV Review -- Feasibility of Extending to Vessels 400-4,999 GT (COM(2025) 109)

FACT: "The analysis shows that 8 525 vessels between 400 – 4999 GT called at EU ports in 2023" *Source: European Commission - Report COM(2025) 109 final, European Commission, 18 March 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025DC0109

FACT: "Offshore 921 7.5% 3.41 2.7%" *Source: European Commission - Report COM(2025) 109 final, European Commission, 18 March 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025DC0109

FACT: "using a threshold of 5000 GT instead of 400 GT would substantially reduce estimated administrative costs" *Source: European Commission - Report COM(2025) 109 final, European Commission, 18 March 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025DC0109

FACT: the report's own footnotes describe the pre-2025 baseline this way: "excluding smaller (400-4,999 GT) general cargo and offshore vessels to be incorporated from 2025." *Source: European Commission - Report COM(2025) 109 final, European Commission, 18 March 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025DC0109

*Analytical inference:* the economic case for extending ETS to small offshore vessels (400-4,999 GT) is a live, unresolved question the Commission has explicitly reserved for the 2026 review; workspaces with a fleet concentrated below 5,000 GT should treat it as a material planning horizon rather than a settled exemption.

## FuelEU Maritime Regulation -- Operational Intersection

FACT: "All monitored and recorded data under the MRV maritime Regulation can indeed be used for FuelEU calculations, subject to confirmation by FuelEU Verifier, if different from the MRV Verifier." *Source: European Commission - Report COM(2025) 109 final, European Commission, 18 March 2025. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52025DC0109

*Operational implication:* MRV data collected under Regulation (EU) 2015/757 (as amended) feeds directly into FuelEU Maritime compliance calculation; investment in MRV monitoring infrastructure serves a dual compliance purpose from 2025 onward.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 16 October 2024: Commission adopts Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214.
- 27 December 2024: Published in the Official Journal of the EU, L series 2024/3214.
- 1 January 2024: Zero-rating rules for RFNBO, RCF, and synthetic low-carbon fuels apply retroactively (Article 1, point 2).
- 1 January 2025: Offshore ships (400 GT and above) and general cargo ships (400-4,999 GT) included in MRV scope.
- Within three months of first EEA port call from 1 January 2025: monitoring plan (verifier-assessed) due to the administering authority.
- 31 March 2026: first verified emissions report for offshore ships (2025 reporting year) due to the administering authority, flag State, and Commission via THETIS-MRV.
- 30 June 2026: Document of Compliance due onboard for all ships under MRV scope.
- 31 December 2026: Commission report to Parliament and Council on the feasibility of including offshore ships 400-5,000 GT in EU ETS.
- 1 January 2027: offshore ships of 5,000 GT and above included in EU ETS scope.
- 17 July 2026: Commission proposes a targeted revision of the EU ETS (Section 6).
- 31 March 2028: first aggregated company-level emissions report (CER) for offshore ships >=5,000 GT due.
- 30 September 2028: first ETS allowance-surrender deadline for offshore ships >=5,000 GT (for 2027 emissions).

*Sources: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/3214; ABS Regulatory News No. 02/2025; EMSA MRV Regulation changes page; EC Report COM(2025) 109 final; EC DG CLIMA Climate Action page.*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 (FuelEU Maritime) as regards access rights and the functional and technical specifications of the FuelEU database. It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace a single place to see who the database's obligations run to (ship operators, verifiers, and Member State authorities, not forwarders) and how carrier-facing FuelEU compliance data flows through it.

FACT: "This Regulation lays down the rules for access rights and the functional and technical specifications, including notification rules and filtering, of the FuelEU database. It builds upon existing IT systems in the European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA), mainly THETIS-MRV." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

FACT: this implementing regulation coordinates with the earlier verification-activities instrument: "Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2027 of 26 July 2024 on verification activities pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 of the European Parliament and of the Council on the use of renewable and low-carbon fuels in maritime transport," *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This implementing regulation is the technical rulebook for the FuelEU database, the central IT system through which FuelEU Maritime compliance is reported, verified, and enforced. It does not create new emissions limits or fuel obligations; those sit in the parent regulation, (EU) 2023/1805.

FACT: The regulation is adopted under the parent FuelEU Maritime regulation: "Having regard to Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 September 2023 on the use of renewable and low-carbon fuels in maritime transport, and amending Directive 2009/16/EC ( 1 ) , and in particular Article 19(3) thereof" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

FACT: "The primary foundational structure upon which the FuelEU database is built is THETIS-MRV, which was created to support the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2015/757 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 2 ) , with the aim of capitalising on previously submitted data" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

FACT: [jurisdictional_scope] The regulation is directly applicable Union law: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

FACT: [effective_date] "This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union"; the Official Journal publication is dated 24.2.2026 (OJ L series 2026/394). *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

*Operational implication:* The workspace, as a freight forwarder buying ocean freight rather than operating ships, has no direct login, reporting duty, or data-entry obligation in the FuelEU database. Exposure is indirect: carriers' FuelEU compliance costs, penalty pass-throughs, and pooling strategies are administered through this system.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**Severity: MONITORING.** No immediate action is required of the workspace by this instrument. The regulation assigns database access and management duties to Member State authorities, shipping companies, verifiers, and the European Commission; freight forwarders and shippers are not among the enumerated user classes (Section 7).

*Operational implication:* The monitoring posture should watch two things: (a) carrier surcharge and pass-through behaviour as FuelEU penalties and compliance balances become visible to carriers through the database, and (b) any future amendment extending database access or disclosure to commercial counterparties, which would change the workspace's data-access position.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The regulation maps database rights onto the FuelEU Maritime compliance chain.

FACT: "Access rights and functionalities of the FuelEU database shall correspond to the respective responsibilities of the actors involved in the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

The enumerated user classes are: Member States in four configurations (administering State; flag State; competent authority of the Member State of the port of call; national accreditation body), companies, verifiers, and the European Commission.

FACT: A company holds "access to all information on the ships under its responsibility and previous records, including the FuelEU document of compliance, the FuelEU report and partial FuelEU report, the verification report, the compliance balance, the additional checks report, OPS exceptions". *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

*Operational implication:* The workspace sits outside this chain, downstream of the "company" actor (the shipowner or ISM company). Any FuelEU compliance evidence the workspace needs from carriers (for example a FuelEU document of compliance) must be requested commercially; the database itself will not provide it to a forwarder.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of the export date: no Commission guidance document interpreting this implementing regulation was identified in the source corpus.* EMSA maintains FuelEU Maritime webinar and tutorial material offering orientation on database workflows, cited here as Tier 4 institutional guidance material, not an interpretive legal source. *Source: EMSA FuelEU webinars page, European Maritime Safety Agency. https://www.emsa.europa.eu/reducing-emissions/webinars_and_tutorials/fueleu-webinars.html

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The regulation builds in a controlled evolution path for the database.

FACT: "Specifications for data exchange formats shall be made available no later than 1 month before implementation." Updates and corrections are to be notified to all users prior to implementation through release notes and detailed technical specifications. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

EMSA may update functionalities and the interface of the database considering experience gained, technological advancements, evolving user needs, and emerging best practices. A future connection to the Union Database under Directive (EU) 2018/2001 is anticipated (Section 13).

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the workspace have access to the FuelEU database?**

*Per the workspace's reading:* No. The user classes with access rights are exhaustively enumerated as Member State configurations, companies, verifiers, and the European Commission. A freight forwarder that is not the ISM company of a ship is not an enumerated user class.

**Q2: Does this regulation impose reporting obligations on the workspace?**

*Per the workspace's reading:* No. The reporting, verification, and penalty workflows administered through the database attach to companies, verifiers, and authorities under Regulation (EU) 2023/1805. *Legal Confirmation Required:* If any affiliated entity ever assumes the role of a "company" for a vessel within FuelEU Maritime scope (for example through ship management arrangements), its database obligations under this regulation and the parent regulation should be confirmed by counsel.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

## A. Access Model

FACT: "Access rights referred to in paragraph 1 shall be restricted to read-only. Management functionalities referred to in paragraph 1 shall include creating and modifying data." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

## B. On-Shore Power Supply (OPS) Records

FACT: "The FuelEU database shall enable the competent authority of the Member State of the port of call or any duly authorised entity to record exceptions provided for in Article 6(5) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805", together with records of non-compliance with OPS obligations, using an electronic form available in THETIS-MRV. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

## C. Compliance Balance Management

FACT: "The FuelEU database shall incorporate a compliance balance calculator to enable the company to monitor and manage its compliance balance and to use the flexibility mechanisms provided for in Articles 20 and 21 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 as necessary." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

The database supports banking of a compliance surplus to the following reporting period and borrowing of an advance compliance surplus from the following reporting period.

FACT: "The FuelEU database shall incorporate a pooling functionality that enables companies and verifiers to interact with one another in order to pool the compliance balance of different ships", including registration and verification of the pool composition and allocation. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

## D. Penalty Administration

FACT: [penalty_summary] "The FuelEU database shall enable the administering state to record and notify to the company the amount of FuelEU penalties applicable to its ships, pursuant to Article 23 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

*Operational implication:* Penalty amounts themselves are set by the parent regulation, not by this instrument; what this instrument does is make penalty issuance, notification, and payment-proof a recorded, auditable database workflow.

## E. Cross-Reference -- Parent Regulation's Own Phase-In (Context)

FACT: "The regulation is fully applied from 1 January 2025 except for articles 8 and 9 on monitoring plans that are applied from August 2024." *Source: FuelEU Maritime policy page, European Commission, DG MOVE. https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-modes/maritime/decarbonising-maritime-transport-fueleu-maritime_en

*Analytical inference:* this phase-in belongs to the parent Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, not to this database implementing regulation itself, which has no phase-in of its own (Section 14) -- it is included here so the workspace does not mistake the database's own single entry-into-force date for the parent regulation's own staggered start.

## F. Union Database Connection (Scope Statement)

FACT: "the FuelEU database environment shall be connected to the Union Database when its scope and functionalities have been adapted accordingly", referring to the Union Database established under Directive (EU) 2018/2001. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: no per-year phase-in is stated for this instrument itself (see metadata.requirement_trajectory for the parent regulation's own 2025/August 2024 split, carried here as context only). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (Part E, the parent regulation's own articles 8 and 9 exception). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (Part F, the Union Database scope-adaptation statement).

Obligations surveyed: 7; workspace-adjacent: 6; extracted as FACT: 7.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of the export date: this section is not applicable to the workspace's profile as a freight forwarder. The regulation specifies compliance infrastructure for ship operators, verifiers, and authorities; it does not regulate products or services sold by the workspace.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

## Reporting Flow Through the Database

Companies report each ship's energy consumption and emissions through the database; verifiers use it for the verification process and issuance of the FuelEU document of compliance; administering authorities access and enter the information needed for their activities.

FACT: "A notification system shall be implemented to inform the company when the verified compliance balance of its ship has been recorded in the FuelEU database." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

FACT: "The FuelEU database shall enable the verifier or the administering State as appropriate, to issue the FuelEU document of compliance for the ship concerned, as provided for in Article 22 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805." For issuance, the verifier provides the required data using an electronic template available in the database. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

After verification concludes, compliance balance information is made available by verifiers to the other user classes through the database, and document of compliance information is likewise shared after issuance.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

## Identity, Authentication, and Auditability

The database implements a secure identification mechanism assigning each user a unique ID, with authentication for system-to-system interfaces based on recognised authentication methods.

FACT: The system ensures non-repudiation of user actions: "the database shall record the user, timestamp and action carried out for any modifications", facilitating auditing and forensic analysis. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

## Interfaces and Public Information

FACT: "All information made publicly available shall be provided in English" to ensure accessibility to a wide audience. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

The database is designed to accommodate various screen sizes and viewports, with a non-support message and guidance displayed for incompatible browsers.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

## OPS Exceptions and Non-Compliance Records

The database records both exceptions to on-shore power supply obligations and records of non-compliance with those obligations (Section 8, Part B). These records feed the enforcement workflows of the parent regulation.

## Personal Data

FACT: Processing of personal data in the database is bounded by the GDPR: "The personal data should be kept in a form which permits the identification of data subjects for no longer than necessary for the purposes for which the data were collected" *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

FACT: "Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 5 ) applies." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

FACT: "The European Data Protection Supervisor was consulted in accordance with Article 42(1) of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 7 ) and delivered an opinion on 24 July 2025." *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Retention periods and data-subject rights for any personal data a company enters into the database are governed by Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 and should be confirmed by counsel where an affiliated entity acts as a database user.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

## Union Database Linkage (Renewable Energy Directive)

FACT: To support fuel certification integrity, "the FuelEU database environment shall be connected to the Union Database when its scope and functionalities have been adapted accordingly", so marine bunker fuel compliance can be demonstrated across the supply chain. *Source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394, European Commission. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32026R0394

*Analytical inference:* This planned linkage points toward end-to-end digital chain-of-custody for marine fuels. For the workspace, carrier claims about renewable or low-carbon fuel use on booked services should, over time, become verifiable against certified records rather than marketing statements.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 13 September 2023: Parent Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 (FuelEU Maritime) adopted.
- 26 July 2024: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2027 on verification activities adopted.
- 1 January 2025: Parent regulation fully applied (except articles 8 and 9, applied from August 2024).
- 24 July 2025: European Data Protection Supervisor opinion delivered.
- 24 February 2026: Published in the Official Journal (OJ L series 2026/394).
- Day following publication: entry into force of this Regulation.

*Sources: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394; FuelEU Maritime policy page, European Commission DG MOVE.*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the New York State and New York City regulatory framework governing truck and motor carrier operations: the household-goods common-carrier permitting rules at 17 CRR-NY Part 814 and the NYS DOT "Mover's Guide" that implements them, USDOT number and Unified Carrier Registration (UCR) requirements, and the NYC DOT truck-route, weight-limit, and cross-over-mirror rules that apply to commercial vehicles operating in New York City. It exists to give a freight forwarder with New York road-transport exposure a single place to see: which permits and registrations are required, what the recurring renewal cycles are, what the stated penalties for non-compliance are, and which New York City operating restrictions apply to trucks.

FACT: "This Part is applicable to the transportation of household goods, defined as personal effects and property used or to be used in a dwelling when a part of the equipment or supply of such dwelling and such other similar property." *Source: 17 CRR-NY Part 814, Transportation of Household Goods by Common Carriers, reproduced in the NYS DOT Mover's Guide. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

*Analytical inference:* the workspace's exposure to this framework depends on whether its New York operations include household-goods common-carriage (Part 814) as distinct from general freight, USDOT-numbered motor carrier operation (any commercial motor vehicle operation), or New York City truck-route/weight/mirror compliance (any truck operating on NYC streets regardless of cargo type).

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This is a live, currently-enforced state and municipal regulatory framework, not a proposed or pending rule: household-goods common-carrier permitting under Part 814, USDOT/UCR registration under federal and New York State law, and NYC DOT's truck-route and equipment rules.

FACT: "Every USDOT number holder must file a biennial update with the FMCSA every two years." *Source: How to Apply for a USDOT Number in New York, LegalClarity, citing eCFR 49 CFR 390.19. https://legalclarity.org/how-to-apply-for-a-dot-number-in-new-york/

*Operational implication:* Any workspace unit operating a commercial motor vehicle in or through New York State under its own USDOT number is directly subject to this recurring filing obligation, independent of whether it also holds a Part 814 household-goods permit.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "Missing your biennial update triggers real consequences: deactivation of your USDOT number and potential civil penalties of up to $1,000 per day, capped at $10,000." *Source: How to Apply for a USDOT Number in New York, LegalClarity. https://legalclarity.org/how-to-apply-for-a-dot-number-in-new-york/

*Operational implication:* A workspace should verify now whether every USDOT number it operates under has a current biennial update on file; a deactivated number is a legal bar to continued operation, not merely a paperwork lapse.

FACT: "Cross over mirrors must be installed on all trucks that Qualify as Commercial Vehicles , Are registered in New York State, and Operate in New York City (except for expressways)." *Source: NYC DOT, Trucks and Commercial Vehicles. http://nyc.gov/trucks

*Operational implication:* Any workspace-operated or workspace-contracted truck meeting all three conditions needs cross-over mirrors installed before operating in New York City on non-expressway streets.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Part 814 permitting and USDOT/UCR registration are duties running directly to the operating motor carrier (which may be the workspace itself, a subcontracted carrier, or both). Whether a specific workspace engagement in New York makes the workspace itself the permitted carrier of record, versus a customer of a separately permitted carrier, is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope and requires counsel or compliance-team review of the specific contracting structure.

*Analytical inference:* Because NYC DOT's truck-route, weight-limit, and cross-over-mirror rules attach to the vehicle and its registration and operation in the city (Section 3), they apply regardless of which entity in the chain is the permitted Part 814 carrier -- any truck meeting the stated conditions is covered.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Household goods shall not include property moving from a factory or store, except such property as the householder has purchased with intent to use in his or her dwelling and which is transported at the request of, and the transportation charges paid to the carrier by, the householder." *Source: 17 CRR-NY Part 814, Transportation of Household Goods by Common Carriers. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

*Per the workspace's reading:* this definitional exclusion is the operative test for whether a specific New York shipment falls inside or outside Part 814's household-goods permitting regime; factory-to-store or store-to-store freight is outside it, while a householder's own purchased goods moved to a dwelling at the householder's request and expense are inside it even if originating at a store.

FACT: "The New York City Traffic Rules and Regulations are contained in Chapter 4 of Title 34 of the Rules of the City of New York." *Source: NYC DOT, Trucks and Commercial Vehicles. http://nyc.gov/trucks

FACT: "17 CRR-NY 814.0 Current through April 30, 2019" *Source: 17 CRR-NY Part 814, Cornell LII capture reproduced in the NYS DOT Mover's Guide. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

*Operational implication:* this is the most recent currency date this brief's own captured text carries for Part 814; a workspace relying on this brief for a live compliance decision should confirm no amendment has landed since this capture date directly against NYS DOT or Cornell LII.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "November 2024 change: State Driver Licensing Agencies (including NY DMV) must now query the Clearinghouse before issuing, renewing, or upgrading CDLs." *Source: OneWayBIT, New York: Navigating Commercial Vehicle Inspections and DOT Compliance guide. https://onewaybit.com/guides/new-york-navigating-commercial-vehicle-inspections-and-dot-compliance-guide/

*Operational implication:* This is an obligation running to NY DMV as the licensing agency, not directly to a freight forwarder; its practical effect on the workspace is that a driver with an unresolved FMCSA Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse violation can be refused a new, renewed, or upgraded CDL by NY DMV, so a workspace hiring or renewing New York CDL holders should expect this check to already be in effect.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This brief's own corpus also captured a 2020 New York State Department of Transportation COVID-19 emergency order for motor carriers (Case 27647, dated by the order's own text to the Office of the Department of Transportation in the City of Albany); the captured text states no expiration date and this brief does not confirm whether any part of that order remains in effect. See Section 13 for what the order's own text states; a workspace with an active question about emergency-waiver status should confirm current status directly with NYSDOT rather than relying on this historical capture.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does operating a truck in New York City automatically make the workspace a Part 814 household-goods common carrier?**

*Analytical inference:* No. Part 814 permitting (Section 5) is defined by the nature of the cargo (household goods, as defined) and the carrier relationship, not by mere presence on New York City streets; NYC DOT's truck-route, weight, and mirror rules (Section 3) apply to any qualifying commercial vehicle regardless of Part 814 status.

**Q2: Does the USDOT biennial update obligation apply only to carriers based in New York?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* The captured source frames the biennial update as a USDOT-number-holder obligation under federal law (49 CFR 390.19), not a New York-specific one; whether a specific out-of-state workspace unit operating into New York carries its own USDOT number, and on what filing cycle, is a fact-specific registration question outside this brief's scope.

**Q3: Is Unified Carrier Registration (UCR) required in addition to, or instead of, New York's own Vehicle Identification receipt?**

FACT: "If your USDOT number identifies you as an interstate carrier, in lieu of registering for Vehicle Identification cab cards, you must register for Unified Carrier Registration (UCR)." *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

*Operational implication:* the two are alternatives keyed to interstate versus intrastate-only operating status, not cumulative requirements for the same carrier.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Bodily injury and property damage insurance minimums.** FACT: "For personal injury or death to one person, $100,000; For personal injury or death to all persons in one accident, $300,000, with a maximum of $100,000 for each person; Property damage (excluding cargo insurance), $50,000" *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

*Operational implication:* these are the minimum liability and property-damage insurance amounts a Part 814 household-goods carrier must carry and have the insurer file with NYS DOT on Form E.

**2. Cargo insurance minimums.** FACT: "For loss or damage to property being transported (cargo insurance), each motor vehicle, $5,000; For loss or damage to property being transported (cargo insurance), aggregate losses or damages at any one time and place, $10,000." *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

*Operational implication:* filed on Form H, separately from the bodily injury/property damage insurance in obligation 1.

**3. Tariff-change notice period.** FACT: "All changes to initial tariffs are effective on 30 days statutory notice (Thirty days after received by Department)." *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

*Operational implication:* a Part 814 carrier changing its filed rates cannot make the change effective sooner than 30 days after NYS DOT receives the filing.

**4. False-certification penalty on the Part 814 application.** FACT: "(Federal penalties, maximum of $20,000 or imprisonment for 5 years, or both, 18 USC 1001; State penalties, maximum $10,000 or suspension/revocation of operating authority, or both, 17 NYCRR 145)." *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this penalty attaches to a false statement on the application itself, not to ordinary operational non-compliance; the applicant's certification is made "under penalty for false statement."

**5. Part 814 applicability and definition.** FACT: "This Part is applicable to the transportation of household goods, defined as personal effects and property used or to be used in a dwelling when a part of the equipment or supply of such dwelling and such other similar property." *Source: 17 CRR-NY Part 814. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

**6. Household-goods definitional exclusion (exceptions and carve-outs).** FACT: "Household goods shall not include property moving from a factory or store, except such property as the householder has purchased with intent to use in his or her dwelling and which is transported at the request of, and the transportation charges paid to the carrier by, the householder." *Source: 17 CRR-NY Part 814. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

**7. Travel-time rate scope exception.** FACT: "Travel time does not apply on shipments transported under weight distance transportation rates (Section 3)." *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide sample tariff rules. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

*Operational implication:* travel-time charges are scoped to non-weight-distance-rated moves only; a shipment billed under weight-distance rates does not carry a separate travel-time charge.

**8. USDOT biennial update requirement.** FACT: "Every USDOT number holder must file a biennial update with the FMCSA every two years." *Source: LegalClarity, citing eCFR 49 CFR 390.19. https://legalclarity.org/how-to-apply-for-a-dot-number-in-new-york/

**9. USDOT deactivation and civil-penalty consequence.** FACT: "Missing your biennial update triggers real consequences: deactivation of your USDOT number and potential civil penalties of up to $1,000 per day, capped at $10,000." *Source: LegalClarity. https://legalclarity.org/how-to-apply-for-a-dot-number-in-new-york/

**10. New York intrastate Vehicle Identification receipt fee.** FACT: "The fee per vehicle is $10." *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide, Vehicle Identification/UCR section. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

**11. Vehicle Identification receipt annual cycle.** FACT: "Receipts must be purchased annually and are effective from January 1 through December 31 each year." *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

**12. Unified Carrier Registration yearly requirement.** FACT: "This is also a yearly requirement, with the fee based on the number of commercial motor vehicles you operate." *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

**13. Workers' Compensation and Disability Benefits exemption validity.** FACT: "Worker's Compensation & Disability Benefits exemption is valid for one (1) year from the date of issuance." *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

**14. NYC parkway restriction.** FACT: "Trucks and commercial vehicles cannot travel on most parkways in New York City." *Source: NYC DOT, Trucks and Commercial Vehicles. http://nyc.gov/trucks

**15. NYC truck route network.** FACT: "With nearly 1,000 miles of designated roadway, New York City has one of the most complex truck route systems in the nation." *Source: NYC DOT, Trucks and Commercial Vehicles. http://nyc.gov/trucks

**16. NYC gross vehicle weight limit.** FACT: "The allowed gross vehicle weight in New York City is 80,000 pounds." *Source: NYC DOT, Trucks and Commercial Vehicles. http://nyc.gov/trucks

**17. NYC cross-over mirror requirement.** FACT: "Cross over mirrors must be installed on all trucks that Qualify as Commercial Vehicles , Are registered in New York State, and Operate in New York City (except for expressways)." *Source: NYC DOT, Trucks and Commercial Vehicles. http://nyc.gov/trucks

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the recurring 2-year USDOT biennial-update cycle and the recurring annual January 1 to December 31 New York Vehicle Identification/UCR cycle). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 6, the household-goods definitional exclusion). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 7, the travel-time rate scope exception).

Obligations surveyed: 19; workspace-adjacent: 17; extracted as FACT: 17.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*Note: this framework does not distinguish compliance status by cargo product beyond the Part 814 household-goods definition already stated in Sections 5 and 8 (obligations 5 and 6); no source in this brief's corpus states a separate product-specific compliance regime (for example, hazardous materials or refrigerated cargo) within this particular framework.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Every USDOT number holder must file a biennial update with the FMCSA every two years." *Source: LegalClarity. https://legalclarity.org/how-to-apply-for-a-dot-number-in-new-york/

FACT: "The fee per vehicle is $10." *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

FACT: "This is also a yearly requirement, with the fee based on the number of commercial motor vehicles you operate." *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

FACT: "Worker's Compensation & Disability Benefits exemption is valid for one (1) year from the date of issuance." *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

*Operational implication:* a New York intrastate-only carrier registers Vehicle Identification receipts per vehicle annually; an interstate carrier registers UCR annually instead; both are separate from the federal USDOT biennial update cycle.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: "operational system requirements" here means the vehicle-equipment and route-compliance infrastructure a New York City truck operation must maintain, plus the monitoring a workspace should keep on its own USDOT filing status.*

**1. Cross-over mirrors.** FACT: "Cross over mirrors must be installed on all trucks that Qualify as Commercial Vehicles , Are registered in New York State, and Operate in New York City (except for expressways)." *Source: NYC DOT, Trucks and Commercial Vehicles. http://nyc.gov/trucks

**2. Vehicle identification/registrant display.** FACT: "The New York City Traffic Rules require that commercial vehicles display the registrant's name and address on both sides of the vehicle. This is described in Section 4.08 of the Traffic Rules." *Source: NYC DOT, Trucks and Commercial Vehicles. http://nyc.gov/trucks

**3. Weight and route compliance.** FACT: "The allowed gross vehicle weight in New York City is 80,000 pounds." *Source: NYC DOT, Trucks and Commercial Vehicles. http://nyc.gov/trucks

*Operational implication:* a workspace dispatching trucks into New York City should maintain a recurring check of its USDOT biennial filing status (Section 8, obligation 8) alongside vehicle-level route, weight, and mirror compliance, since the two compliance tracks (federal registration and NYC vehicle/route rules) are independent of each other.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "Household goods shall not include property moving from a factory or store, except such property as the householder has purchased with intent to use in his or her dwelling and which is transported at the request of, and the transportation charges paid to the carrier by, the householder." *Source: 17 CRR-NY Part 814. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

FACT: "Travel time does not apply on shipments transported under weight distance transportation rates (Section 3)." *Source: NYS DOT Mover's Guide sample tariff rules. https://www.dot.ny.gov/divisions/operating/osss/repository/HHG%20Binder-%20Updated%202-28-24.pdf

FACT: "Cross over mirrors must be installed on all trucks that Qualify as Commercial Vehicles , Are registered in New York State, and Operate in New York City (except for expressways)." *Source: NYC DOT, Trucks and Commercial Vehicles. http://nyc.gov/trucks

*Analytical inference:* the cross-over mirror requirement's own "except for expressways" clause is the framework's narrowest edge case -- a qualifying truck operating exclusively on NYC expressways, with no non-expressway street operation, falls outside this specific equipment mandate even though it remains subject to every other requirement in this brief.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "At the Office of the Department of Transportation in the City of Albany on May 13, 2020" *Source: NYSDOT COVID-19 Order for Motor Carriers, Case 27647, as captured by FMCSA. https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/emergency/new-york-department-transportation-covid-19-order-motor-carriers

FACT: "That motor carrier vehicles shall not travel on any Parkways in New York where commercial vehicles are prohibited." *Source: NYSDOT COVID-19 Order for Motor Carriers, Case 27647. https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/emergency/new-york-department-transportation-covid-19-order-motor-carriers

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this is a 2020 emergency order; the captured text states no expiration date and this brief does not confirm current effect (see Section 6). It is presented here as historical context for the same parkway-restriction subject matter Section 8 (obligation 14) covers on a non-emergency basis, not as a currently-relied-upon independent obligation.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- April 30, 2019: 17 CRR-NY Part 814 (Transportation of Household Goods by Common Carriers) is current through this date in the captured Cornell LII source.
- May 13, 2020: NYSDOT issues its COVID-19 Order for Motor Carriers, Case 27647 (historical; current effect not confirmed, see Sections 6 and 13).
- November 2024: State Driver Licensing Agencies, including NY DMV, began querying the FMCSA Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse before issuing, renewing, or upgrading CDLs.

*Operational implication:* the November 2024 change is the most recent dated milestone in this corpus and the one most likely to affect a workspace hiring or renewing New York CDL holders; the two earlier dates mark this brief's own source-currency limits rather than ongoing obligations.

*Source for timeline entries: 17 CRR-NY Part 814 via Cornell LII (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/new-york/title-17/chapter-VI/subchapter-E/article-2/part-814); NYSDOT COVID-19 Order for Motor Carriers, Case 27647, as captured by FMCSA (https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/emergency/new-york-department-transportation-covid-19-order-motor-carriers); OneWayBIT commercial vehicle compliance guide (https://onewaybit.com/guides/new-york-navigating-commercial-vehicle-inspections-and-dot-compliance-guide/).*

metadata.what_is_it: New York's household-goods common-carrier permitting rules (17 CRR-NY Part 814), USDOT number and Unified Carrier Registration requirements, and NYC DOT's truck-route, weight-limit, and equipment rules for commercial vehicles operating in New York City.
metadata.why_matters: It sets the recurring registration and insurance-filing cycles (USDOT biennial, New York annual) a New York-operating carrier must keep current, states the stated penalties for lapses, and sets the New York City street-level equipment and route rules that apply to any qualifying truck.
key_data: USDOT biennial update required every two years under 49 CFR 390.19
USDOT deactivation civil penalty up to $1000 per day capped at $10000
Part 814 bodily injury/property damage insurance minimums of $100000/$300000/$50000
Part 814 cargo insurance minimums of $5000 per vehicle and $10000 aggregate
NYC gross vehicle weight limit of 80000 pounds

steps.label: Every USDOT number holder must file a biennial update with the FMCSA every two years

steps.value: New York intrastate Vehicle Identification / UCR registration cycle
steps.label: Vehicle Identification receipts and Unified Carrier Registration are purchased on a yearly cycle

requirement_trajectory.note: Both cycles are recurring administrative renewal cycles; no source in this corpus states a sub-cycle phase-in of individual substantive obligations within either cycle.

metadata.penalty_range: civil penalties up to $1,000 per day, capped at $10,000 (USDOT deactivation); up to $20,000 federal / $10,000 state for false certification on the Part 814 application
metadata.enforcement_body: FMCSA administers USDOT registration; NYS DOT administers Part 814 permitting; NYC DOT administers truck-route, weight, and equipment rules

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Slovenia's National Energy and Climate Plan (NEPN, also referred to as NECP) process: the currently-operative Integrated NEPN 2021-2030 (adopted December 27, 2024) and the newly-initiated preparation of the NEPN 2030-2040 (announced May 13, 2026). It exists to give a freight forwarder with Slovenian or Central/Southeast European road, rail, or intermodal exposure a single place to see: which EU and Slovenian targets are already binding on the government, which are still being drafted, what the EU submission deadlines are, and which of the plan's transport and energy targets are most likely to affect fuel pricing, infrastructure, and grid electricity emission factors.

FACT: "The NEPN is Slovenia’s main strategic document for energy and climate policy over a ten-year period, aligned with long-term climate goals." *Source: Slovenia begins preparation of NEPN 2030-2040, CEENERGYNEWS, May 13, 2026. https://ceenergynews.com/climate/slovenia-new-nepn-2030-2040/

*Analytical inference:* this is a government-to-EU planning obligation, not a rule with private-party compliance duties; the workspace's exposure is indirect, through the targets' downstream effect on fuel availability, pricing, and infrastructure investment in Slovenia.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This is a live, EU-mandated national planning instrument, not a proposed or pending rule at the EU level (the Governance Regulation itself is already in force); the specific NEPN 2030-2040 content is still in early preparation.

FACT: "Required under the Regulation (EU)2018/1999 on the governance of the energy union and climate action (Governance Regulation), the NECPs first took shape in 2020 and have since then been updated to incorporate the ambitious targets set by the European Green Deal," *Source: European Commission, National energy and climate plans. https://commission.europa.eu/energy-climate-change-environment/implementation-eu-countries/energy-and-climate-governance-and-reporting/national-energy-and-climate-plans_en

*Operational implication:* the currently-operative Integrated NEPN 2021-2030 (Section 8) already sets binding-on-government targets affecting transport-sector renewable fuel content, fossil fuel subsidies, and coal-fired power capacity that a workspace routing freight through Slovenia should track now, independent of the 2030-2040 update's own timeline.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "Member States must submit a draft updated NEPN to the European Commission by 1 January 2028 and adopt the final version by 1 January 2029." *Source: CEENERGYNEWS. https://ceenergynews.com/climate/slovenia-new-nepn-2030-2040/

*Operational implication:* a workspace tracking Slovenia's regulatory trajectory should expect the draft NEPN 2030-2040 (with its own transport and fuel-sector targets) to become public no later than January 2028, roughly 16 months from this brief's own capture date.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the NEPN/NECP obligations described in Section 8 run from Slovenia to the European Commission under the Governance Regulation (EU) 2018/1999, not from Slovenia (or the EU) to a private freight forwarder. Whether any specific Slovenian implementing measure adopted to meet a NEPN target (for example, a fuel-tax or subsidy change) creates a direct compliance duty on a specific workspace operation is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope and requires counsel or compliance-team review of the specific implementing measure once adopted.

*Analytical inference:* because the plan's transport-sector target (Section 8) and fossil-fuel-subsidy phase-out (Section 8) are the two elements most likely to flow into fuel-pricing and availability, they are the practical leverage points for a workspace's own Slovenian fuel-sourcing and routing planning, not a source of direct legal obligation.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Each country shall submit a progress report every 2 years, according to the structure, format, technical details and process set out in the" *Source: European Commission, National energy and climate plans. https://commission.europa.eu/energy-climate-change-environment/implementation-eu-countries/energy-and-climate-governance-and-reporting/national-energy-and-climate-plans_en

*Per the workspace's reading:* this is the recurring monitoring mechanism underneath the plan (separate from the once-per-decade full NEPN revision cycle described in Sections 2 and 3); it is how a workspace can track incremental progress against the 2030 targets in Section 8 between now and the next full plan revision.

FACT: "On 27 February 2020, the Slovenian Government adopted the Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan of the Republic of Slovenia (NECP). This version of the NECP was already lacking ambition in four main areas. The target for reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 of 36% by 2030 (compared to 2005) was not sufficient" *Source: Together for 1.5C (Climate Action Network Europe), Slovenia country page. https://1point5.caneurope.org/countries/slovenia/

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "Slovenia aims to decide by 2028 whether it will build its second nuclear power plant." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News, Slovenia adopts updated Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

*Operational implication:* the 2028 nuclear decision is a distinct forward event from the 2028/2029 NEPN 2030-2040 submission deadlines in Section 3; a workspace tracking Slovenian grid-electricity emission factors for Scope 2/3 reporting should watch both separately.

FACT: "A small modular reactor (SMR), of 250 MW, would come online by mid-century, the NECP reads." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this brief's own captured text confirms the Slovenian government reorganised its ministries at some point before this capture (the ministry the item's own source_url names as "Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Energy" is captured here under the name "Ministry of the Environment and Spatial Planning"); this brief does not independently confirm the exact reorganisation date or which ministry now holds the energy portfolio, and a workspace with a live question about current ministerial responsibility for the NEPN process should confirm directly with the Slovenian government.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the currently-operative Integrated NEPN 2021-2030, or the not-yet-drafted NEPN 2030-2040, govern Slovenia's targets today?**

*Analytical inference:* the Integrated NEPN 2021-2030 (adopted December 27, 2024, Section 8) is the currently-operative instrument; the NEPN 2030-2040 (Sections 2 and 3) is still in the analytical-groundwork and public-consultation stage as of this brief's own capture date and is not yet a binding document.

**Q2: Does Slovenia's 2033 coal-exit date change its EU Fit for 55 compliance timeline?**

FACT: "The Fit-for-55 goal of a 55% drop in emissions is for 2030. Slovenia aims to achieve it only by 2033, the deadline it set for quitting the use of coal." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the 2033 coal-exit date creates any interim compliance gap against the EU-wide 2030 Fit for 55 target is a question this brief's own corpus does not resolve; the captured text states only that Slovenia targets 2033 for its own coal exit, not any EU-level consequence of that gap.

**Q3: Is there a stated penalty or fine for a Member State that misses a NEPN submission or target deadline?**

GAP: No source in this brief's corpus states a penalty, fine, or sanction running to Slovenia (or to any private party) for missing a NEPN submission deadline or a stated target; the captured European Commission process page describes submission deadlines and Commission assessments only, with no stated enforcement consequence.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. NEPN 2030-2040 submission deadlines.** FACT: "Member States must submit a draft updated NEPN to the European Commission by 1 January 2028 and adopt the final version by 1 January 2029." *Source: CEENERGYNEWS. https://ceenergynews.com/climate/slovenia-new-nepn-2030-2040/

**2. Governance Regulation legal basis.** FACT: "Required under the Regulation (EU)2018/1999 on the governance of the energy union and climate action (Governance Regulation), the NECPs first took shape in 2020 and have since then been updated to incorporate the ambitious targets set by the European Green Deal," *Source: European Commission. https://commission.europa.eu/energy-climate-change-environment/implementation-eu-countries/energy-and-climate-governance-and-reporting/national-energy-and-climate-plans_en

**3. Biennial progress-report requirement.** FACT: "Each country shall submit a progress report every 2 years, according to the structure, format, technical details and process set out in the" *Source: European Commission. https://commission.europa.eu/energy-climate-change-environment/implementation-eu-countries/energy-and-climate-governance-and-reporting/national-energy-and-climate-plans_en

**4. EU 2040 and Slovenia 2045 targets underlying the new plan.** FACT: "the European Union. Home … Topics Climate action Delivering the European Green Deal Fit for 55: Delivering on the proposals Fit for 55: Delivering on the proposals On the path to climate neutrality Under the European Climate Law, the EU committed to reduce its net greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030. The ‘Fit for 55’ package of legislation makes all sectors of the EU’s economy fit to meet this target. It sets the EU on a path to reach its climate targets in a fair, cost-effective and competitive way. For each of the countries covered, the tool looks into overall and sectoral greenhouse gas emissions reduction pathways and some energy transition indicators . In other words, the tool shows where Member States really stand, what they have promised and how far they are from the minimum EU requirements. By doing so, it provides key information to identify gaps in ambition and implementation of national climate action. Check the key findings and methodology behind the figures. Key findings The October 2024 update of the NECP tracker revelas that: Despite some improvements, the current level of ambition of the latest available NECP updates is insufficient not only to align with Paris Agreement commitments, but also to reach the EU 2030 climate and energy objectives , which would be in breach of the European Climate Law. The implementation of the old 2019 NECPs is lagging behind . All Member States assessed in the tracker seem to show some worrying trends and gaps in keeping up to their pledges. NECPs present varying but overall poor transparency and quality of data , which hinders the plans’ credibility as well as access to information. Home Climate Slovenia begins preparation of NEPN 2030–2040 Climate Powered by Slovenia begins preparation of NEPN 2030–2040 By Emese Fabian May 13, 2026 Facebook X WhatsApp Linkedin Email Print Slovenia has started preparing its new National Energy and Climate Plan (NEPN) for 2030- 2040 and is inviting the public and experts to take part in a consultation on long-term scenarios that will form the basis of future energy and climate policy. The NEPN is Slovenia’s main strategic document for energy and climate policy over a ten-year period, aligned with long-term climate goals. Member States must submit a draft updated NEPN to the European Commission by 1 January 2028 and adopt the final version by 1 January 2029. The first step is preparing analytical groundwork, including long-term scenarios for different pathways towards climate neutrality. These scenarios are based on two key commitments: the European Union’s target of a 90 per cent net emissions reduction by 2040 compared to 1990 levels, and Slovenia’s national commitment to achieve climate neutrality by 2045." *Source: CEENERGYNEWS. https://ceenergynews.com/climate/slovenia-new-nepn-2030-2040/

Transport-sector renewables target (2030).** FACT: "The government is targeting a 55.4% share of renewables in electricity, 45.2% in heating and cooling and 25.8% in transportation, according to the updated NECP for 2030." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

*Operational implication:* the transport-sector renewables share rising to 25.8% by 2030 is the single most operationally relevant figure in this brief for a road-freight workspace, since it drives the required renewable content of fuel sold in Slovenia over the current decade.

**6. Overall renewables target (2030).** FACT: "The targeted share of renewables in gross final energy consumption 33%." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

**7. Fossil fuel subsidy phase-out.** FACT: "The plan stipulates ending fossil fuel subsidies by the end of the period." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

**8. Gross final energy consumption cap.** FACT: "Gross final energy consumption in 2030 is determined at a maximum of 50.2 TWh, compared to 54.9 TWh in the initial document, adopted in 2020." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

**9. Coal exit and 2033 emissions-reduction deadline.** FACT: "The Fit-for-55 goal of a 55% drop in emissions is for 2030. Slovenia aims to achieve it only by 2033, the deadline it set for quitting the use of coal." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

**10. Buildings-sector emissions target.** FACT: "Slovenia now aspires to cut emissions in buildings by at least 70%." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

**11. Investment envelope (scenario total).** FACT: "The scenario with additional measures in Slovenia’s updated Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP or, in Slovenian, NEPN) envisages EUR 57 billion in investment from 2021 until the end of the decade." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

**12. Investment envelope (government-adopted, energy/climate-specific).** FACT: "The government adopted the final document, which envisages EUR 22 billion for energy and climate targets in particular." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

**13. Investment breakdown by category.** FACT: "The biggest chunk, EUR 5.4 billion, is for households, with measures including energy renovation and the replacement of devices. Electricity distribution and transmission grids are entitled to EUR 4 billion, followed by distributed electricity generation from renewable sources, EUR 3.8 billion." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

**14. Public-sector investment total.** FACT: "Total public sector investments 2021-2030 are estimated at EUR 6.9 billion." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

**15. Hydrogen infrastructure investment target.** FACT: "Projected investments in hydrogen infrastructure by 2030 are EUR 223 million, of which nearly the entire amount is for a pipeline system and electrolyzers." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

**19. Gas power-generation capacity cap.** FACT: "The Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan envisages an overall 500 MW in gas power plants in Slovenia by the end of the decade." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

**20. Cross-border electricity connectivity target.** FACT: "Slovenia plans to maintain a high level of electricity connectivity with neighboring countries, with a goal of more than 80%." *Source: Balkan Green Energy News. https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*Note: this framework sets national and sector-level energy targets, not product-level compliance requirements; no source in this brief's corpus states a product-specific compliance regime (for example, a vehicle emissions standard) within this particular plan.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Member States must submit a draft updated NEPN to the European Commission by 1 January 2028 and adopt the final version by 1 January 2029." *Source: CEENERGYNEWS. https://ceenergynews.com/climate/slovenia-new-nepn-2030-2040/

FACT: "Each country shall submit a progress report every 2 years, according to the structure, format, technical details and process set out in the" *Source: European Commission. https://commission.europa.eu/energy-climate-change-environment/implementation-eu-countries/energy-and-climate-governance-and-reporting/national-energy-and-climate-plans_en

*Operational implication:* these are government-to-Commission reporting obligations; no source in this brief's corpus states a parallel reporting obligation running from a private freight forwarder to either the Slovenian government or the European Commission under this specific framework.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: "operational system requirements" here means the monitoring a workspace should maintain on Slovenia's energy-transition targets, not a technical system the plan itself requires the workspace to build.*

**1. Fuel-pricing and availability monitoring.** *Operational implication:* a workspace should track the transport-sector renewables target (Section 8, obligation 5) and the fossil fuel subsidy phase-out (Section 8, obligation 7) as the two levers most likely to change diesel and alternative-fuel economics for Slovenian road freight over the current decade.

**2. Grid-emission-factor monitoring for Scope 2/3 reporting.** *Operational implication:* the coal-exit date (Section 8, obligation 9) and the domestic power-supply and connectivity targets (Section 8, obligations 18 and 20) together determine how quickly Slovenian grid electricity's emission factor is likely to fall, which is relevant to a workspace's own Scope 2/3 emissions accounting for Slovenian operations.

**3. NEPN 2030-2040 drafting-calendar monitoring.** FACT: "Member States must submit a draft updated NEPN to the European Commission by 1 January 2028 and adopt the final version by 1 January 2029." *Source: CEENERGYNEWS. https://ceenergynews.com/climate/slovenia-new-nepn-2030-2040/

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

GAP: No exceptions, carve-outs, or exemptions running to a private freight forwarder are stated anywhere in this brief's corpus; every target and deadline in Section 8 runs to the Slovenian government or, at the EU level, to Member States collectively.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "On 27 February 2020, the Slovenian Government adopted the Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan of the Republic of Slovenia (NECP). This version of the NECP was already lacking ambition in four main areas. The target for reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 of 36% by 2030 (compared to 2005) was not sufficient" *Source: Together for 1.5C (Climate Action Network Europe). https://1point5.caneurope.org/countries/slovenia/

*Analytical inference:* Together for 1.5C is an NGO advocacy tracker, not an authoritative source of Slovenian government policy; its own assessment (that the 2019 NECP's 36% target, and the current NEPN's ambition level, remain below what a 1.5C-aligned trajectory would require) is adjacent commentary on the same targets Section 8 reports from primary/government-adjacent sources, not itself a governing instrument.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- February 27, 2020: original Slovenian Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) adopted.
- December 27, 2024: updated Integrated NEPN 2021-2030 adopted by the Slovenian government.
- May 13, 2026: Slovenia initiates preparation of the NEPN 2030-2040; public and expert consultation on long-term scenarios opens.
- 2027: draft NEPN 2030-2040 to be prepared and consulted.
- January 1, 2028: draft NEPN 2030-2040 due at the European Commission.
- 2028: decision due on Slovenia's second nuclear power plant.
- January 1, 2029: final NEPN 2030-2040 due for adoption by Slovenia.
- 2030: operative NEPN 2021-2030 targets apply (33% overall renewables; 25.8% transport renewables; fossil fuel subsidies ended; maximum 50.2 TWh gross final energy consumption).
- 2033: Slovenia's targeted coal-exit date and 55% emissions-reduction deadline (versus 2005).
- 2040: Slovenia's targeted second nuclear power plant online date; the EU's 90 per cent net emissions reduction target (versus 1990) underlies the NEPN 2030-2040 design.
- 2045: Slovenia's national climate-neutrality commitment.
- 2050: small modular reactor (250 MW) targeted online.

*Source for timeline entries: CEENERGYNEWS (https://ceenergynews.com/climate/slovenia-new-nepn-2030-2040/); Balkan Green Energy News (https://balkangreenenergynews.com/slovenia-adopts-updated-integrated-national-energy-and-climate-plan/); European Commission, National energy and climate plans (https://commission.europa.eu/energy-climate-change-environment/implementation-eu-countries/energy-and-climate-governance-and-reporting/national-energy-and-climate-plans_en); Together for 1.5C (https://1point5.caneurope.org/countries/slovenia/).*

National Energy and Climate Plans (NECPs) are the right opportunity to push the fast-forward button and accelerate climate action. Inspiring stories from all over Europe showcase how the just transition can be accelerated, as the deadline for Member States to come up with their new draft NECPs – end of June 2023 – is swiftly approaching. Climate and environment NGOs based in 12 European countries gathered almost one hundred concrete examples of climate action measures implemented on the ground. These should inspire all governments and put Europe on track for achieving a safe and stable climate and to ensure we all harvest the benefits of a sustainable life. By examining the stories of countries taking action, such as promoting clean public transport, advancing renewable energy deployment, greening cities, shortening food supply chains, and combating energy poverty, we can find inspiration. We should urge our governments to include these effective measures in their NECPs and exclude those that civil society deems problematic. Home … Topics Climate action Delivering the European Green Deal Fit for 55: Delivering on the proposals Fit for 55: Delivering on the proposals On the path to climate neutrality Under the European Climate Law, the EU committed to reduce its net greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030. The ‘Fit for 55’ package of legislation makes all sectors of the EU’s economy fit to meet this target. It sets the EU on a path to reach its climate targets in a fair, cost-effective and competitive way. For each of the countries covered, the tool looks into overall and sectoral greenhouse gas emissions reduction pathways and some energy transition indicators . In other words, the tool shows where Member States really stand, what they have promised and how far they are from the minimum EU requirements. By doing so, it provides key information to identify gaps in ambition and implementation of national climate action. Check the key findings and methodology behind the figures. Key findings The October 2024 update of the NECP tracker revelas that: Despite some improvements, the current level of ambition of the latest available NECP updates is insufficient not only to align with Paris Agreement commitments, but also to reach the EU 2030 climate and energy objectives , which would be in breach of the European Climate Law. The implementation of the old 2019 NECPs is lagging behind . All Member States assessed in the tracker seem to show some worrying trends and gaps in keeping up to their pledges. NECPs present varying but overall poor transparency and quality of data , which hinders the plans’ credibility as well as access to information. Home Climate Slovenia begins preparation of NEPN 2030–2040 Climate Powered by Slovenia begins preparation of NEPN 2030–2040 By Emese Fabian May 13, 2026 Facebook X WhatsApp Linkedin Email Print Slovenia has started preparing its new National Energy and Climate Plan (NEPN) for 2030- 2040 and is inviting the public and experts to take part in a consultation on long-term scenarios that will form the basis of future energy and climate policy. The NEPN is Slovenia’s main strategic document for energy and climate policy over a ten-year period, aligned with long-term climate goals. Member States must submit a draft updated NEPN to the European Commission by 1 January 2028 and adopt the final version by 1 January 2029. The first step is preparing analytical groundwork, including long-term scenarios for different pathways towards climate neutrality. These scenarios are based on two key commitments: the European Union’s target of a 90 per cent net emissions reduction by 2040 compared to 1990 levels, and Slovenia’s national commitment to achieve climate neutrality by 2045.
