entries.body: # 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) No 815/2013, a narrow technical amendment that replaces the Annex to Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 (the EU Emissions Trading System list of aircraft operators and their administering Member State) to take Croatia's 2013 accession into account. It exists to give a workspace with EU aviation exposure a single place to confirm the amendment's own scope, effective date, and the absence of any independent compliance deadline or penalty in this Regulation's own text. FACT: "amending Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 on the list of aircraft operators that performed an aviation activity listed in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on or after 1 January 2006 specifying the administering Member State for each aircraft operator to take into consideration the accession of Croatia to the European Union" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 815/2013, EUR-Lex CELEX:32013R0815. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R0815 **Coverage note.** This brief addresses the Regulation's own recitals and two operative Articles as captured from the EUR-Lex legal-content page; the replacement Annex itself (the operator-by-operator administering-state list, several million characters of tabular data) was captured but not individually itemised, since it is a data table rather than obligation-shaped text. # 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace FACT: "Directive 2008/101/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council (2) amended Directive 2003/87/EC to include aviation activities in the scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the European Union." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 815/2013, recital 1, EUR-Lex CELEX:32013R0815. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R0815 FACT: "Commission Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 (3) establishes a list of aircraft operators which had performed an aviation activity as defined in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC on or after 1 January 2006." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 815/2013, recital 2, EUR-Lex CELEX:32013R0815. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R0815 FACT: "That list aims to reduce the administrative burden on aircraft operators by providing information on which Member State will be regulating a particular aircraft operator." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 815/2013, recital 3, EUR-Lex CELEX:32013R0815. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R0815 FACT: "The inclusion of an aircraft operator in the Union's emissions trading scheme is dependent upon the performance of an aviation activity as set out in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC and is not dependent on the inclusion in the list of aircraft operators established by the Commission on the basis of Article 18a(3) of that Directive." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 815/2013, recital 4, EUR-Lex CELEX:32013R0815. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R0815 *Operational implication:* an aircraft operator's EU ETS obligations turn on performing an Annex I Directive 2003/87/EC aviation activity, not on its presence on (or absence from) the Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 list this Regulation replaces; a workspace should not treat inclusion or exclusion from the Annex as itself determinative of ETS liability. # 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action *No content for this section: this Regulation has been fully in force since 2013 and its sole substantive effect (the one-time Annex replacement) is complete; nothing in the captured text presents an open, time-sensitive action item for the workspace today.* # 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain *Legal Confirmation Required:* this Regulation creates no new compliance obligation, fee, or deadline running to an aircraft operator directly; it re-attributes which Member State administers certain aircraft operators' EU ETS compliance following Croatia's accession. Whether a specific aircraft operator's own administering-Member-State attribution changed under the replacement Annex should be confirmed against that Annex (not individually captured here) or with the relevant national competent authority, not inferred from this brief alone. FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 815/2013, closing clause, EUR-Lex CELEX:32013R0815. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R0815 FACT: "[jurisdictional_scope] The accession of Croatia to the European Union on 1 July 2013 and the criteria set under Article 18a(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC to determine an aircraft operator's administering Member State imply that certain aircraft operators should be administered by Croatia." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 815/2013, recital 5, EUR-Lex CELEX:32013R0815. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R0815 *Analytical inference:* because the Regulation's own effect is a Member-State re-attribution rather than a new duty, the workspace's practical compliance-chain position is unchanged by this Regulation itself; only the identity of the administering Member State for certain aircraft operators may have changed. # 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis *No content for this section: the captured pool contains only this Regulation's own text (recitals, two Articles, and the replacement Annex); no separate authoritative guidance document interpreting it was found in the corpus.* # 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events *No content for this section: this item's export carries no forward_events, and the Regulation has been fully in force since 2013 with no pending amendment, review clause, or scheduled event in the captured text.* # 7. Threshold Questions **Q1: Does this Regulation change which aircraft operators must comply with the EU ETS?** *Analytical inference:* No. Per recital 4 above, ETS liability depends on performing an Annex I Directive 2003/87/EC aviation activity, not on inclusion in the Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 list this Regulation replaces; this Regulation only reassigns which Member State administers certain already-covered operators. **Q2: Does the workspace need to check the replacement Annex directly?** *Legal Confirmation Required:* a workspace with an aircraft operator counterparty potentially affected by Croatia's accession should confirm that operator's current administering Member State against the replacement Annex itself (not individually captured in this brief's pool extraction) rather than against the superseded Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 list. # 8. Substantive Requirements **1. Annex replacement (the Regulation's sole operative substantive change).** FACT: "The Annex to Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 is replaced by the Annex to this Regulation." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 815/2013, Article 1, EUR-Lex CELEX:32013R0815. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R0815 *Operational implication:* this is the entirety of this Regulation's substantive legal effect; every other provision (recitals, Article 2, the closing clause) is either background reasoning or a standard EU-regulation formality. **2. Entry into force (effective_date).** FACT: "[effective_date] This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 815/2013, Article 2, EUR-Lex CELEX:32013R0815. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R0815 FACT: "OJ L 236, 4.9.2013, pp. 1–188" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 815/2013, Official Journal citation, EUR-Lex CELEX:32013R0815. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R0815 *Analytical inference:* Article 2 sets entry into force at the third day after Official Journal publication; the Official Journal publication itself is dated 4.9.2013 (OJ L 236, 4.9.2013), so the derived entry-into-force date is 7.9.2013. This derived date is analytical, not itself a separate date stated in the Regulation's own text. **3. No penalty provision (penalty_summary).** GAP: no penalty, fine, or sanctions provision was identified anywhere in this Regulation's captured recitals, operative Articles, or replacement Annex (a full-text search for "enalt" and "sanction" across the entire captured document returned zero matches). This Regulation carries no enforcement mechanism of its own; EU ETS compliance penalties (where applicable to an aircraft operator generally) derive from Directive 2003/87/EC and national implementing legislation, not from this Regulation's own text. **4. No compliance deadline distinct from entry into force (primary_deadline).** GAP: no compliance deadline distinct from the Article 2 entry-into-force date was found in the captured text; the Regulation's sole substantive effect (obligation 1 above) is an immediate, one-time Annex replacement with no phased or scheduled compliance date of its own. **Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2. Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 2. Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 2. Obligations surveyed: 3; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 2. Shortfall: the third surveyed obligation (the Regulation's general binding-and-directly-applicable closing clause) is captured as a FACT claim attached to Section 4 rather than Section 8, and the pool's remaining several million characters are the replacement Annex's own data table, not further obligation-shaped prose. # 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status *No content for this section: this Regulation concerns aircraft-operator administering-Member-State attribution, not a product compliance status; nothing in the captured text speaks to a specific product.* # 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations *No content for this section: no registration or reporting obligation running to an aircraft operator appears anywhere in this Regulation's own captured text; registration/reporting under the EU ETS more broadly derives from Directive 2003/87/EC, not from this amending Regulation.* # 11. Operational System Requirements *Operational implication:* a workspace with an aircraft-operator counterparty potentially affected by Croatia's 2013 accession should maintain a record of that operator's current administering Member State, cross-checked against the replacement Annex rather than the superseded Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 list, since this Regulation's own text does not restate the Annex's individual entries. # 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases *No content for this section: no exemption or edge-case provision was found anywhere in this Regulation's own captured recitals, Articles, or closing clause.* # 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives *No content for this section: the captured pool contains only this Regulation's own text; no adjacent industry research, alternative instrument, or related body's material was captured for this item.* # 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline - August 27, 2013: Commission Regulation (EU) No 815/2013 adopted (from the instrument title). - September 4, 2013: Regulation published in the Official Journal (OJ L 236, 4.9.2013). - September 7, 2013: Regulation enters into force under Article 2, the third day following its Official Journal publication (derived from the Article 2 entry-into-force rule and the Official Journal's own publication date; not itself a separate date stated in the Regulation's text). # 15. Sources | # | Source | Type | URL | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Commission Regulation (EU) No 815/2013 of 27 August 2013, EUR-Lex legal-content page | EU legislative instrument (EUR-Lex) | https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013R0815 |

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Norway's zero-emission requirements for cruise ships, tourist boats, and ferries operating in the UNESCO World Heritage fjords, adopted by the Norwegian Maritime Authority (NMA) Circular RSR 04-2025 amending the Environmental Safety Regulations. It exists to give a freight forwarder or cruise/ferry operator with Norwegian fjord exposure a single place to see: the phased effective dates by vessel size, the exemption pathways and their own hard deadline, the shore power and biogas alternatives, and the stated enforcement mechanism.

FACT: "The Norwegian Government has decided to introduce zero-emission requirements in the World Heritage fjords, effective from 1 January 2026 for passenger ships of less than 10,000 gross tonnage, and from 1 January 2032 for passenger ships of 10,000 gross tonnage and upwards." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

*Analytical inference:* the phased dual-threshold structure (10,000 gross tonnage as the dividing line) means a workspace's exposure timeline depends directly on vessel size, not on operator type.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This is a live, adopted regulatory amendment (not a proposal): the NMA circular explains regulations already amended into the Environmental Safety Regulations (Forskrift om miljomessig sikkerhet).

FACT: "The World Heritage Fjords include the five fjords: Nærøyfjorden, Aurlandsfjorden, Geirangerfjorden, Sunnylvsfjorden, and Tafjorden." *Source: Norwegian Government (regjeringen.no), Introducing Zero-Emission Requirements in the World Heritage Fjords. https://www.regjeringen.no/en/whats-new/introducing-zero-emission-requirements-in-the-world-heritage-fjords/id3051481/

*Operational implication:* a workspace operating or chartering any passenger vessel (cruise ship, tourist boat, or ferry carrying more than 12 passengers) that calls at any of these five fjords is within scope, regardless of whether the voyage transits the fjords fully or only partially (Section 8).

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "The first paragraph of the provision stipulates that, from 1 January 2026, passenger ships of less than 10,000 gross tonnage operating in the World Heritage fjords shall use energy sources that do not result in direct emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2) or methane (CH4). According to the second paragraph, from 1 January 2032, passenger ships of 10,000 gross tonnage and upwards operating in the World Heritage fjords shall use energy sources that do not result in direct emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2) or methane (CH4)." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

*Operational implication:* the first threshold (the smaller-vessel tier) is already in force as of the export date, well after the 1 January 2026 effective date; a workspace operating a qualifying small passenger vessel should confirm compliance now, not treat this as a future deadline.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "Although the requirements apply to individual ships, it is the company's responsibility to ensure compliance in accordance with section 4 of the Ship Safety and Security Act." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

*Legal Confirmation Required:* compliance responsibility runs to the operating company under section 4 of the Ship Safety and Security Act, not to a freight forwarder arranging carriage on a third-party vessel; whether a specific workspace engagement makes it the responsible "company" for a given voyage is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope and requires counsel review of the specific charter or booking structure.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The zero-emission requirement set out in section 10b applies to all passenger ships while they are within the World Heritage fjords, regardless of whether they operate exclusively within the fjords or only partially transit through them." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

*Per the workspace's reading:* this is the controlling scope statement for section 10b of the Environmental Safety Regulations; a vessel that only briefly transits a World Heritage fjord (rather than operating a full itinerary within it) is still covered.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "No exemption may extend beyond 31 December 2029, as the objective is for sufficient electricity infrastructure to be in place in the World Heritage fjords by that date." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

*Operational implication:* this is the hard backstop on every temporary exemption under Section 10c (Section 8, obligation 12); a workspace holding or planning to apply for such an exemption should treat 31 December 2029 as an absolute end date, not a renewable arrangement.

FACT: "Published 07 April 2023 Deadline 03 October 2023" *Source: NMA, Consultation - proposed implementation of zero emissions requirement in the World Heritage fjords by 2026. https://www.sdir.no/en/regelverk/hearings/consultation---proposed-implementation-of-zero-emissions-requirement-in-the-world-heritage-fjords-by-2026/

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the zero-emission requirement apply to a vessel that only transits part of a World Heritage fjord?**

FACT: "The zero-emission requirement set out in section 10b applies to all passenger ships while they are within the World Heritage fjords, regardless of whether they operate exclusively within the fjords or only partially transit through them." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

*Analytical inference:* yes; partial transit does not exempt a qualifying passenger ship.

**Q2: Can a small passenger vessel already operating in the fjords avoid the 2026 deadline entirely?**

FACT: "the exemption applies to established vessels that were operating in the World Heritage fjords in 2024 and intend to continue operating there until 2030." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this is a narrow, NMA-discretionary exemption (Section 8, obligation 12), capped at 31 December 2029 regardless of grant date; this is a case-by-case NMA determination, not an automatic entitlement.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Phased zero-emission effective dates by vessel size.** FACT: "The Norwegian Government has decided to introduce zero-emission requirements in the World Heritage fjords, effective from 1 January 2026 for passenger ships of less than 10,000 gross tonnage, and from 1 January 2032 for passenger ships of 10,000 gross tonnage and upwards." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

**2. Section 10b first and second paragraphs (the operative requirement text).** FACT: "The first paragraph of the provision stipulates that, from 1 January 2026, passenger ships of less than 10,000 gross tonnage operating in the World Heritage fjords shall use energy sources that do not result in direct emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2) or methane (CH4). According to the second paragraph, from 1 January 2032, passenger ships of 10,000 gross tonnage and upwards operating in the World Heritage fjords shall use energy sources that do not result in direct emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2) or methane (CH4)." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

**3. Passenger ship definition.** FACT: "A passenger ship is defined as a vessel that may carry more than 12 passengers." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

**4. Scope of application (regardless of transit type).** FACT: "The zero-emission requirement set out in section 10b applies to all passenger ships while they are within the World Heritage fjords, regardless of whether they operate exclusively within the fjords or only partially transit through them." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

**5. Shore power mandate.** FACT: "According to the seventh paragraph of the provision, passenger ships operating in the World Heritage fjords are required to use shore power where such facilities are available." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

**6. Biogas alternative-fuel pathway (final adopted rule).** FACT: "The Government has decided that all passenger ships may use biogas as an energy source, as an alternative to meeting the zero-emission requirements set out in the first and second paragraphs of section 10b. The use of biogas as an alternative energy source will also be permitted beyond 2032." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

FACT: "The proposal outlined a general rule mandating zero emissions, alongside a transitional arrangement permitting the use of biogas under specific conditions until the end of 2035." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025 (describing the NMA's own earlier proposal). https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this earlier proposal figure was superseded: the final adopted rule quoted above instead permits biogas beyond 2032 with no stated end date, subject to the sustainability criteria the circular separately describes -- this brief grounds only the final adopted text, not the superseded proposal figure.

**7. Company compliance responsibility.** FACT: "Although the requirements apply to individual ships, it is the company's responsibility to ensure compliance in accordance with section 4 of the Ship Safety and Security Act." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

**8. Enforcement mechanism and violation fines (penalty).** FACT: "The NMA may supervise compliance with the provision and, where necessary, implement administrative measures in accordance with chapter 8 of the Ship Safety and Security Act or impose violation fines pursuant to chapter 9." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

**9. Limitation of scope (vessel-type definition).** FACT: "Limitation of scope In both previous work and under the current mandate, the scope of the term "cruise ships, tourist boats and ferries" has been limited to passenger ships." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

**10. Exemption for roadworks and emergency situations.** FACT: "The Government has determined that there is a need for an exemption from the zero-emission requirements for passenger ships deployed in regular service due to planned roadworks or in response to emergency situations." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

**11. Exemption for county-operated high-speed craft.** FACT: "The Government has decided that county-operated high-speed craft shall be exempt from the zero- emission requirements." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

**12. Temporary exemption for the smaller-vessel tier, capped at 31 December 2029.** FACT: "No exemption may extend beyond 31 December 2029, as the objective is for sufficient electricity infrastructure to be in place in the World Heritage fjords by that date." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

**13. World Heritage fjords, named.** FACT: "The World Heritage Fjords include the five fjords: Nærøyfjorden, Aurlandsfjorden, Geirangerfjorden, Sunnylvsfjorden, and Tafjorden." *Source: Norwegian Government (regjeringen.no). https://www.regjeringen.no/en/whats-new/introducing-zero-emission-requirements-in-the-world-heritage-fjords/id3051481/

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: 2026 smaller-vessel threshold, 2029 exemption backstop, 2032 full-fleet threshold). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligations 10 and 11, the roadworks/emergency exemption and the county-operated high-speed craft exemption). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 9, the limitation of scope to passenger ships).

Obligations surveyed: 13; workspace-adjacent: 13; extracted as FACT: 13.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*Note: this framework's product-level distinction is vessel size (below vs at/above 10,000 gross tonnage, Section 8 obligations 1-2) and vessel type (passenger ship as defined in Section 8, obligation 3); no source in this brief's corpus states a further product-specific (e.g. cargo-type) compliance distinction within this regulation.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Although the requirements apply to individual ships, it is the company's responsibility to ensure compliance in accordance with section 4 of the Ship Safety and Security Act." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

*Operational implication:* no source in this brief's corpus states a separate registration or periodic reporting filing distinct from ordinary Ship Safety and Security Act compliance; the operating company's own responsibility to ensure and be able to demonstrate compliance (Section 8, obligation 7) is the closest analogue this corpus states.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

**1. Fleet-size compliance calendar.** FACT: "The Norwegian Government has decided to introduce zero-emission requirements in the World Heritage fjords, effective from 1 January 2026 for passenger ships of less than 10,000 gross tonnage, and from 1 January 2032 for passenger ships of 10,000 gross tonnage and upwards." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

**2. Shore power and biogas fuel-planning.** FACT: "According to the seventh paragraph of the provision, passenger ships operating in the World Heritage fjords are required to use shore power where such facilities are available." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

*Operational implication:* a workspace planning Norwegian fjord calls should maintain both an electrification/shore-power connection plan and a biogas-sourcing plan (Section 8, obligation 6) as parallel compliance pathways, since the regulation itself treats them as alternatives rather than a single mandated technology.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "The Government has determined that there is a need for an exemption from the zero-emission requirements for passenger ships deployed in regular service due to planned roadworks or in response to emergency situations." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

FACT: "The Government has decided that county-operated high-speed craft shall be exempt from the zero- emission requirements." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

FACT: "No exemption may extend beyond 31 December 2029, as the objective is for sufficient electricity infrastructure to be in place in the World Heritage fjords by that date." *Source: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025. https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf

*Analytical inference:* all three exemption pathways are narrow and either discretionary (Section 10c, case-by-case NMA assessment) or categorical but limited to a specific operator type (county-operated high-speed craft under public service contracts); a workspace should not assume a general commercial-hardship exemption exists.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "The World Heritage Fjords include the five fjords: Nærøyfjorden, Aurlandsfjorden, Geirangerfjorden, Sunnylvsfjorden, and Tafjorden." *Source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Norwegian parliament adopts zero-emission regulations in World Heritage fjords. https://whc.unesco.org/en/news/1824

*Analytical inference:* the UNESCO World Heritage Centre's own coverage of this adoption, and Lloyd's Register's classification-society guidance on the same requirements (https://www.lr.org/en/knowledge/class-news/03-26/), corroborate the requirement's substance from a heritage-conservation and classification perspective respectively, without adding new obligations beyond what Section 8 already states from the NMA's own circular.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- May 3, 2018: Storting Resolution No. 672 adopts a zero-emission requirement for World Heritage fjords by 2026.
- February 1, 2021: Storting Resolutions No. 690 and No. 691 adopted (emissions reduction measures; shore power in Flam and cruise calls beyond 2026).
- 07 April 2023: NMA public consultation on proposed regulations opens, with a deadline of 03 October 2023.
- September 30, 2024: Ministry of Climate and Environment confirms zero-emission requirements and finalises the phased schedule.
- April 14, 2025: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025 issued; the Environmental Safety Regulations are amended and the zero-emission requirements formally adopted.
- January 1, 2026: zero-emission requirement enters force for passenger ships below 10,000 gross tonnage.
- December 31, 2029: latest possible expiry date for any temporary exemption granted under Section 10c on shore-power-gap grounds.
- January 1, 2032: zero-emission requirement extends to passenger ships of 10,000 gross tonnage and upwards.

*Source for timeline entries: NMA Circular RSR 04-2025 (https://www.sdir.no/contentassets/ac4f83e167b749c3b3ffccbed0e730ff/eng-rsr-om-miljosikkerhetsforskriften-vaf.pdf); NMA news release (https://www.sdir.no/en/news/zero-emission-requirement-for-the-world-heritage-fjords-adopted/); Norwegian Government announcement (https://www.regjeringen.no/en/whats-new/introducing-zero-emission-requirements-in-the-world-heritage-fjords/id3051481/).*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This brief covers Directive (EU) 2023/959 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023, which amends Directive 2003/87/EC (the EU ETS Directive) and Decision (EU) 2015/1814 (the Market Stability Reserve Decision). It is structured as a Regulatory Fact Document under the regulatory_fact_document format.

**Convention notes:** The directive amends but does not replace the consolidated ETS Directive. References to articles are to the *amended* Directive 2003/87/EC as it stands post-2023 revision, not to standalone articles of Directive 2023/959 itself. The consolidated text as of 5 June 2023 is the operative instrument. All FACT citations draw from the primary source (id: 13f9585a-1f19-4b07-a0f7-df65ae0f5712) and corroborating sources as identified below.

**Workspace relevance filter:** This directive is analyzed through the lens of a freight forwarding operation whose transport mode priority is air primary, road secondary, ocean tertiary, and whose cargo verticals include live events, fine art, luxury goods, film and TV, high-value automotive, and humanitarian. The directive's maritime provisions are the highest-relevance stream for ocean-mode operations. The ETS2 (buildings, road transport, and additional sectors) stream is relevant to road-mode operations and fuel surcharge exposure. The aviation stream affects air-mode cost structure. The workspace's supply chain roles  -  freight forwarder, importer, customs broker  -  each carry distinct exposure profiles analyzed below.

**Dates:** This document is current as of the export date. The directive entered into force on 5 June 2023 (see Section 2). Source content was retrieved and grounded at generation time.

---

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

## Plain-Language Summary

FACT: Directive (EU) 2023/959 was adopted on "10 May 2023" and published in the Official Journal of the European Union on "16.5.2023" as OJ L 130/134. *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

FACT: Article 5 states "This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union," which places the entry-into-force date at **5 June 2023**. *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 5, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

The directive is the primary instrument of the EU's "Fit for 55" package as it applies to the EU ETS. Its structural changes span three distinct systems:

1. **EU ETS (ETS1)  -  existing cap-and-trade for power, industry, aviation:** Tighter cap trajectory, maritime sector inclusion from 2024, CBAM interaction with free allocation, strengthened Market Stability Reserve.
2. **ETS2  -  new cap-and-trade for buildings, road transport, and additional sectors:** Separate system, upstream point of regulation (fuel distributors, not end-users), operational from 2028 following a one-year postponement.
3. **Market Stability Reserve amendments:** Higher intake rates, revised invalidation threshold, new ETS2-specific reserve section.

FACT: The directive's stated objective is achieving "a reduction in the emissions of the sectors covered by the EU ETS of 62 % compared to 2005" by 2030. *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, recital (39), EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

## Why It Applies to the Workspace

The workspace operates as a freight forwarder arranging ocean freight, air freight, and road freight on behalf of clients. Three channels of exposure exist:

**Channel 1  -  Ocean freight cost pass-through:** The directive extends EU ETS allowance surrender obligations to shipping companies operating vessels at or above the directive's own gross-tonnage threshold (see Section 7, Q1, for the FAQ's stated figure). Ocean carriers serving trade lanes used by the workspace (Americas, Europe, Asia) are covered entities. Those carriers pass allowance costs through freight rates and surcharges to shippers, including freight forwarders and their clients.

**Channel 2  -  Air freight cost exposure:** The directive tightens the aviation cap and phases out free allocation for aircraft operators by 2026. Airlines pass ETS allowance costs into fuel surcharges and freight rates on intra-EEA and mixed routes.

**Channel 3  -  Road freight cost exposure (ETS2):** ETS2 covers fuel distributors supplying road transport fuel. Fuel cost increases flow into road freight rates, affecting drayage, line-haul, and last-mile costs for cargo verticals including live events, luxury goods, and high-value automotive.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, in any transaction where it acts as importer of record or shipper of record, bears a direct ETS compliance obligation (rather than a cost passed through by a carrier) depends on the specific contractual and regulatory classification of its role in each transaction. This is a legal determination requiring counsel review.

---

FACT (verbatim, complete): "This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959 / corroborating capture, EUR-Lex or corroborating source, 16 May 2023 (or as dated in the capture). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

FACT (verbatim, complete): "16.5.2023 EN Official Journal of the European Union L 130/134 DIRECTIVE (EU) 2023/959 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 10 May 2023" *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959 / corroborating capture, EUR-Lex or corroborating source, 16 May 2023 (or as dated in the capture). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

FACT (verbatim, complete): "This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959 / corroborating capture, EUR-Lex or corroborating source, 16 May 2023 (or as dated in the capture). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

FACT (verbatim, complete): "a reduction in the emissions of the sectors covered by the EU ETS of 62 % compared to 2005" *Source: corroborating capture (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng).

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

### COST ALERT  -  Maritime ETS Surcharge Exposure Is Financially Active Now

The first maritime ETS surrender deadline covering 2024 emissions was **30 September 2025**. That deadline has passed. Shipping companies surrendered allowances equal to 40% of verified 2024 CO₂ emissions by that date. The 2025 compliance cycle (70% of 2025 emissions) has a surrender deadline of **30 September 2026**  -  which is within the current operating window.

**Action:** For every ocean shipment on EU-connected trade lanes (Americas-Europe, Asia-Europe, intra-Europe), the workspace should confirm that ocean carrier surcharge invoices explicitly identify the ETS component, and that the workspace's client contracts contain appropriate carbon cost pass-through or disclosure clauses. Failure to have this language in place means ETS cost is absorbed in margin rather than recovered.

**Cargo vertical filter:** High-value automotive, live events (equipment), and film and TV production freight carried by ocean on Europe routes are fully exposed. Fine art and luxury goods shipped by ocean (even if air is primary mode) on any EU port-to-EU port leg face 100% allowance coverage on that leg.

### ACTION REQUIRED  -  ETS2 Transposition and Monitoring Obligations Are in Force

FACT: Article 3(1) of Directive 2023/959 required Member States to "bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with Article 1 of this Directive by 31 December 2023" for ETS1 maritime and aviation provisions, with provisions for ETS2 regulated entities and monitoring plans due by "30 June 2024." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 3(1), EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

FACT: Article 30f(2) states "Member States shall ensure that each regulated entity monitors for each calendar year from 2025 the emissions corresponding to the quantities of fuels released for consumption pursuant to Annex III." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 30f(2) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

## Maritime Compliance Chain

FACT: The directive defines "shipping company" as "the shipowner or any other organisation or person, such as the manager or the bareboat charterer, that has assumed the responsibility for the operation of the ship from the shipowner and that, on assuming such responsibility, has agreed to take over all the duties and responsibilities imposed by the International Management Code for the Safe Operation of Ships and for Pollution Prevention." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 1(3)(d)(w) inserting definition into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, in any capacity (freight forwarder, NVOCC, or otherwise), meets the definition of "shipping company" under this article in any transaction requires counsel review of each operational arrangement. A freight forwarder that does not operate or manage vessels does not on its face meet this definition, but any NVO or vessel-operating arrangement would require specific legal analysis.

FACT: Article 3gc provides that "when the ultimate responsibility for the purchase of the fuel, or the operation of the ship, or both, is assumed by an entity other than the shipping company pursuant to a contractual arrangement, the shipping company is entitled to reimbursement from that entity for the costs arising from the surrender of allowances." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 3gc as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether any contractual arrangements the workspace holds with shipping companies constitute "assuming responsibility for the operation of the ship" such that the shipping company could seek reimbursement from the workspace requires counsel review of specific contract terms.

Operational implication: For the workspace acting as a shipper or cargo owner (not vessel operator), the ETS cost flows from shipping company → freight rate or surcharge → workspace → client. The workspace's position is as a cost recipient and potential pass-through entity, not a direct compliance obligor.

## Aviation Compliance Chain

Aircraft operators are the compliance entities for aviation ETS. The workspace, as a freight forwarder purchasing cargo space, is exposed through rate structures. No direct surrender obligation attaches to freight forwarders in the aviation stream.

## ETS2 Road Transport Compliance Chain

FACT: The directive defines "regulated entity" for ETS2 purposes as "any natural or legal person, except for any final consumer of the fuels, that engages in the activity referred to in Annex III"  -  that activity being "Release for consumption of fuels which are used for combustion in the buildings, road transport and additional sectors." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 3(ae) inserting definition into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

FACT: The regulated entity categories are aligned with excise duty liability under Council Directive (EU) 2020/262, specifically: "(i) where the fuel passes through a tax warehouse as defined in Article 3, point (11), of Council Directive (EU) 2020/262, the authorised warehousekeeper…; (ii) if point (i) of this point is not applicable, any other person liable to pay the excise duty…; (iii) if points (i) and (ii) of this point are not applicable, any other person that has to be registered by the relevant competent authorities of the Member State for the purpose of being liable to pay the excise duty." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 3(ae)(i)-(iii) inserting definition into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, as a freight forwarder, is or could become an ETS2 "regulated entity" under any of these categories in any Member State requires counsel review. The point of regulation is upstream (fuel distributors), and freight forwarders are not ordinarily fuel distributors, but arrangements in specific jurisdictions or specific operational models could create exposure.

Operational implication: For road freight operations (drayage to ports, cross-border road freight in Europe), ETS2 cost will be passed through by trucking operators into rates from 2028. The workspace should build ETS2 cost escalation into multi-year European road freight contracts.

# 7. Threshold Questions

### Q1: Which ships are covered by ETS maritime obligations?

FACT: The directive inserts the following into Annex I of Directive 2003/87/EC as the maritime row: "Maritime transport activities covered by Regulation (EU) 2015/757 with the exception of the maritime transport activities covered by Article 2(1a) and, until 31 December 2026, Article 2(1b) of that Regulation." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Annex (1)(c)(ix) amending Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

FACT: The FAQ confirms: "Since 2024: cargo and passenger ships of or above 5000 gross tonnage (GT); From 2027: offshore ships of or above 5000 GT." *Source: FAQ  -  Maritime transport in EU ETS, European Commission Climate Action, updated 02/04/2025. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-shipping-sector/faq-maritime-transport-eu-emissions-trading-system-ets_en.

**Decided:** Vessels below 5000 GT are outside scope until at least the 2026 Commission report and any subsequent legislative action. The workspace can treat feeder vessels below this threshold as outside current ETS compliance scope, with the caveat that this may change post-2028.

### Q2: Which greenhouse gases are covered for maritime?

FACT: The maritime Annex I entry specifies "Carbon dioxide" initially, and the directive provides: "From 1 January 2026 and 1 January 2027 respectively, the quantity of allowances shall be increased to take into account the coverage of greenhouse gas emissions other than CO₂ emissions from maritime transport activities and the coverage of emissions of offshore ships." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 1(11) inserting paragraphs into Article 9 of Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Decided:** CO₂ from 2024; methane (CH₄) and nitrous oxide (N₂O) added to ETS scope from 2026 (monitoring of CH₄ and N₂O began in 2024 under the MRV regulation). For LNG-powered vessels used by carriers on Europe routes, the methane slip factor becomes commercially significant from 2026.

### Q3: Is the ice-class derogation relevant to carriers serving Arctic/Nordic routes used by workspace clients?

FACT: Article 12(3-e) of the amended directive provides: "By way of derogation from paragraph 3, first subparagraph, point (c), shipping companies may surrender 5 % fewer allowances than their verified emissions released until 31 December 2030 from ice-class ships, provided that such ships have the ice class IA or IA Super or an equivalent ice class, established based on HELCOM Recommendation 25/7." FACT (qualification): "Where fewer allowances are surrendered compared to the verified emissions, once the difference between verified emissions and allowances surrendered has been established in respect of each year, an amount of allowances corresponding to that difference shall be cancelled rather than auctioned." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 1(21)(d) inserting Article 12(3-e) into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Decided:** Carriers operating ice-class vessels on Nordic or Baltic routes can surrender 5% fewer allowances until 31 December 2030. For the workspace, this is a minor carrier-side cost reduction that may marginally affect surcharge calculations on those routes.

### Q4: Does the outermost region derogation affect any routes relevant to the workspace?

FACT: Article 12(3-b) states: "An obligation to surrender allowances shall not arise in respect of emissions released until 31 December 2030 from voyages between a port located in an outermost region of a Member State and a port located in the same Member State, including voyages between ports within an outermost region and voyages between ports in the outermost regions of the same Member State." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 1(21)(d) inserting Article 12(3-b) into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

Analytical inference: For workspaces moving cargo to/from Canary Islands, Madeira, Azores, French overseas territories, or other outermost regions of EU Member States, voyages between those ports and mainland ports of the same Member State are exempt from ETS through 2030. This is a routing cost factor for clients with operations in those regions.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

## A. Maritime ETS  -  Scope of Coverage (Article 3ga)

FACT: The directive specifies the following coverage fractions for maritime ETS allowance surrender:
- "fifty percent (50 %) of the emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call outside the jurisdiction of a Member State"
- "fifty percent (50 %) of the emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call outside the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State"
- "one hundred percent (100 %) of emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State"
- "one hundred percent (100 %) of emissions from ships within a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State"

*Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 3ga(1) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Qualification  -  neighboring container transhipment ports:** FACT: The directive provides that the Commission shall "by 31 December 2023, by means of implementing acts establish a list of neighbouring container transhipment ports" and update it "by 31 December every two years thereafter." A port qualifies if "the share of transhipment of containers… exceeds 65 % of the total container traffic of that port during the most recent twelve-month period" AND "that port is located outside the Union but less than 300 nautical miles from a port under the jurisdiction of a Member State." The list "shall not include ports located in a third country for which that third country effectively applies measures equivalent to this Directive." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 3ga(2) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

Industry interpretation (Sustainable Ships): The Commission adopted an Implementing Regulation on 26 October 2023 identifying Tanger Med (Morocco) and East Port Said (Egypt) as 'neighbouring container transhipment ports'. This act is to be revised every two years. *Source: Sustainable Ships EU ETS Maritime page, undated (current). https://www.sustainable-ships.org/rules-regulations/eu-ets. This is an industry secondary source cited for operational context.

**Effect on workspace cargo verticals:** For containers routed through Tanger Med or East Port Said as transhipment hubs before entering EU ports, stops at those ports are excluded from voyage start/end calculations. This reduces ETS exposure for certain Asia-Europe container flows. For the workspace's live events and film/TV equipment cargo moving in full container loads on hub-and-spoke routes, this is a routing cost factor worth confirming with ocean carriers.

## B. Phase-In Schedule (Article 3gb)

FACT: "Shipping companies shall be liable to surrender allowances according to the following schedule:
(a) 40 % of verified emissions reported for 2024 that would be subject to surrender requirements in accordance with Article 12;
(b) 70 % of verified emissions reported for 2025 that would be subject to surrender requirements in accordance with Article 12;
(c) 100 % of verified emissions reported for 2026 and each year thereafter in accordance with Article 12."

**Qualification  -  cancellation during phase-in:** FACT: "Where fewer allowances are surrendered compared to the verified emissions from maritime transport for the years 2024 and 2025, once the difference between verified emissions and allowances surrendered has been established in respect of each year, an amount of allowances corresponding to that difference shall be cancelled rather than auctioned pursuant to Article 10." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 3gb as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

Operational implication: From 2026, 100% of verified emissions on covered routes are subject to allowance surrender. The cost step-up from 70% (2025) to 100% (2026) is a material year-over-year increase in surrender obligation, and this should be modeled into freight budget planning for the remainder of 2026.

## C. Surrender Deadline and Compliance Cycle

FACT: Article 12(3) of the amended directive states: "The Member States, administering Member States and administering authorities in respect of a shipping company shall ensure that, by 30 September each year: … (c) each shipping company surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to its total emissions during the preceding calendar year." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 1(21)(c) replacing Article 12(3) of Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Qualification  -  stationary installations deadline change:** The same article moved the stationary installation surrender deadline from 30 April to 30 September (Article 16(3) amendment). This affects industrial clients but not the workspace's core freight operations.

## D. Penalty Provisions (Article 16)

FACT: Article 16 paragraph 3 of the amended directive applies a penalty of €100 per tonne of CO₂ equivalent for which no allowance has been surrendered. Article 1(23)(c) of Directive 2023/959 inserts paragraph 3a: "The penalties set out in paragraph 3 shall also apply in respect of shipping companies." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 1(23)(c)-(d) amending Article 16 of Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

FACT: The FAQ confirms: "heavy fines are imposed" for non-compliance: "if a company emits 10,000 tonnes of CO₂ falling within the scope of the EU ETS Directive during a reporting period, that company needs to buy and surrender 10,000 allowances by 30 September of the following year." *Source: FAQ  -  Maritime transport in EU ETS, European Commission Climate Action, updated 02/04/2025. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-shipping-sector/faq-maritime-transport-eu-emissions-trading-system-ets_en.

**Escalation provision  -  expulsion order:** FACT: "In the case of a shipping company that has failed to comply with the surrender obligations for two or more consecutive reporting periods, and where other enforcement measures have failed to ensure compliance, the competent authority of the Member State of the port of entry may… issue an expulsion order… every Member State, with the exception of the Member State whose flag the ship is flying, shall refuse entry of the ships under the responsibility of the shipping company concerned into any of its ports until the shipping company fulfils its surrender obligations." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 1(23)(d) inserting Article 16(11a) into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

Operational implication: For cargo verticals requiring time-critical delivery (live events equipment, humanitarian supplies), a carrier subject to an expulsion order could result in cargo being stranded. The workspace should confirm, for high-value or time-sensitive ocean shipments, that carriers have active ETS compliance accounts and no outstanding enforcement actions.

## E. Cap Trajectory  -  ETS1 (Article 9 amendments)

FACT: The directive amends Article 9 of Directive 2003/87/EC as follows: "In 2024, the Union-wide quantity of allowances shall be decreased by 90 million allowances. In 2026, the Union-wide quantity of allowances shall be decreased by 27 million allowances. In 2024, the Union-wide quantity of allowances shall be increased by 78,4 million allowances for maritime transport. The linear factor shall be 4,3 % from 2024 to 2027 and 4,4 % from 2028." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 1(11) inserting paragraphs into Article 9 of Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

FACT: The Commission confirmed the 2024 cap: "The Commission informed that the EU ETS cap for 2024 amounts to 1,386,051,745 allowances." *Source: EU ETS Emissions Cap page, European Commission Climate Action, undated (current). https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/carbon-markets/eu-emissions-trading-system-eu-ets/eu-ets-emissions-cap_en.

FACT: *Industry interpretation:* ICAP confirms the 2026 cap: "the cap in 2026 is determined to be 1,185 MtCO₂e" for installations. *Source: EU ETS factsheet, ICAP, 2025/2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/eu-emissions-trading-system-eu-ets.

Operational implication: A tighter cap means higher allowance scarcity and directionally higher ETS prices over time, increasing the cost pass-through to shippers across all transport modes.

## F. CBAM Free Allocation Phase-Out Schedule

FACT: The full CBAM factor schedule as enacted is: "100 % for the period between the entry into force of that Regulation and the end of 2025; 97,5 % in 2026; 95 % in 2027; 90 % in 2028; 77,5 % in 2029; 51,5 % in 2030; 39 % in 2031; 26,5 % in 2032; 14 % in 2033. From 2034, no CBAM factor shall apply." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 10a(1a) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Qualification on calculation basis:** FACT: "The reduction of free allocation shall be calculated annually as the average share of the demand for free allocation for the production of goods listed in Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2023/956 compared to the calculated total free allocation demand for all installations, for the relevant period referred to in Article 11(1) of this Directive." The reduction is calculated on a sector-average, annual basis, not per individual installation's output. *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 10a(1a) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

## G. Free Allocation Conditionality (Article 10a  -  Energy Audit Requirement)

FACT: The directive inserts the following conditionality into free allocation for stationary installations: "If an installation is covered by the obligation to conduct an energy audit or to implement a certified energy management system under Article 8 of Directive 2012/27/EU… and if the recommendations of the audit report or of the certified energy management system are not implemented, unless the pay-back time for the relevant investments exceeds three years or unless the costs of those investments are disproportionate, then the amount of free allocation shall be reduced by 20 %." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 10a(1) as amended in Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Qualification:** FACT: "The amount of free allocation shall not be reduced if an operator demonstrates that it has implemented other measures which lead to greenhouse gas emission reductions equivalent to those recommended by the audit report or by the certified energy management system for the installation concerned." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 10a(1) as amended, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

Operational implication: For clients operating EU manufacturing facilities in CBAM-relevant sectors, failure to implement energy audit recommendations triggers a 20% free allocation reduction. This increases their ETS cost burden, which can feed through to input material costs for automotive or other manufactured goods the workspace ships.

## H. ETS2  -  Buildings, Road Transport, and Additional Sectors

**Scope:** FACT: Annex III (inserted by the directive) covers "Release for consumption of fuels which are used for combustion in the buildings, road transport and additional sectors." The exclusions are explicit: "(a) the release for consumption of fuels used in the activities listed in Annex I [ETS1 activities]… (b) the release for consumption of fuels for which the emission factor is zero; (c) the release for consumption of hazardous or municipal waste used as fuel." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Annex (3) inserting Annex III into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Compliance start:** FACT: Article 30e(2) states "From 1 January 2028, Member States shall ensure that, by 31 May each year, the regulated entity surrenders an amount of allowances covered by this Chapter that is equal to the regulated entity's total emissions." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 30e(2) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng. (Note: ICAP confirms start was postponed to 2028 by March 2026 Council/Parliament decision.)

**Linear reduction factor:** FACT: "the linear reduction factor should be set at 5,10 %" for 2024-2027 trajectory. From 2028, "the linear reduction factor of 5,38 %." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, recital (80), EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Price ceiling mechanism:** FACT: "Where the average price of allowances referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article exceeds a price of EUR 45 for a period of two consecutive months, 20 million allowances covered by this Chapter shall be released from the market stability reserve in accordance with Article 1a(7) of Decision (EU) 2015/1814. Indexation based on the European index of consumer prices for 2020 shall apply. Allowances shall be released through the mechanism provided for in this paragraph up to 31 December 2029." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 30h(2) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Postponement trigger:** FACT: The directive provides that if "the average TTF gas price for the six calendar months ending 30 June 2026 was higher than the average TTF gas price in February and March 2022" OR "the average Brent crude oil price for the six calendar months ending 30 June 2026 was more than twice the average Brent crude oil price during the five preceding years," the system is delayed by one year (to 2028 in the original text; effectively further delayed now that March 2026 postponement has already been enacted). *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 30k(1) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**ETS2 penalty:** FACT (ICAP): "Covered entities must pay an excess emissions penalty of EUR 100 (USD 113), adjusted for inflation with 2013 as the base year, for each tCO₂ emitted for which no allowance has been surrendered." *Source: EU ETS 2 factsheet, ICAP, 2025/2026. https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/ets/eu-emissions-trading-system-buildings-and-road-transport-eu-ets-2.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

## For the Workspace as Freight Forwarder (Cost Monitoring and Contract Infrastructure)

**Maritime ETS cost tracking system:**
- **What to build:** A per-shipment ETS cost attribution capability that maps ocean freight invoices to their ETS surcharge components, segregated by route type (intra-EU = 100%, mixed = 50%).
- **Gap from current baseline:** If the workspace currently does not separate ETS surcharges from base freight in its cost accounting, this gap means ETS cost cannot be accurately reported to clients or modeled for contract pricing.
- **Deadline:** Immediate  -  2026 compliance year (100% surrender) is underway.
- **Scope:** All ocean freight on EU-port-touching routes across Americas, Europe, and Asia trade lanes.

**Contract clause review:**
- **What to build:** A standard ETS cost pass-through clause for client service agreements covering ocean freight, reviewed against applicable law in the governing jurisdiction.
- **Gap:** Absent an explicit clause, ETS cost increases that arise mid-contract are absorbed in margin.
- **Deadline:** Apply to all new contracts and renewal events. Retroactive clauses are subject to negotiation.
- *Legal Confirmation Required:* Clause language should be reviewed by counsel familiar with the law of the contract's governing jurisdiction, including whether English law (common for shipping contracts) or EU Member State law applies.

**Aviation ETS monitoring:**
- **What to build:** Rate monitoring process that tracks air freight rate changes attributable to the complete removal of aviation free allocation from 2026, specifically on intra-EEA routes and routes involving EU hub airports.
- **Cargo vertical priority:** Air primary mode  -  live events, fine art, humanitarian, luxury goods, film and TV.
- **Deadline:** 2026 rate review cycle.

**ETS2 road freight modeling:**
- **What to build:** Forecast model for European road freight rate escalation attributable to ETS2 fuel cost pass-through from 2028 onward.
- **Deadline:** Build by end of 2026; apply to multi-year European road freight contracts from 2027.

**Carrier compliance verification protocol:**
- **What to build:** A due diligence step for ocean carrier selection confirming active ETS monitoring plan approval, no outstanding surrender failures, and no expulsion order status.
- **Rationale:** An expulsion-ordered carrier cannot call EU ports; the workspace's cargo would be disrupted. This risk is acute for live events and humanitarian cargo with hard delivery deadlines.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

## Outermost Region Exemption

FACT: "An obligation to surrender allowances shall not arise in respect of emissions released until 31 December 2030 from voyages between a port located in an outermost region of a Member State and a port located in the same Member State, including voyages between ports within an outermost region and voyages between ports in the outermost regions of the same Member State, and from the activities, within a port, of such ships in relation to such voyages." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 12(3-b) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Scope of this exemption:** The Canary Islands, Madeira, Azores, Guadeloupe, Martinique, French Guiana, Réunion, Mayotte, and Saint-Martin qualify as outermost regions. Voyages between these ports and mainland ports of the same Member State (e.g., Lanzarote-Valencia, Guadeloupe-Marseille) are exempt from ETS through 2030. Voyages from these regions to another EU Member State's ports are not exempt on this basis.

## Small Island Exemption

FACT: Article 12(3-d) allows Member States to request that emissions from passenger ships and ro-pax ships between "a port of an island under the jurisdiction of that requesting Member State, with no road or rail link with the mainland and with a population of fewer than 200 000 permanent residents" be exempted from surrender obligations "until 31 December 2030." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 12(3-d) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

**Qualification:** This exemption applies only to "passenger ships, other than cruise passenger ships, and by ro-pax ships" on these specific routes. General cargo vessels are not covered by this derogation.

## ETS2  -  National Carbon Tax Derogation

FACT: Article 30e(3) provides that "until 31 December 2030, by way of derogation from paragraphs 1 and 2… where a regulated entity established in a given Member State is subject to a national carbon tax in force for the years 2027 to 2030, covering the activity referred to in Annex III, the competent authority of the Member State concerned may exempt that regulated entity from the obligation to surrender allowances… provided that: (a) the Member State concerned notifies the Commission of that national carbon tax by 31 December 2023, and the national law setting the tax rates applicable for the years 2027 to 2030 has, by that date, entered into force; (b) for the reference year, the national carbon tax of the Member State concerned effectively paid by that regulated entity is higher than the average auction clearing price of the emissions trading system established under this Chapter." *Source: Directive (EU) 2023/959, Article 30e(3) as inserted into Directive 2003/87/EC, EUR-Lex, 16 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/959/oj/eng.

Analytical inference: In Member States with pre-existing carbon taxes on road fuel (e.g., Austria, Germany, which had national carbon pricing systems), regulated entities may be exempt from ETS2 surrender obligations if the national tax is higher than the ETS2 clearing price. This creates a complex multi-jurisdiction cost environment for cross-border European road freight. The workspace should confirm with European road freight partners which regulatory regime applies in each Member State where fuel is released for consumption.

claims.source_span: Member States shall ensure that each regulated entity monitors for each calendar year from 2025 the emissions corresponding to the quantities of fuels released for consumption pursuant to Annex III. They shall also ensure that each regulated entity reports those emissions to the competent authority in the following year, starting in 2026, in accordance with the implementing acts referred to in Article 14(1).

claims.source_span: This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .

claims.claim_text: The maritime Annex I entry specifies "Carbon dioxide" initially, and the directive provides: "From 1 January 2026 and 1 January 2027 respectively, the quantity of allowances shall be increased to take into account the coverage of greenhouse gas emissions other than CO₂ emissions from maritime transport activities and the coverage of emissions of offshore ships."
claims.source_span: From 1 January 2026 and 1 January 2027 respectively, the quantity of allowances shall be increased to take into account the coverage of greenhouse gas emissions other than CO 2 emissions from maritime transport activities and the coverage of emissions of offshore ships

claims.claim_text: [jurisdictional_scope] The directive inserts the following into Annex I of Directive 2003/87/EC as the maritime row: "Maritime transport activities covered by Regulation (EU) 2015/757 with the exception of the maritime transport activities covered by Article 2(1a) and, until 31 December 2026, Article 2(1b) of that Regulation."
claims.source_span: Maritime transport activities covered by Regulation (EU) 2015/757 with the exception of the maritime transport activities covered by Article 2(1a) and, until 31 December 2026, Article 2(1b) of that Regulation

claims.claim_text: [effective_date] Directive (EU) 2023/959 was adopted on "10 May 2023" and published in the Official Journal of the European Union on "16.5.2023" as OJ L 130/134.
claims.source_span: 16.5.2023 EN Official Journal of the European Union L 130/134 DIRECTIVE (EU) 2023/959 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 10 May 2023

claims.claim_text: "For voyages starting and ending in two different calendar years, the respective data must be accounted under each reporting period."
claims.source_span: for voyages starting and ending in two different calendar years, the respective data must be accounted under each reporting period.

claims.claim_text: From the EU ETS cap description, "free allocation for aircraft operators will be phased out from 2026."
claims.source_span: As a result, free allocation for aircraft operators will be phased out from 2026.

claims.claim_text: Article 30e(3) provides that "until 31 December 2030, by way of derogation from paragraphs 1 and 2… where a regulated entity established in a given Member State is subject to a national carbon tax in force for the years 2027 to 2030, covering the activity referred to in Annex III, the competent authority of the Member State concerned may exempt that regulated entity from the obligation to surrender allowances… provided that: (a) the Member State concerned notifies the Commission of that national carbon tax by 31 December 2023, and the national law setting the tax rates applicable for the years 2027 to 2030 has, by that date, entered into force; (b) for the reference year, the national carbon tax of the Member State concerned effectively paid by that regulated entity is higher than the average auction clearing price of the emissions trading system established under this Chapter."
claims.source_span: Until 31 December 2030, by way of derogation from paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article, where a regulated entity established in a given Member State is subject to a national carbon tax in force for the years 2027 to 2030, covering the activity referred to in Annex III, the competent authority of the Member State concerned may exempt that regulated entity from the obligation to surrender allowances under paragraph 2 of this Article for a given reference year, provided that: (a) the Member State concerned notifies the Commission of that national carbon tax by 31 December 2023, and the national law setting the tax rates applicable for the years 2027 to 2030 has, by that date, entered into force; the Member State concerned shall notify the Commission of any subsequent change to the national carbon tax; (b) for the reference year, the national carbon tax of the Member State concerned effectively paid by that regulated entity is higher than the average auction clearing price of the emissions trading system established under this Chapter

claims.claim_text: [primary_deadline] Article 12(3) of the amended directive states: "The Member States, administering Member States and administering authorities in respect of a shipping company shall ensure that, by 30 September each year: … (c) each shipping company surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to its total emissions during the preceding calendar year."
claims.source_span: 3. The Member States, administering Member States and administering authorities in respect of a shipping company shall ensure that, by 30 September each year: (a) the operator of each installation surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to the total emissions from that installation during the preceding calendar year, as verified in accordance with Article 15; (b) each aircraft operator surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to its total emissions during the preceding calendar year, as verified in accordance with Article 15; (c) each shipping company surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to its total emissions during the preceding calendar year, as verified in accordance with Article 3ge.

claims.claim_text: [penalty_summary] Article 1(23)(c) of Directive 2023/959 inserts paragraph 3a: "3a. The penalties set out in paragraph 3 shall also apply in respect of shipping companies."
claims.source_span: 3a. The penalties set out in paragraph 3 shall also apply in respect of shipping companies.

claims.claim_text: The directive requires the Commission to present a report "no later than 31 December 2026" on "the feasibility and economic, environmental and social impacts of the inclusion in this Directive of emissions from ships, including offshore ships, below 5 000 gross tonnage but not below 400 gross tonnage."
claims.source_span: No later than 31 December 2026, the Commission shall present a report to the European Parliament and to the Council in which it shall examine the feasibility and economic, environmental and social impacts of the inclusion in this Directive of emissions from ships, including offshore ships, below 5 000 gross tonnage but not below 400 gross tonnage

claims.claim_text: [penalty_summary] The FAQ confirms: "heavy fines are imposed" for non-compliance: "if a company emits 10,000 tonnes of CO₂ falling within the scope of the EU ETS Directive during a reporting period, that company needs to buy and surrender 10,000 allowances by 30 September of the following year."
claims.source_span: if a company emits 10,000 tonnes of CO 2 falling within the scope of the EU ETS Directive during a reporting period, that company needs to buy and surrender 10,000 allowances by 30 September of the following year.

claims.claim_text: "Carbon credits or certificates cannot be used for EU ETS compliance purposes."
claims.source_span: Carbon credits or certificates cannot be used for EU ETS compliance purposes.

claims.claim_text: [penalty_summary] "In the case of a shipping company that has failed to comply with the surrender obligations for two or more consecutive reporting periods, and where other enforcement measures have failed to ensure compliance, the competent authority of the Member State of the port of entry may… issue an expulsion order… every Member State, with the exception of the Member State whose flag the ship is flying, shall refuse entry of the ships under the responsibility of the shipping company concerned into any of its ports until the shipping company fulfils its surrender obligations."
claims.source_span: In the case of a shipping company that has failed to comply with the surrender obligations for two or more consecutive reporting periods, and where other enforcement measures have failed to ensure compliance, the competent authority of the Member State of the port of entry may, after giving the opportunity to the shipping company concerned to submit its observations, issue an expulsion order, which shall be notified to the Commission, the European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA), the other Member States and the flag State concerned.
