# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

### Information System registration

The EUDR Information System must provide "registration of operators and traders and their authorised representatives in the Union; for operators placing relevant products under the customs procedure 'release for free circulation' or 'export', the Economic Operators Registration and Identification (EORI) number established pursuant to Article 9 of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013, shall be included in their registration profile." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 33(2)(a), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

*Operational implication:* Workspaces that import or export relevant products for free circulation must have their EORI number linked to their Information System registration. This is a precondition for submitting due diligence statements.

Under Regulation 2025/2650: "Downstream operators and traders 'other than SMEs' will not have to file returns but will need to register in the Information System." *Source: European Commission Access2Markets, "Delay until December 2026," European Commission, 28 January 2026. https://trade.ec.europa.eu/access-to-markets/en/news/delay-until-december-2026-and-other-developments-implementation-eudr-regulation

### Annual public reporting (non-SME operators, Article 12(3))

"Operators who do not fall within the categories of SMEs, including microenterprises, or natural persons shall, on an annual basis, publicly report as widely as possible, including via the internet, on their due diligence system, including on the steps taken by them to fulfil their obligations as set out in Article 8." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 12(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

The report must include: a summary of the Article 9(1)(a) to (c) information (description, quantity, country of production); conclusions of the risk assessment and mitigation measures; and "where applicable, a description of the process of consultation of indigenous peoples, local communities and other customary tenure rights holders or of the civil society organisations that are present in the area of production." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 12(4), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

"Operators who fall also within the scope of other Union legal acts that lay down requirements regarding value chain due diligence may fulfil their reporting obligations under this paragraph by including the required information when reporting in the context of those other Union legal acts." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 12(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 *Operational implication:* Workspaces already reporting under CSRD or CSDDD may be able to consolidate EUDR reporting into those existing frameworks, reducing duplication.

### Member State competent authority reporting

Member States must designate competent authorities by 30 December 2023. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 14(2), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 The Commission publishes the list of designated competent authorities. *Source: European Commission DG Environment, "Regulation on Deforestation-free Products," European Commission. https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/forests/deforestation/regulation-deforestation-free-products_en

### Customs reference number requirement

"The reference number of the due diligence statement shall be made available to customs authorities before the release for free circulation or export of a relevant product entering or leaving the market." Except where the due diligence statement is made available through the electronic interface referred to in Article 28(2), "the person lodging the customs declaration for release for free circulation or export of a relevant product shall make available to customs authorities the reference number of the due diligence statement assigned to that relevant product by the information system." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 26(4), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

*Operational implication:* For workspaces lodging customs declarations (as customs broker or importer of record) for relevant products, having the DDS reference number available at the time of customs declaration submission is a procedural prerequisite.

### Record retention periods

- Due diligence statements: five years from the date of submission. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 4(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115
- Article 9 information: five years from the date of placing on the market or export. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 9(1), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115
- Due diligence documentation (measures and procedures): at least five years. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 12(5), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115
- SME trader records: at least five years. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 5(4), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115
- Competent authority check records: at least 10 years. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 16(14), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**Additional grounded provisions:**
- FACT: "By 30 December 2023 at the latest, Member States shall inform the Commission of the names, addresses and contact details of the competent authorities referred to in paragraph 1." *Source: EUDR corpus capture, https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32023R1115*
- FACT: "SME traders shall keep the information referred to in paragraph 3 for at least five years from the date of the making available on the market and shall provide that information to the competent authorities upon request." *Source: EUDR corpus capture, https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32023R1115*
- FACT: "Technical and other assistance and guidance shall take into account the situation of SMEs, including microenterprises, and natural persons, in order to facilitate compliance with this Regulation, including as regards the conversion of data from relevant systems to identify the geolocation in the information system as referred to in Article 33." *Source: EUDR corpus capture, https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32023R1115*
- FACT: "SME traders shall collect and keep the following information relating to the relevant products they intend to make available on the market: (a) the name, registered trade name or registered trade mark, the postal address, the email address and, if available, a web address of the operators or the traders who have supplied the relevant products to them, as well as the reference numbers of the due diligence statements associated to those products; (b) the name, registered trade name or registered trade mark, the postal address, the email address and, if available, a web address of the operators or the traders to whom they have supplied the relevant products." *Source: EUDR corpus capture, https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32023R1115*


# 11. Operational System Requirements

### 1: Information System access and integration

**Scope:** All entities that will submit due diligence statements (operators) or reference numbers (downstream operators and traders) must register in the EUDR Information System.
**Deadline:** Before 30 December 2026 (large/medium operators, downstream operators, traders); before 30 June 2027 (micro/small operators for non-EUTR products; natural persons).
**Gap from current operational baseline:** *Operational implication:* Workspaces without an existing EUDR Information System registration and without an integrated API connection to that system face a registration and IT-integration gap. The Commission plans to relaunch the IS in June 2026 with updated APIs; system integration planning should await the June 2026 API release to avoid rework.

### 2: Geolocation data collection and management

**Scope:** Operators must collect and maintain geolocation coordinates (minimum 6 decimal places; polygon for plots over 4 hectares for non-cattle commodities) for all plots of land or establishments in their supply chain.
**Deadline:** Before placing any relevant product on the market or exporting from 30 December 2026.
**Gap from current operational baseline:** *Operational implication:* Workspaces whose cargo management systems record country-of-origin data but not plot-level geolocation face a fundamental data gap. Sourcing geolocation from upstream suppliers: particularly smallholders in cocoa, coffee, rubber, and soya supply chains: requires supplier onboarding processes, data collection tools, and verification mechanisms that cannot be built at customs declaration time.

*Operational implication:* The WRI notes that for workspaces sourcing from supply chains with many smallholder producers, "securing plot-level polygon data is a supply-chain readiness gap" that requires engagement well upstream of the EU border. Indonesia, Ghana, and Vietnam are cited as countries investing in government-led geospatial verification systems, which may ease data collection for producers in those origins. *Source: World Resources Institute, "What Is the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)?", WRI, 15 May 2026. https://www.wri.org/insights/explain-eu-deforestation-regulation

### 3: Due diligence system documentation and annual review

**Scope:** Non-SME operators must maintain a formal due diligence system framework, review it at least once a year, update it when new developments arise, and keep records of updates for five years.
**Deadline:** System in place before 30 December 2026; annual review thereafter.
**Gap from current operational baseline:** *Operational implication:* Workspaces that have not previously operated a formal commodity due diligence system (separate from customs or trade compliance programs) must build documentation frameworks covering risk assessment criteria, risk mitigation procedures, supplier records, and compliance officer designation.

### 4: Compliance officer designation (non-SME operators)

Article 11(2)(a) requires "the appointment of a compliance officer at management level for non-SME operators." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 11(2)(a), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115
**Deadline:** Before 30 December 2026.
*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace qualifies as a non-SME operator (and therefore is subject to this requirement) depends on its defined role under the regulation and its SME status under Directive 2013/34/EU.

### 5: Customs declaration process modification

**Scope:** The person lodging customs declarations for relevant products entering or leaving the market must include the due diligence statement reference number before the release for free circulation or export.
**Deadline:** 30 December 2026 (when Article 26 applies); the Article 28(1) electronic interface is not expected until 30 June 2028, so manual or system-to-system reference number provision at declaration time is the interim mechanism.
**Gap from current operational baseline:** *Operational implication:* Workspaces acting as customs broker or lodging declarations as importer of record must modify their customs declaration workflows to include the EUDR DDS reference number field. Customs declarations submitted for relevant products without this reference number may result in delays or refusals by customs authorities.

### 6: Substantiated concern response capability

Article 4(5) states: "Operators that obtain or are made aware of relevant new information, including substantiated concerns, indicating that a relevant product that they have placed on the market is at risk of not complying with this Regulation shall immediately inform the competent authorities of the Member States in which they placed the relevant product on the market, as well as traders to whom they supplied the relevant product." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 4(5), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115
*Operational implication:* Workspaces must establish an internal process for receiving, triaging, and escalating substantiated concerns, including from third parties (NGOs, civil society, other operators), and for notifying competent authorities without undue delay.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

### 1: Products produced before 29 June 2023

Regulation does "not apply to relevant products listed in Annex I produced before the date indicated in Article 38(1)" (29 June 2023), with the exception of timber/timber products produced before 29 June 2023 placed on the market from 31 December 2027 (Article 37(3) carve-out). *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Articles 1(2) and 37(2) to (3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 2: Recycled/end-of-lifecycle products

Products "produced entirely from material that has completed its lifecycle and would otherwise have been discarded as waste as defined in Article 3, point (1), of Directive 2008/98/EC" are excluded. This exclusion does "not apply to certain by-products of the manufacturing process." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Annex I preamble, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 3: Private use by EU consumers

*Analytical inference:* The updated FAQs confirm that EU consumers purchasing for private use are not operators. *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures The regulation defines "in the course of a commercial activity" as "for the purpose of processing, for distribution to commercial or non-commercial consumers, or for use in the business of the operator or trader itself." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 2(19), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 4: FLEGT-licensed wood products

"Wood products which fall within the scope of Regulation (EC) No 2173/2005 that are covered by a valid FLEGT license from an operational licensing scheme shall be deemed to comply with Article 3, point (b)" (the legality requirement) only. The deforestation-free requirement (Article 3(a)) and the due diligence statement requirement (Article 3(c)) remain in force. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 10(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 5: SME operator derogation for already-subject-to-due-diligence products

SME operators are not required to exercise full due diligence (Articles 10 to 11) for relevant products that have already been subject to due diligence and for which a due diligence statement has been submitted. They provide the reference number upon request. The derogation applies only to the already-covered portion; parts not subject to prior due diligence require full due diligence. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 4(8), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 6: Authorised representative delegation

"Operators or traders may mandate an authorised representative to submit the due diligence statement … on their behalf. In such cases, the operator or trader shall retain responsibility for the compliance of the relevant product with Article 3." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 6(1), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 Additionally: "An operator that is a natural person or a microenterprise may mandate the next operator or trader further down the supply chain that is not a natural person or a microenterprise to act as an authorised representative." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 6(3), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

### 7: Proposed exemptions under draft delegated act (not yet in force)

The draft delegated act open for consultation until 1 June 2026 proposes horizontal exemptions for: samples and products used for examination, analysis, and testing; single-use and reusable packaging materials and containers; marketing and information materials; waste, used, and secondhand products; and items of correspondence. *Source: Latham & Watkins / Global ELR, "European Commission Releases New EU Deforestation Regulation Measures," Global ELR, 7 May 2026. https://www.globalelr.com/2026/05/european-commission-releases-new-eu-deforestation-regulation-measures These are proposed, not yet in force. Monitor Commission adoption.

### 8: Bamboo-based paper products

Per Annex I, pulp and paper of Chapters 47 and 48 are in scope "with the exception of bamboo-based and recovered (waste and scrap) products." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Annex I, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

**Additional grounded provisions:**
- FACT: "By way of derogation from Article 1(2) of this Regulation, the timber and timber products as defined in Article 2, point (a), of Regulation (EU) No 995/2010 that were produced before 29 June 2023 and placed on the market from 31 December 2027 shall comply with Article 3 of this Regulation." *Source: EUDR corpus capture, https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32023R1115*
- FACT: "Except for by-products of a manufacturing process, where that process involved material that was not waste as defined in Article 3, point (1), of Directive 2008/98/EC, this Regulation does not apply to goods if they are produced entirely from material that has completed its lifecycle and would otherwise have been discarded as waste as defined in Article 3, point (1), of that Directive." *Source: EUDR corpus capture, https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32023R1115*


# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

### Country-level readiness and traceability systems

Producer countries are developing traceability infrastructure that will affect supply-chain data availability for EUDR compliance. Vietnam has adopted "a national action plan prioritizing sustainable agricultural transformation" and "launched a traceability system for coffee farms, piloting geospatial verification (such as satellite images) in key producing provinces." The system "cross-references land-use maps and registration data to ensure EUDR compliance. Plans are also underway to expand it to rubber and cocoa." *Source: World Resources Institute, "What Is the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)?", WRI, 15 May 2026. https://www.wri.org/insights/explain-eu-deforestation-regulation

Indonesia, Ghana, and Vietnam are cited as countries "investing in government-led efforts to make information available to companies that must comply with the regulation." *Source: World Resources Institute, "What Is the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)?", WRI, 15 May 2026. https://www.wri.org/insights/explain-eu-deforestation-regulation

*Analytical inference:* For workspaces sourcing from these origins, government-led traceability programmes may reduce the data collection burden on individual operators by providing publicly accessible geolocation reference datasets. Monitoring these programmes and engaging government contacts in-country is a viable supply-chain strategy.

### EU Observatory on Deforestation and Forest Degradation

The Commission has established an "EU Observatory on deforestation, forest degradation, changes in the world's forest cover and associated drivers" which "should provide for land cover maps, including with time series since the cut-off date defined in this Regulation." The Observatory "should participate in the development of an early warning system combining research and monitoring capacity." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Recital 31, European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115 The Observatory is publicly accessible and provides maps and datasets. *Source: European Commission DG Environment, "Regulation on Deforestation-free Products," European Commission. https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/forests/deforestation/regulation-deforestation-free-products_en

*Operational implication:* Workspaces conducting risk assessments (Article 10) can use EU Observatory data as a public, Commission-backed source for identifying deforestation risk in specific production areas, supporting the risk assessment criteria at Article 10(2)(a) and (f).

### Third-party verification and certification schemes

The regulation permits (but does not require) the use of "certification or other third-party verified schemes" in risk assessment, "including voluntary schemes recognised by the Commission under Article 30(5) of Directive (EU) 2018/2001." These may supplement but cannot substitute for operator due diligence responsibility. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115, Article 10(2)(n), European Parliament and of the Council, 31 May 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1115

*Analytical inference:* Certification schemes (e.g., Rainforest Alliance, RSPO for palm oil, FSC/PEFC for timber) provide a partial evidence base for risk assessments but do not satisfy the full geolocation and deforestation-free documentation requirements. Workspaces relying on certification as a primary compliance tool face the risk that certifications do not meet the Article 9 information requirements.

### Team Europe Initiative on Deforestation-free Value Chains

The Commission and EU Member States (Germany, Netherlands, France) have launched a "Team Europe Initiative on Deforestation-free Value Chains … with an initial package of €70 million in funding." *Source: European Commission DG Environment, "Regulation on Deforestation-free Products," European Commission. https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/forests/deforestation/regulation-deforestation-free-products_en This initiative supports partner countries in transitioning to sustainable, deforestation-free agricultural value chains.

*Analytical inference:* This initiative may produce technical assistance, traceability tools, and capacity-building resources in producer countries that reduce compliance costs for operators sourcing from those regions over the medium term.

**Additional grounded provisions:**
- FACT: "lands and France, with an initial package of €70 million in funding to implement the Initiative. See more about the" *Source: EUDR corpus capture, https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/forests/deforestation/regulation-deforestation-free-products_en*

metadata.what_is_it: The EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR, Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650), which bars deforestation-linked cattle, cocoa, coffee, oil palm, rubber, soya and wood products from the EU market unless covered by a due diligence statement.
metadata.why_matters: It creates due diligence, geolocation, information-system registration and reporting obligations that attach to the first EU entity placing covered products on the market, with entry-into-application dates of 30 December 2026 for large and medium operators and 30 June 2027 for micro and small operators, and fines up to 4% of EU-wide turnover for non-compliance.
key_data: 4% of total annual EU-wide turnover maximum fine (Article 25(2)(a))
30 December 2026 primary compliance deadline for large/medium operators
30 June 2027 compliance deadline for micro/small operators and natural persons
9% high-risk / 3% standard-risk / 1% low-risk annual competent-authority check rates
five-year minimum record retention for due diligence documentation

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyses Australia's National Electric Vehicle Strategy (the Strategy) as a regulatory and policy framework, assessing its substantive requirements, compliance obligations, and operational implications for workspaces operating in freight forwarding, logistics, and transport-adjacent roles. The Strategy was released in April 2023 by the Australian Government (Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water, DCCEEW) and is updated annually.

**Convention notes:** The Strategy is a national strategic framework, not a single enacted statute with fixed penalties and deadlines. It operates through a combination of legislative instruments (the New Vehicle Efficiency Standard, Electric Car Discount FBT exemption), funding programs (Driving the Nation Fund), and intergovernmental collaboration agreements. Each instrument has its own operative provisions. This document synthesises obligations across all sourced instruments and flags where legal confirmation is required. The annual update for 2024-25 (see Section 15 for its citation) is the most current progress report and is treated as the primary corroborating source alongside the original Strategy document.

**Dates:** Unless otherwise stated, all sourced dates are drawn from the corpus as provided.

---

FACT (verbatim, complete): "The New Vehicle Efficiency Standard (NVES) came into effect on the 1 January 2025, and the first NVES reporting period commenced on 1 July 2025." *Source: corroborating capture. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf.

FACT (verbatim, complete): "The New Vehicle Efficiency Standard (NVES) came into effect on the 1 January 2025, and the first NVES reporting period commenced on 1 July 2025." *Source: corroborating capture. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

**The Strategy  -  plain-language summary:**

FACT: "The National Electric Vehicle Strategy (the Strategy) is part of the Australian Government's Powering Australia plan to improve affordability, create jobs, and reduce emissions. It provides a nationally consistent framework to get Australia's road transport sector on a pathway to net zero emissions." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy, DCCEEW, 2023. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy.pdf

FACT: The Strategy "sets out 3 key objectives: increase the supply of affordable and accessible EVs; establish the resources, systems and infrastructure to enable rapid EV uptake; encourage increased EV demand." *Source: The National Electric Vehicle Strategy  -  DCCEEW, https://www.dcceew.gov.au/energy/transport/national-electric-vehicle-strategy

FACT: "This Strategy focuses specifically on light passenger and light commercial vehicles, as they are the major source of road transport emissions." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy, DCCEEW, 2023. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy.pdf

FACT: "Transport makes up 19% of Australia's emissions." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy, DCCEEW, 2023. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy.pdf

**Effective date:** FACT: The Strategy was released on 19 April 2023. *Source: Australia's first National Electric Vehicle Strategy to drive cleaner, cheaper to run vehicles, Minister for Infrastructure media release, 19 April 2023. https://minister.infrastructure.gov.au/c-king/media-release/australias-first-national-electric-vehicle-strategy-drive-cleaner-cheaper-run-vehicles

**Jurisdictional scope:** FACT: The Strategy is a national framework applying across all Australian states and territories, delivered in partnership with state and territory governments. FACT: "The Strategy will be delivered in partnership with all Australian states and territories." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy, DCCEEW, 2023. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy.pdf

**Why it applies to workspaces in freight, logistics, and transport operations:**

*Operational implication:* Workspaces operating road freight fleets in Australia  -  whether light commercial, medium, or heavy vehicles  -  sit within the Strategy's broader transport decarbonisation agenda. While the Strategy's headline vehicle scope is light passenger and light commercial vehicles, its infrastructure, fleet procurement, and fuelling/charging mandates create operational conditions and cost structures that affect all road-based logistics operations.

*Operational implication:* Workspaces managing vehicle fleets on behalf of clients, or whose clients include fleet operators subject to the New Vehicle Efficiency Standard (NVES), face direct commercial and operational interface with the Strategy's requirements  -  including procurement advice, charging infrastructure access, fleet transition planning, and reporting obligations tied to fuel consumption and emissions intensity.

*Operational implication:* Workspaces managing government or quasi-government freight contracts face procurement policy requirements: FACT: "the Government has committed to ensuring Commonwealth fleet new passenger vehicle purchases and leases are 75% low emissions vehicles by 2025." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy, DCCEEW, 2023. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy.pdf

---

FACT (verbatim, complete): "Media release Wednesday 19 April 2023" *Source: corroborating capture. https://minister.infrastructure.gov.au/c-king/media-release/australias-first-national-electric-vehicle-strategy-drive-cleaner-cheaper-run-vehicles.

FACT (verbatim, complete): "Media release Wednesday 19 April 2023" *Source: corroborating capture. https://minister.infrastructure.gov.au/c-king/media-release/australias-first-national-electric-vehicle-strategy-drive-cleaner-cheaper-run-vehicles.

FACT (verbatim, complete): "Delivered in partnership with ARENA, the $523.2 million Battery Breakthrough Program will support battery manufacturers to make high-value battery products and build scale across the value chain in Australia." *Source: corroborating capture. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf.

FACT (verbatim, complete): "The Strategy sets out 3 key objectives: increase the supply of affordable and accessible EVs establish the resources, systems and infrastructure to enable rapid EV uptake encourage increased EV demand." *Source: corroborating capture. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/energy/transport/national-electric-vehicle-strategy.

FACT (verbatim, complete): "Transport makes up 19% of Australia’s emissions (DCCEEW 2022a)" *Source: corroborating capture (https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy.pdf).

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

### 1  -  MONITORING | New Vehicle Efficiency Standard (NVES) reporting period commenced

FACT: "legislation for the New Vehicle Efficiency Standard (NVES) entered into force" on 1 January 2025, "and on 1 July, the first reporting period began." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy Annual Update 2024-25, DCCEEW, October 2025. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf

**Action:** Assess whether any vehicle procurement or fleet management activities conducted on behalf of clients, or under the workspace's own fleet, intersect with NVES reporting obligations for suppliers of new light vehicles.

*Operational implication:* The NVES directly binds vehicle importers and manufacturers; *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight forwarder or logistics operator acting as importer of record for fleet vehicles constitutes an "importer" subject to NVES reporting obligations requires counsel review against the NVES's own definitions.

*Operational implication:* The NVES is estimated to "provide over $95 billion in fuel cost savings and reduce CO2 emissions by around 321 million tonnes by 2050," which signals a multi-decade structural shift in fleet economics relevant to any workspace advising clients on transport costs. *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy Annual Update 2024-25, DCCEEW, October 2025. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf

**Re-check window:** First NVES compliance reporting outcomes expected by end of 2025-26 financial year. Set monitor: Q2 2026.

---

### 2  -  ACTION REQUIRED | Commonwealth fleet low-emissions vehicle target deadline

FACT: "Commonwealth fleet new passenger vehicle purchases and leases are 75% low emissions vehicles by 2025." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy, DCCEEW, 2023. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy.pdf

**Action:** Verify the current compliance status of any Commonwealth fleet procurement contracts the workspace supports, and confirm whether vehicle supply or delivery obligations intersect with this 75% threshold.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the 75% threshold applies to the workspace as a supply-chain party (vehicle broker, fleet manager, or freight forwarder handling import of Commonwealth fleet vehicles) depends on the specific contractual role; this is a legal determination requiring counsel review.

---

### 3  -  MONITORING | Electric Car Discount FBT exemption: PHEV exclusion and mid-2027 review

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Strategy creates a compliance chain that differs by instrument:

**Vehicle supply chain (NVES):**
- Primary obligated parties: vehicle manufacturers and importers supplying new light vehicles to the Australian market.
- *Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether a freight forwarder acting as customs broker or importer of record for fleet vehicle shipments constitutes an "importer" under NVES definitions is a legal determination requiring counsel review.
- Secondary commercial impact: workspaces that source or procure vehicles for client fleet programs face changed supply dynamics as manufacturers prioritise NVES compliance.

**Fleet procurement (Commonwealth targets):**
- Primary obligated party: Commonwealth agencies.
- *Operational implication:* Workspaces holding transport or logistics service contracts with Commonwealth agencies may face indirect requirements if those agencies' fleet electrification affects the vehicles used in serviced operations.

**FBT exemption (Electric Car Discount):**
- Primary obligated party: employers providing eligible electric cars to employees under salary packaging or novated lease arrangements.
- *Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, in its role as employer, is subject to FBT obligations on vehicles provided through salary packaging arrangements, and whether those vehicles qualify for the exemption, requires ATO guidance and counsel review applied to the workspace's specific fleet composition.

**Charging infrastructure:**
- No direct compliance obligation on freight operators has been identified in the sourced corpus. Charging infrastructure obligations attach to project proponents receiving Driving the Nation Fund grants and to building operators under National Construction Code provisions.
- *Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, as a property owner or tenant operating logistics facilities, faces obligations under state-level building codes requiring EV-charging-readiness in new or renovated facilities requires state-specific counsel review.

**EV battery recycling and stewardship:**
- FACT: "DCCEEW has been progressing research on EV battery circularity. This research is expected to be completed shortly and will inform future work by governments and industry on appropriate frameworks for handling end-of-life EV batteries." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy Annual Update 2024-25, DCCEEW, October 2025. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf
- *Analytical inference:* No binding product stewardship scheme for EV batteries has been enacted as of the corpus date; the obligation trajectory points toward a future scheme whose scope and obligated parties have not been defined. Workspaces handling EV battery logistics (import, transport, storage) should monitor this development.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

### NVES Reporting

FACT: "the first NVES reporting period commenced on 1 July 2025." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy Annual Update 2024-25, DCCEEW, October 2025. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf

*Specific reporting format, submission platform, and deadline for the first NVES reporting period are not available from primary sources as of the corpus date.* The operative NVES legislation and its reporting requirements are referenced in the corpus but not reproduced in full.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether any entity in the workspace's supply chain role is an obligated NVES reporter requires review of the NVES's own definitions of "importer" and "manufacturer."

### FBT Reportable Benefits

FACT: The FBT exemption for eligible electric cars creates a reportable fringe benefit obligation: the workspace "will need to work out: the notional taxable value of the benefits associated with the private use of the exempt electric car; whether the benefit amount needs to be reported." *Source: Electric cars exemption, Australian Taxation Office. https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/fbt-on-cars-other-vehicles-parking-and-tolls/electric-cars-exemption

FACT: "The Green Vehicle Guide helps consumers by providing tools to search for and compare the environmental performance and fuel consumption of new light vehicles sold in Australia since 2004." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy Annual Update 2024-25, DCCEEW, October 2025. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf

*Operational implication:* No registration obligation on freight operators is created by these consumer information tools; however, workspaces advising clients on fleet procurement should reference these tools in client communications.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

### System 1: Fleet composition tracking and FBT categorisation

**Scope:** All BEV, PHEV, and hybrid vehicles in the workspace's fleet or under salary-packaging programs.

**Deadline:** Operative from 1 April 2025 (PHEV exclusion from FBT exemption).

**Gap from baseline:** *Operational implication:* Workspaces without vehicle-by-vehicle FBT categorisation records  -  distinguishing BEV (eligible), PHEV (ineligible from 1 April 2025), and other hybrids  -  face miscategorisation risk and potential FBT liability on vehicles incorrectly treated as exempt.

**Action:** Assess current fleet management system to confirm it captures vehicle type at the BEV/PHEV/hybrid level, records the LCT history for each vehicle, and tracks the "held and used" date for each vehicle in the fleet. Commission an ATO-compliant reconciliation if records are incomplete.

---

### System 2: EV home charging rate recordkeeping

FACT: "To make it easier for you to calculate these electricity costs, you can choose to use the shortcut EV home charging rate if you're eligible … Make sure you keep the necessary records to substantiate how you determined the cost of electricity used to charge the EV." *Source: Electric cars exemption, Australian Taxation Office. https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/fbt-on-cars-other-vehicles-parking-and-tolls/electric-cars-exemption

**Scope:** Employees who charge eligible BEVs at home.

**Deadline:** Ongoing, current FBT year.

*Operational implication:* Workspaces providing eligible BEVs under salary packaging without a system to capture home-charging percentages or kilometres driven may face ATO scrutiny on electricity cost calculations. A telematics or charge-logging system capable of distinguishing home-charging from public-charging events is the recommended baseline.

---

### System 3: NVES compliance monitoring for fleet procurement

**Scope:** Any workspace activity that involves procuring, importing, or advising on the import of new light vehicles for client fleets.

**Deadline:** NVES in force 1 January 2025; first reporting period from 1 July 2025.

*Operational implication:* Workspaces that handle customs clearance or act as importer of record for client vehicle consignments need to confirm with counsel whether NVES reporting obligations attach to that role. If they do, a system to capture vehicle CO₂ ratings and fleet-average calculations will be required.

---

### System 4: EV charging infrastructure readiness assessment for facilities

**Scope:** Owned or leased logistics facilities where new construction or major renovation may trigger National Construction Code EV-readiness provisions.

*Operational implication:* Workspaces planning to construct or substantially renovate Australian logistics facilities should commission a building code review to determine whether EV charging conduit and infrastructure provisions are required before permits are sought, as the requirement applies to "new buildings" under the October 2022 NCC update.

---

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

### Exemption 1: PHEVs  -  transitional FBT exemption conditions

FACT: PHEVs are excluded from the FBT exemption from 1 April 2025. However: "you can continue to apply the electric car exemption in certain conditions." *Source: Electric cars exemption, Australian Taxation Office. https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/fbt-on-cars-other-vehicles-parking-and-tolls/electric-cars-exemption

*Specific transitional conditions for continued PHEV FBT exemption post-1 April 2025 are not reproduced in full in the corpus as of the document date.* *Legal Confirmation Required:* The precise conditions under which a PHEV arrangement entered before 1 April 2025 may continue to qualify require ATO guidance and counsel review.

---

### Exemption 2: Heavy vehicles  -  outside NVES and Strategy primary scope

FACT: The Strategy "focuses specifically on light passenger and light commercial vehicles." Heavy freight vehicles are not within the Strategy's primary vehicle scope as of the corpus date. *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy, DCCEEW, 2023. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy.pdf

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces whose freight operations are conducted exclusively with heavy commercial vehicles (above light commercial classification) are not directly subject to NVES fleet-average CO₂ obligations as currently enacted. This is subject to change in the 2026 review.

---

### Exemption 3: Motorcycles and scooters  -  FBT exemption

FACT: "Motorcycles and scooters are not cars for FBT purposes and don't qualify for the exemption, even if they are electric." *Source: Electric cars exemption, Australian Taxation Office. https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/fringe-benefits-tax/types-of-fringe-benefits/fbt-on-cars-other-vehicles-parking-and-volls/electric-cars-exemption

*Operational implication:* Workspaces operating electric cargo bikes or scooters for last-mile delivery and providing these to employees should not claim FBT exemption on these vehicles.

---

### Exemption 4: Private charging infrastructure  -  outside Minimum Operating Standards

FACT: The Minimum Operating Standards apply only to "government-supported EV charging infrastructure projects starting on or after 1 January 2024." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy Annual Update 2024-25, DCCEEW, October 2025. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf

*Analytical inference:* Privately funded EV charging infrastructure at workspace depots or logistics facilities is not directly subject to these standards, though compliance with them may be advantageous for interoperability and future-proofing.

---

FACT (verbatim, complete): "Stamp duty is being removed for EVs (includes plug-in hybrids) up to a purchase price of $50,000, from 1 July 2022. The incentive will be in place for 5 years to 1 July 2027." *Source: corroborating capture (https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy.pdf).

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

### V2G and bidirectional charging  -  emerging operational opportunity

FACT: "In August 2024, Standards Australia issued a revised standard (AS/NZS 4777.2:2020 and 2:2024) that removes a barrier to many distribution network service providers (DNSPs) accepting V2G chargers on their networks." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy Annual Update 2024-25, DCCEEW, October 2025. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf

FACT: "In February 2025, ARENA in partnership with the RACE for 2030 Cooperative Research Centre, published the National Roadmap for Bidirectional EV Charging in Australia." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy Annual Update 2024-25, DCCEEW, October 2025. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf

*Operational implication:* Workspaces operating depot-based EV fleets have an emerging opportunity to deploy V2G-capable charging infrastructure, potentially generating revenue from grid services and reducing net energy costs. The regulatory pathway has been partly cleared by AS/NZS 4777.2:2024; commercial viability depends on network operator agreements and tariff structures not yet standardised.

---

### EV battery recycling and logistics  -  emerging sector

FACT: The National Battery Strategy (May 2024) includes "the $523.2 million Battery Breakthrough Program" to "support battery manufacturers to make high-value battery products and build scale across the value chain in Australia." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy Annual Update 2024-25, DCCEEW, October 2025. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf

*Analytical inference:* As EV adoption accelerates, the logistics of transporting, storing, and managing end-of-life EV batteries presents a growing commercial opportunity for workspaces with hazardous goods handling capability. Regulatory frameworks for this activity (dangerous goods classification for lithium batteries, storage requirements) already exist under separate regimes not covered in this corpus.

---

### Salary packaging and novated lease market size

FACT: "the National Automotive Leasing and Salary Packaging Association (NALSPA) estimates that between July 2022 and March 2025, around 109,000 EVs were financed through salary packaging." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy Annual Update 2024-25, DCCEEW, October 2025. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf

*Analytical inference:* The scale of the novated lease/salary packaging market demonstrates significant employer-facing demand for EV fleet advisory services, creating a client-conversation opportunity for workspaces with fleet procurement capabilities.

---

### Used EV market growth

FACT: "Sales of used EVs nearly doubled year-on-year to June 2025 with over 18,000 used EVs sold in 2024-25 compared to around 9,400 in 2023-24." *Source: National Electric Vehicle Strategy Annual Update 2024-25, DCCEEW, October 2025. https://www.dcceew.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/national-electric-vehicle-strategy-annual-update-2024-25.pdf

*Analytical inference:* A growing second-hand EV market expands the addressable fleet for workspaces offering fleet logistics and remarketing services, and also means more complex FBT LCT-history determinations will be required for vehicles changing hands multiple times.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyses Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156 of 13 July 2015 as a regulatory framework
instrument: an EU procedural act setting the European Union's own negotiating position within the EEA
Joint Committee, not a substantive compliance regulation in its own right. It exists to give a
freight forwarder with EEA (EU plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) exposure a single place to see
what this Decision itself commits the Union to, and what it does not yet do.

**Convention notes:** This is a short, 2-article, 7-recital Council Decision. The captured source
(267,932 characters) is a single EUR-Lex page; the overwhelming majority of that capture is EUR-Lex
site furniture and navigation, not instrument text -- the Decision's own substantive content is
exhausted by the recitals and two articles quoted verbatim below. Workspace-anchored, generic role
language is used throughout; no customer company or person is named.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "(‘the EEA Agreement’) entered into force on 1 January 1994." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156, recital 1, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32015D1156. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D1156.

FACT: "Pursuant to Article 98 of the EEA Agreement, the EEA Joint Committee may decide to amend, inter alia, Annex II to the EEA Agreement." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156, recital 2, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32015D1156. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D1156.

FACT: "The position of the Union within the EEA Joint Committee should be based on the attached draft Decision," *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156, recital 7, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32015D1156. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D1156.

*Operational implication:* This Decision only sets the EU's own negotiating position ahead of a corresponding EEA Joint Committee decision; it does not itself amend the EEA Agreement or create a compliance obligation. Once the corresponding EEA Joint Committee decision is adopted (not captured in this brief), the practical effect is that Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway become bound by the EU's batteries-and-accumulators Directive 2013/56/EU on the same terms as EU Member States, with the Liechtenstein carve-out described in Section 12 below -- relevant to any workspace tracking battery and accumulator compliance obligations across EEA-wide, not only EU, supply chains.

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 13 July 2015." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156, signature block, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32015D1156. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D1156.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The compliance chain here runs Union to EEA Joint Committee to EEA/EFTA States, not Union to a private operator directly.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Decision's own text does not itself bind an EEA/EFTA State or a private operator; whether and when Directive 2013/56/EU's battery-and-accumulator obligations become directly effective in Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway depends on the corresponding EEA Joint Committee decision, which is referenced in Article 1 but not reproduced or captured in this item's own pool.

*Analytical inference:* A workspace whose battery/accumulator supply chain touches Iceland, Liechtenstein or Norway should treat this Council Decision as the EU-side procedural predicate for that later EEA-side act, not as itself creating or timing a compliance obligation.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*Legal Confirmation Required:* The corresponding EEA Joint Committee decision that this Council Decision's Article 1 references as the attached draft is not reproduced within this Decision's own text and was not itself captured in this item's pool; its own entry-into-force and any transposition terms for Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway are not confirmed here.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**Requirement 1: The EU's negotiating position (Article 1).** FACT: "The position to be adopted, on behalf of the Union, within the EEA Joint Committee on the proposed amendment to Annex II (Technical regulations, standards, testing and certification) to the EEA Agreement shall be based on the draft decision of the EEA Joint Committee attached to this Decision." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156, Article 1, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32015D1156. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D1156.

**Requirement 2: Liechtenstein carve-out on Article 17 of Directive 2006/66/EC (recital 5).** FACT: "Given the specific legal and factual situation in Liechtenstein, Article 17 of Directive 2006/66/EC is not to apply to Liechtenstein." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156, recital 5, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32015D1156. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D1156.

**Requirement 3: Entry into force (Article 2).** FACT: "This Decision shall enter into force on the date of its adoption." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156, Article 2, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32015D1156. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D1156.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Decision. No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Decision, beyond the Liechtenstein carve-out counted above as its own obligation. No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Decision, beyond that same carve-out.

Obligations surveyed: 3; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 3.
Shortfall: the 267,932-character captured pool is overwhelmingly EUR-Lex site furniture and navigation around a 2-article, 7-recital Council position Decision; the instrument's own substantive text is exhausted by the three obligations counted above, so K remains under 5 despite the large raw capture size.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Decision itself creates no registration or reporting obligation on any operator; the corresponding EEA Joint Committee decision, not captured here, is the instrument that would carry any such obligation once adopted.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

**Liechtenstein carve-out.** FACT: "Given the specific legal and factual situation in Liechtenstein, Article 17 of Directive 2006/66/EC is not to apply to Liechtenstein." *Source: Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156, recital 5, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32015D1156. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D1156.

*Analytical inference:* This is the only stated jurisdictional carve-out in the captured text; no other exemption or edge case is stated in Recitals 1 to 7 or Articles 1 and 2.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 January 1994 | EEA Agreement entered into force | In force |
| 13 July 2015 | Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156 adopted at Brussels; entered into force the same date per Article 2 | In force |
| 15 July 2015 | Decision published in the Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 187/24) | In force |

# 15. Sources

| # | Title | Issuing Body | Type | URL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156 of 13 July 2015 on the position to be adopted, on behalf of the European Union, within the EEA Joint Committee concerning an amendment to Annex II to the EEA Agreement (Batteries and Accumulators) | Council of the European Union | Tier 1 - Binding law (Official Journal) | https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D1156 |

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

*Analytical inference:* *Status (FACT):* "A series of implementing regulations are also expected to follow, such as regulations on marine environmental protection, chemical management, environmental monitoring, etc., which would be drafted by the respective ministries." *Source: ClientEarth Asia, "China's new Environmental Code: how big of a deal is it?", March 17, 2026. https://www.clientearth.asia/latest/news/china-s-new-environmental-code-how-big-of-a-deal-is-it/

*Parties:* Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE), relevant sector ministries.
*Phase:* Announced intent; no published draft schedule as of the export date.
*Analytical inference:* Implementing regulations for chemical management are of highest direct relevance to freight forwarders moving chemical cargo. MEE regulations on environmental monitoring will determine the technical standards for MRV data that Chinese ETS-covered shippers must meet.
*Re-check window:* Q4 2026 for first MEE implementing regulation publications.

**Additional grounded provisions:**
- FACT: "China's top legislature on Thursday passed the landmark Ecological and Environmental Code" *Source: https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202603/13/content_WS69b36ae1c6d00ca5f9a09d90.html*
- FACT: "The 1,242-article code has five chapters, covering areas including pollution control, ecological protection, and green and low-carbon development." *Source: https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202603/13/content_WS69b36ae1c6d00ca5f9a09d90.html*
- FACT: "It is China’s second formal legal code, after the 2020 Civil Code" *Source: https://npcobserver.com/2026/03/11/china-npc-2026-eco-environmental-code-analysis/*


# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

*Analytical inference:* *Status (FACT):* "Local legislature will also conduct a comprehensive review of local environmental laws and regulations. Provisions that conflict with the Code will be repealed or amended in line with the Code." *Source: ClientEarth Asia, "China's new Environmental Code: how big of a deal is it?", March 17, 2026. https://www.clientearth.asia/latest/news/china-s-new-environmental-code-how-big-of-a-deal-is-it/

*Operational implication:* Provincial-level environmental rules that currently apply to the workspace's China-based facilities may be amended or repealed. Compliance postures based on local regulations should be re-verified after August 15, 2026.

**Additional grounded provisions:**
- FACT: "It is set to take effect on Aug. 15, 2026." *Source: https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202603/13/content_WS69b36ae1c6d00ca5f9a09d90.html*
- FACT: "本法自 2026 年 8 月 15 日起施行。" *Source: https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/bgt/art/2026/art_e81fe47c6817477da98d33f96fdd11a3.html*
- FACT: "The code is aligned with China's pledges to peak carbon emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060." *Source: https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202603/13/content_WS69b36ae1c6d00ca5f9a09d90.html*
- FACT: "中华人民共和国领域和中华人民共和国管辖的其他海域内的污染防治、生态保护、绿色低碳发展等生态环境保护相关活动，适用本法。" *Source: https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/bgt/art/2026/art_e81fe47c6817477da98d33f96fdd11a3.html*


# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Status (FACT):* "The Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate might also release new judicial interpretations or guidance documents to ensure effective implementation of the Code." *Source: CCICED/ClientEarth, "How China's New Environmental Code Lays the Ground for 2060 Carbon Neutrality," March 25, 2026. https://cciced.eco/climate-governance/how-chinas-new-environmental-code-lays-the-ground-for-2060-carbon-neutrality-and-aligns-with-cciced-recommendations/

*What it will decide:* How liability provisions in Part V are applied to corporate entities and individuals; scope of public interest litigation standing; interpretation of joint liability for supply chain participants.
*What the workspace should expect to need to decide:* Whether individual managers in China-registered entities require personal environmental liability coverage or indemnity arrangements.
*Re-check window:* End of 2026.

**Primary deadline slot (FACT):** "The Code's framework anticipates a transition from intensity-based benchmarks to absolute emission caps by 2027" *Operational implication:* Chinese ETS-covered manufacturing counterparties face a step-change in carbon cost exposure starting 2027; this is the first near-term dated milestone after the Code's own August 15, 2026 effective date.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Status (FACT):* "the chapter on 'green and low carbon development' lays the foundation for a climate law, which is expected to be drafted in the coming years." *Source: ClientEarth Asia, "China's new Environmental Code: how big of a deal is it?", March 17, 2026. https://www.clientearth.asia/latest/news/china-s-new-environmental-code-how-big-of-a-deal-is-it/

*Analytical inference:* The Code's Part IV is explicitly designed as a legal placeholder until a dedicated climate law provides "much needed legal specificity." No published drafting schedule exists as of the export date. The workspace should monitor NPCSC legislative planning announcements for inclusion of a climate law in the 15th NPC work programme.
*Re-check window:* Annual NPCSC legislative plan publications (typically March each year).

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*Analytical inference:* *Status (FACT):* "The Code's framework anticipates a transition from intensity-based benchmarks to absolute emission caps by 2027: a structural shift that will significantly strengthen price signals for heavy industry." *Source: AllBright Law Offices, "China's Eco-Environment Code: Codifying the Green Transformation," April 30, 2026. https://www.allbrightlaw.com/EN/10531/177523769611f595.aspx

*Operational implication:* Chinese industrial shippers on the workspace's lanes that are ETS-covered entities will face a step-change in carbon cost exposure in 2027. *Analytical inference:* This is likely to increase demand for carbon-efficient logistics options and generate client conversations about Scope 3 emissions in freight specifically.
*Re-check window:* Q1 2027 for MEE ETS rule publication on cap methodology.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*Analytical inference:* *Status (FACT):* "The main objectives of the 15th Five-Year Plan are listed in Chapter III. The climate-related objectives are to achieve the goal of carbon peaking as scheduled, to reduce the carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP by 17% by 2030, and to build a clean, low-carbon, safe and efficient new energy system." *Source: Climate-Laws.org, "15th Five-Year Plan," 2026. https://climate-laws.org/document/14th-five-year-plan_0496

*Analytical inference:* The 15th FYP's explicit energy intensity reduction target (17% CO₂ per unit GDP by 2030) creates a policy environment in which Chinese industrial counterparties face both statutory Code obligations and central government planning targets. The combination increases the probability that Chinese shippers will generate carbon performance requirements for logistics providers as part of their own supply chain emissions management.

**Additional grounded provisions:**
- FACT: "representing approximately 59% of China's stock market capitalization" *Source: https://www.allbrightlaw.com/EN/10531/177523769611f595.aspx*


# 7. Threshold Questions

## Q1: Does the Code directly regulate foreign freight forwarders operating in China?

**Status: Legal Confirmation Required.**
*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the Code's general enterprise obligations in Part I (including environmental impact obligations and the GHG reporting framework) apply to wholly foreign-owned enterprises (WFOEs) or foreign-invested entities operating logistics services within China, in the same manner as domestic enterprises, requires counsel review of the Code's jurisdictional scope provisions and China foreign investment law.

## Q2: Does the Code's ETS obligation cover road transport operators in China?

**Decided (partial):** The Code's ETS (Article 1037) currently covers "key greenhouse gas emitting entities" as defined under national regulations. *Analytical inference:* Road freight operators are not currently listed as covered sectors in published ETS rules (which cover power, steel, cement, aluminum, chemicals, paper, and aviation). Whether road freight will be added under implementing regulations is a research gap; no authoritative guidance has been published as of the export date. The workspace should track MEE ETS sector expansion publications.

## Q3: Does the Code's EPR expansion to new energy vehicles affect the workspace?

**Status: Narrow applicability.** *Analytical inference:* EPR obligations for NEV manufacturers and battery producers do not directly apply to freight forwarders unless the workspace acts as importer of record for EVs or batteries into China. Workspaces handling automotive cargo on China import lanes should confirm the specific import-of-record role.

## Q4: Does the Code's dual penalty system apply to expatriate personnel?

**Status: Legal Confirmation Required.**
*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the dual penalty provisions in Part V apply to expatriate managers or foreign nationals acting as legal representatives of Chinese-registered entities requires counsel review of the Code's enforcement scope and conflict-of-laws implications.

## Q5: Does the Code's new pollutant framework create cargo acceptance obligations for the workspace?

*Analytical inference:* **Decided (partial):** The Key Controlled New Pollutant List under Article 649 creates obligations for producers, importers, and users of listed substances. *Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether freight forwarders who accept, transport, or facilitate the import of goods containing listed substances are subject to direct obligations (rather than their shipper clients) under the Code requires counsel review.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Analytical inference:* **Statutory foundation (FACT):** Article 1037: "The State shall establish a national carbon emissions trading market. Key greenhouse gas emitting entities included in the national carbon emissions trading market shall fulfil their mandatory emission reduction responsibilities in accordance with national regulations." *Source: ClientEarth Asia, "China's new Environmental Code: how big of a deal is it?", March 17, 2026. https://www.clientearth.asia/latest/news/china-s-new-environmental-code-how-big-of-a-deal-is-it/

*Analytical inference:* **Data integrity requirement (FACT):** "Article 1037 of the Code that major greenhouse emitters are responsible for the authenticity, accuracy, and completeness of their emission statistics and annual emission reports." *Source: CCICED/ClientEarth, "How China's New Environmental Code Lays the Ground for 2060 Carbon Neutrality," March 25, 2026. https://cciced.eco/climate-governance/how-chinas-new-environmental-code-lays-the-ground-for-2060-carbon-neutrality-and-aligns-with-cciced-recommendations/

*Analytical inference:* **ETS sector coverage (FACT):** "The ETS expansion to steel, cement, and aluminum smelting (adding approximately 1,500 enterprises) was completed in 2024, raising total coverage to roughly 60% of China's GHG emissions." *Source: AllBright Law Offices, "China's Eco-Environment Code: Codifying the Green Transformation," April 30, 2026. https://www.allbrightlaw.com/EN/10531/177523769611f595.aspx

*Operational implication:* For workspaces with Chinese manufacturing clients in steel, cement, or aluminum: sectors common in industrial freight: those clients are now statutory ETS participants. Their annual verified emissions reports are legally mandated documents that the workspace may need to request for its own Scope 3 calculations.

*Analytical inference:* **MRV digitisation requirement (FACT):** "the Ecological Environment Monitoring Regulation (effective January 1, 2026) mandates automated, digitized environmental monitoring and establishes legal liability for data falsification." *Source: AllBright Law Offices, "China's Eco-Environment Code: Codifying the Green Transformation," April 30, 2026. https://www.allbrightlaw.com/EN/10531/177523769611f595.aspx

*Analytical inference:* This pre-existing digitisation mandate, now reinforced by the Code's enforcement framework, means that Chinese covered entities producing emissions data for the workspace's Scope 3 calculations are subject to legal liability for data inaccuracy. This increases (but does not guarantee) the reliability of that data compared to the prior voluntary disclosure environment.

**Additional grounded provisions:**
- FACT: "国家建立全国碳排放权交易市场。纳入全国碳排放权交易市场的温室气体重点排放单位，应当按照国家规定履行强制减排责任。" *Source: https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/bgt/art/2026/art_e81fe47c6817477da98d33f96fdd11a3.html*
- FACT: "Article 1037 of the Code that major greenhouse emitters are responsible for the authenticity, accuracy, and completeness of their emission statistics and annul emission reports." *Source: https://cciced.eco/climate-governance/how-chinas-new-environmental-code-lays-the-ground-for-2060-carbon-neutrality-and-aligns-with-cciced-recommendations/*
- FACT: "Fines: RMB 100,000 to 500,000. If the violation is not corrected, additional fines of RMB 500,000 to 1,000,000 may be imposed." *Source: https://en.reach24h.com/news/insights/chemical/china-ecological-environment-code*
- FACT: "Fines: RMB 200,000 to 1,000,000. If the violation is not corrected, additional fines of RMB 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 may be imposed." *Source: https://en.reach24h.com/news/insights/chemical/china-ecological-environment-code*
- FACT: "Part V of the Code introduces a “dual penalty” system applying sanctions simultaneously to both the enterprise and its responsible individuals" *Source: https://www.allbrightlaw.com/EN/10531/177523769611f595.aspx*
- FACT: "Part V (Legal Liability, Arts. 1052–1242) unifies civil, administrative, and criminal liability into a coordinated enforcement framework." *Source: https://www.allbrightlaw.com/EN/10531/177523769611f595.aspx*
- FACT: "Except for Chapters V and VI, the chapters of this Part are largely based on the Environmental Protection Law" *Source: https://npcobserver.com/2026/03/11/china-npc-2026-eco-environmental-code-analysis/*
- FACT: "The Code also covers climate action, and so its scope neatly aligns with the mandate of China’s Ministry of Ecology and Environment" *Source: https://www.clientearth.asia/latest/news/china-s-new-environmental-code-how-big-of-a-deal-is-it/*


*Penalty schedule (FACT):* Article 1205 (Key Controlled New Pollutants violations): "Fines: RMB 100,000 to 500,000. If the violation is not corrected, additional fines of RMB 500,000 to 1,000,000 may be imposed." Article 1206 (Environmental Management Registration Certificate violations): "Fines: RMB 200,000 to 1,000,000. If the violation is not corrected, additional fines of RMB 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 may be imposed." *Operational implication:* These are the first quantified Code-level fine ranges located in this item's pool; the ETS-specific penalty schedule referenced in Section 14 remains genuinely unquantified in the captured secondary sources (see the Shortfall note below).

No per-year phase-in schedule beyond the August 15, 2026 effective date and the 2027 ETS transition milestone (Section 3) is stated in Articles 1037, 1205 and 1206.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 8.
Shortfall: the ETS-specific (as opposed to chemical-pollutant) penalty figure is not quantified anywhere in this item's captured secondary sources.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of the export date.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

**Who registers:** Chinese entities in covered sectors (power, steel, cement, aluminum, and others as expanded by MEE rules).
**What they report:** Verified annual emissions reports; authenticity, accuracy, and completeness are statutory obligations under Article 1037.
*Specific format for workspace Scope 3 data requests not available from primary sources as of the export date.*
*Analytical inference:* The workspace should establish a contractual mechanism with Chinese ETS-covered counterparties to receive copies of verified annual emission reports for Scope 3 calculation purposes under EU CSRD or equivalent frameworks.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

**Gap from current state:** *Analytical inference:* Most freight forwarders do not currently have systematic mechanisms to collect and verify emissions data from Chinese shipper counterparties. The Code's statutory MRV obligations on Chinese ETS-covered entities create, for the first time, a legal basis for that data to exist and be accurate. The workspace should build or update its Scope 3 data collection system to include:
- A field for Chinese counterparty ETS coverage status;
- A process to request and archive verified annual emission reports from ETS-covered Chinese shippers;
- Reconciliation logic to translate Chinese CO₂-equivalent metrics (Article 1036) into the workspace's own emissions accounting framework (ISO 14083 or GLEC Framework, as applicable).

**Deadline:** No specific deadline imposed on forwarders; *Analytical inference:* alignment with Code effective date (August 15, 2026) is a reasonable internal target.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section as of the export date.*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

## EU CBAM Interaction

*Analytical inference:* The Code's carbon footprint measurement framework (Article 1036, CO₂-equivalent across all GHGs) and its statutory ETS MRV requirements create a structural alignment with EU CBAM's embedded emissions methodology. Chinese exporters of CBAM-covered goods (steel, cement, aluminum, fertilizers, electricity, hydrogen) who are also ETS-covered entities will now have statutory MRV data. However, CBAM's specific data verification and default value rules are determined by EU implementing regulation, not by the Code. Whether Chinese ETS data is directly usable for CBAM declarations is not resolved by either instrument and remains a research gap.

**No content for quantified cross-regulatory cost analysis as of the export date:** The interaction between Chinese ETS carbon prices and EU CBAM certificate prices for the same emission units requires case-specific modelling that is not available from primary sources.

## 15th Five-Year Plan Alignment

*Analytical inference:* **Five-Year Plan carbon targets (FACT):** "The climate-related objectives are to achieve the goal of carbon peaking as scheduled, to reduce the carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP by 17% by 2030, and to build a clean, low-carbon, safe and efficient new energy system." *Source: Climate-Laws.org, "15th Five-Year Plan," 2026. https://climate-laws.org/document/14th-five-year-plan_0496

*Analytical inference:* **Zero-carbon infrastructure (FACT):** The 15th FYP calls for building "about 100 national zero-carbon parks to manufacture green products with green energy, with zero-carbon transportation corridors." *Source: Climate-Laws.org, "15th Five-Year Plan," 2026. https://climate-laws.org/document/14th-five-year-plan_0496

*Analytical inference:* The zero-carbon transportation corridors target in the 15th FYP is significant for road freight operators in China. *Analytical inference:* If the workspace operates or subcontracts road freight within designated zero-carbon corridors, it may face operational equipment requirements (electric vehicles, hydrogen vehicles) ahead of a national mandate. This is a directional signal, not a current compliance obligation.

## Dedicated Climate Law: Future Instrument

*Analytical inference:* The Code is explicitly designed as a legal placeholder for a dedicated climate change law expected "in the coming years." When that law is enacted, it is expected to provide "legal specificity around the key measures for China's continued decarbonisation" beyond what the Code's Part IV currently provides. The workspace should track NPCSC legislative planning for this instrument as it represents the highest-risk future regulatory event for carbon-intensive freight operations on China lanes.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

**Penalty slot:** The Code's penalty provisions are operative from August 15, 2026. Chemical violation fines range from RMB 100,000 to RMB 2,000,000 depending on violation type and correction status (Articles 1205 to 1207). Dual penalties apply simultaneously to enterprises and responsible individuals under Part V. *Specific penalty provisions for ETS non-compliance not quantified in penalty summary as of the export date from primary sources;* the Code states consequences include "substantial fines and potential suspension of operations" but the exact ETS penalty schedule was not extracted verbatim from the source blocks. *Specific ETS penalty figure not available from primary sources as of the export date.*

*Operational implication:* The rows above consolidate every dated milestone recorded for this instrument, including the two events (CSDS disclosure, ETS 2027 transition) that originate in adjacent instruments the Code itself cross-references rather than in the Code's own text.
