entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This brief covers Commission Directive 2011/37/EU of 30 March 2011, amending Annex II to Directive 2000/53/EC on end-of-life vehicles (ELV). The instrument's entire substance is the replacement of Annex II, the list of vehicle materials and components exempted from the ELV Directive's prohibition on lead, mercury, cadmium and hexavalent chromium, together with each exemption's scope and expiry.

The brief is structured as a Regulatory Fact Document. Sections without grounded content from the source corpus are omitted with an explanatory note. All claims are labelled FACT, ANALYSIS, or LEGAL per the provenance contract. Inline citations are provided at the point of each claim.

**Convention notes:** "The ELV Directive" refers to Directive 2000/53/EC. Annex entry numbers (1(a), 8(e), 12, and so on) refer to the replacement Annex II table as enacted by this Directive. Figures are quoted exactly as rendered in the enacted text, including comma decimal separators.

**Additional grounded provisions:**
- FACT: "This Directive shall enter into force on the 20th day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037*
- FACT: "2000/53/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 September 2000 on end-of-life vehicles" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037*


# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

## Plain-Language Summary

The ELV Directive bans four heavy metals in vehicle materials and components, with a list of exemptions where their use remains technically unavoidable. This amending directive replaces that exemption list, prolonging some exemptions, closing others by date, and adding a new one for lead-containing thermoelectric materials that recover exhaust heat to cut CO2 emissions.

FACT: "Directive 2000/53/EC prohibits the use of lead, mercury, cadmium or hexavalent chromium in materials and components of vehicles put on the market after 1 July 2003, other than in cases listed in Annex II to that Directive and under the conditions specified therein." *Source: Commission Directive 2011/37/EU, European Commission, 30 March 2011. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037

FACT: "Annex II to Directive 2000/53/EC is replaced by the text set out in the Annex to this Directive." *Source: Commission Directive 2011/37/EU, European Commission, 30 March 2011. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037

FACT: "Pursuant to Article 4(2)(b) of Directive 2000/53/EC, Annex II to that Directive should be adapted to scientific and technical progress by the Commission on a regular basis." *Source: Commission Directive 2011/37/EU, European Commission, 30 March 2011. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037

*Operational implication:* For the workspace, the relevance is vertical rather than direct: automotive and spare-parts freight moves under a compliance regime where a part's legality can depend on the vehicle's type-approval date and the exemption's expiry. Shippers' declarations on automotive consignments (notably spare parts for older vehicles) sit on top of this exemption table.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**Severity: MONITORING.**

No action is required of the workspace. Obligations under this directive fall on Member States (transposition) and, through national law, on vehicle and component manufacturers. The instrument is long-transposed; its practical residue is the exemption table structure that later amendments continue to update.

**Additional grounded provisions:**
- FACT: "Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 31 December 2011 at the latest." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037*


# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The compliance chain runs: Commission (adapts Annex II to technical progress) to Member States (transpose and enforce) to vehicle manufacturers and their component suppliers (comply per material and component). The workspace touches this chain only as a carrier and forwarder of automotive goods.

FACT: "This Directive is addressed to the Member States." *Source: Commission Directive 2011/37/EU, European Commission, 30 March 2011. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No guidance documents interpreting this amending directive have been identified in the source corpus as of the date of this brief.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The replacement Annex II carries its own review clock inside the table: several exemptions state "This exemption shall be reviewed in 2014." or "This exemption shall be reviewed in 2015.", and entry 8(i) carries "This exemption shall be reviewed before 1 January 2012.". Those reviews produced later amendments to Annex II that supersede individual entries; this brief records the table as enacted by Directive 2011/37/EU.

*Analytical inference:* Any current-compliance question on a specific exemption entry must be checked against the latest Annex II amendment in force, not against this 2011 consolidation alone.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this directive impose obligations on the workspace?**

*Per the workspace's reading:* No. It is addressed to the Member States and reaches manufacturers through national transposition. Forwarder relevance is limited to the compliance context of automotive cargo.

**Q2: Are spare parts for older vehicles still allowed to contain the restricted metals?**

*Per the workspace's reading:* Within limits, yes: the annex distinguishes spare parts for vehicles put on the market before given cutoff dates, and a general note preserves the spare-parts exemption for pre-July-2003 vehicles, with named exclusions (see Exemptions and Edge Cases). *Legal Confirmation Required:* Classification of any specific automotive consignment under these entries is for the shipper and counsel, not the forwarder.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

## The Exemption Mechanism

FACT: "Vehicles put on the market before the expiry date of a given exemption may contain lead, mercury, cadmium or hexavalent chromium in materials and components listed in Annex II to Directive 2000/53/EC." *Source: Commission Directive 2011/37/EU, European Commission, 30 March 2011. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037

FACT: The tolerance floor under the annex notes: "A maximum concentration value up to 0,1 % by weight and in homogeneous material, for lead, hexavalent chromium and mercury and up to 0,01 % by weight in homogeneous material for cadmium shall be tolerated". *Source: Commission Directive 2011/37/EU, European Commission, 30 March 2011. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037

## Representative Entries of the Replacement Annex

The table spans lead as an alloying element (steels and aluminium at stated maximum lead contents such as "0,35 % lead by weight"), lead compounds in components (batteries, vibration dampers, solders, ceramics), hexavalent chromium (corrosion coatings, absorption refrigerators in motorcaravans), mercury (discharge lamps, fluorescent tubes), and cadmium (batteries for electrical vehicles), each with its scope and expiry condition.

FACT: The newly added exemption covers "Lead-containing thermoelectric materials in automotive electrical applications to reduce CO2 emissions by recuperation of exhaust heat". *Source: Commission Directive 2011/37/EU, European Commission, 30 March 2011. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037

FACT: That entry's expiry condition reads "Vehicles type approved before 1 January 2019 and spare parts for these vehicles". *Source: Commission Directive 2011/37/EU, European Commission, 30 March 2011. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037

## Spare Parts

FACT: "Spare parts put on the market after 1 July 2003 which are used for vehicles put on the market before 1 July 2003 shall be exempted from the provisions of Article 4(2)(a)". *Source: Commission Directive 2011/37/EU, European Commission, 30 March 2011. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037

**Additional grounded provisions:**
- FACT: "Continuously galvanised steel sheet containing up to 0,35 % lead by weight" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037*
- FACT: "Materials and components exempt from Article 4(2)(a)" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037*
- FACT: "Scope and expiry date of the exemption" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037*
- FACT: "Lead in solders in electrical glazing applications on glass except for soldering in laminated glazing" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037*

Obligations surveyed: 9; workspace-adjacent: 9; extracted as FACT: 9.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*This section is not applicable to the workspace's profile as a freight forwarder. The directive regulates vehicle materials and components, not services sold by the workspace.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No registration or reporting obligations are established by this amending directive. Labelling and identifiability duties for certain annex entries fall on manufacturers under Article 4(2)(b)(iv) of the ELV Directive as reflected in the annex table's labelling column.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No operational systems are established by this directive.*

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

## Edge Cases in the Annex

FACT: The repair problem that motivated the amendment: "In certain cases it is technically impossible to repair vehicles with spare parts other than original ones as this would require changes in dimensional and functional properties of entire vehicle systems." *Source: Commission Directive 2011/37/EU, European Commission, 30 March 2011. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037

FACT: The spare-parts exemption carries named exclusions: "This clause shall not apply to wheel balance weights, carbon brushes for electric motors and brake linings." *Source: Commission Directive 2011/37/EU, European Commission, 30 March 2011. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037

The annex also permits without limitation the re-use of parts already on the market at an exemption's expiry date, since re-use is not covered by the prohibition provision.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*Analytical inference:* The thermoelectric-materials exemption (entry 12) is an early instance of a pattern now common across EU product law: a restricted substance tolerated specifically because it enables a CO2-reduction technology, with a type-approval cutoff forcing eventual substitution. Comparable trade-offs appear in later Annex II reviews. No further adjacent-research material on this instrument is in the source corpus.

| 20th day following publication | Entry into force | In force |

*Sources: Commission Directive 2011/37/EU. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32011L0037

*Operational implication:* The rows above consolidate every dated milestone recorded for this instrument; only the 31 December 2011 transposition deadline and the 20th-day entry into force ever required workspace-facing action, and both are long past.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks California Senate Bill 261 (Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533), the Climate-Related Financial Risk Act, for a global freight-forwarding workspace with air-primary, road-secondary, and ocean-tertiary operations that may have California nexus. It covers the covered-entity revenue threshold, the TCFD-aligned biennial disclosure obligation, the fee, and the administrative penalty regime.

FACT: "Senate Bill No. 261 CHAPTER 383 An act to add Section 38533 to the Health and Safety Code, relating to greenhouse gases, and making an appropriation therefor. [ Approved by Governor October 07, 2023. Filed with Secretary of State October 07, 2023. ]" *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, California Health and Safety Code Section 38533. https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

SB 261 is a binding California statute, not guidance. It applies directly to a "covered entity": a business entity meeting the revenue and California-nexus tests below.

FACT: [jurisdictional_scope] SB 261 applies to entities with "total annual revenues in excess of five hundred million United States dollars ($500,000,000) and that does business in California" *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(a)(4). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

*Operational implication:* The definition of "climate-related financial risk" encompasses "capital and financial investments" and "financial markets and economic health," and the TCFD metrics pillar calls for GHG emissions disclosure (Scope 1, 2, and typically Scope 3 for logistics operations). For a freight forwarder, Scope 3 (customer shipments) dominates total emissions; building or procuring a GHG accounting system capable of producing defensible, methodology-consistent emissions data is a prerequisite for a complete TCFD disclosure.

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces that have not yet implemented ISO 14083 or GLEC Framework-aligned Scope 3 freight emissions accounting face a longer build timeline than those already running carrier-activity-based calculations.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING -- WINDOW CLOSING: first report due January 1, 2026.**

FACT: [primary_deadline] "On or before January 1, 2026, and biennially thereafter, a covered entity shall prepare a climate-related financial risk report disclosing both of the following:" *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(b)(1)(A). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

FACT: "On or before January 1, 2026, and biennially thereafter, a covered entity shall make available to the public, on its own internet website, a copy of the report required by this section." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(c)(1). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

*Operational implication:* The workspace must ensure its corporate website includes a publicly accessible, persistently available section for the SB 261 report before the January 1, 2026 deadline. The report must remain accessible between biennial filings.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The obligation runs directly to the "covered entity" itself (a company over the $500,000,000 revenue threshold with California nexus), not through a Member-State-style intermediary: if the workspace or its parent qualifies, the workspace carries the disclosure and fee duties itself.

*Operational implication:* Where the workspace includes GHG data in the report, engaging a third-party independent verifier strengthens the state board's weighting of those claims under Section 38533(b)(5). Workspaces intending to include GHG metrics should scope a verification engagement as part of the preparation timeline ahead of the January 1, 2026 deadline.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace's California freight operations, client relationships, or California-routed shipments satisfy the undefined "does business in California" element requires counsel review of California business nexus standards.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of the export date: no CARB implementing regulation, guidance document, or FAQ interpreting Section 38533 was identified in the source corpus -- CARB has not yet published its penalty regulations, fee schedule, or a climate reporting organization contract as of this brief.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

## CARB Implementing Regulations (Penalty Authority)

FACT: "The state board shall adopt regulations that authorize it to seek administrative penalties from a covered entity that fails to make the report required by this section publicly available on its internet website or publishes an inadequate or insufficient report." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(e)(2). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

GAP: Specific date for CARB penalty-regulation rulemaking not available from primary sources as of the date of this brief.

*Analytical inference:* Given the January 1, 2026 first-report deadline, CARB's implementing regulations on penalties are expected to be finalized before that date; rulemaking timelines under California's Administrative Procedure Act typically take 12 to 24 months from initiation. Re-check window: Q2 2025.

## CARB Fee Schedule

GAP: Specific fee amount and payment mechanism not available from primary sources as of the date of this brief.

*Analytical inference:* The fee is capped at CARB's actual and reasonable costs and is expected to be modest relative to compliance program costs, given the scale of the regulated universe. Re-check window: Q2 2025.

## Climate Reporting Organization Contract Award

FACT: "The state board shall contract with a climate reporting organization to prepare a biennial public report on the climate-related financial risk disclosures required by this section." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(b)(3). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

GAP: Specific contracting date or named organization not available from primary sources as of the date of this brief.

*Analytical inference:* The identity of the contracted climate reporting organization will determine the methodology and benchmarking framework against which the workspace's report is assessed publicly. Re-check window: Q3 2025.

## U.S. SEC Climate Disclosure Rule

FACT: The legislative findings note that "On March 21, 2022, the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) proposed a rule that would require publicly traded United States companies to include climate-related disclosures in their registration statements and periodic reports, including information about climate-related risks that are reasonably likely to have a material impact on their business, results of operations, or financial condition, and certain climate-related financial statement metrics in a note to their audited financial statements." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533, Legislative Findings Section 1(h). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

*Analytical inference:* The SEC's climate disclosure rulemaking, if finalized and applicable to the workspace, could satisfy SB 261's equivalent-reporting safe harbor under Section 38533(b)(4)(A).

# 7. Threshold Questions

## Q1: What is the revenue threshold for covered-entity status?

Decided. FACT: [jurisdictional_scope] Total annual revenues in excess of "five hundred million United States dollars ($500,000,000)" (calculated based on the business entity's revenue for the prior fiscal year). *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(a)(4). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

## Q2: Are insurance entities excluded?

Decided. FACT: "does not include a business entity that is subject to regulation by the Department of Insurance" *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(a)(4). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

## Q3: Can a parent company report on behalf of a qualifying subsidiary?

Decided. FACT: "Climate-related financial risk reports may be consolidated at the parent company level. If a subsidiary of a parent company qualifies as a covered entity pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (a), the subsidiary is not required to prepare a separate climate-related financial risk report." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(b)(2). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

## Q4: Does existing ISSB-aligned reporting satisfy the requirement?

Decided, with conditions. FACT: "Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a covered entity satisfies the requirements of paragraph (1) if it prepares a publicly accessible biennial report that includes climate-related financial risk disclosure information by any of the following methods: (A) Pursuant to a law, regulation, or listing requirement issued by any regulated exchange, national government, or other governmental entity, including a law or regulation issued by the United States government, incorporating disclosure requirements consistent with clause (i) of subparagraph (A) of paragraph (1), including the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards, as issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board. (B) Voluntarily using a framework that meets the requirements of clause (i) of subparagraph (A) of paragraph (1) or the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards, as issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(b)(4). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace "does business in California" for covered-entity purposes, and whether an existing annual report satisfies the "biennially" requirement, both require counsel review; the phrase is not defined in Section 38533.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

## A. Disclosure Content -- TCFD Framework

FACT: "Its climate-related financial risk, in accordance with the recommended framework and disclosures contained in the Final Report of Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (June 2017) published by the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures, or any successor thereto, or pursuant to an equivalent reporting requirement as described in paragraph (4)." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(b)(1)(A)(i). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

*Analytical inference:* The TCFD June 2017 framework organizes disclosures around four pillars: governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets. The statute also references "any successor" -- the TCFD was formally consolidated into the ISSB in 2023, making ISSB IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures the likely successor framework.

## B. Disclosure Content -- Measures to Reduce and Adapt

FACT: "Its measures adopted to reduce and adapt to climate-related financial risk disclosed pursuant to clause (i)." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(b)(1)(A)(ii). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

## C. Incomplete Disclosure Pathway

FACT: "If a covered entity does not complete a report consistent with all required disclosures pursuant to clause (i) of subparagraph (A), the covered entity shall provide the recommended disclosures to the best of its ability, provide a detailed explanation for any reporting gaps, and describe steps the covered entity will take to prepare complete disclosures." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(b)(1)(B). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

## D. Public Posting Deadline

FACT: "On or before January 1, 2026, and biennially thereafter, a covered entity shall make available to the public, on its own internet website, a copy of the report required by this section." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(c)(1). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

## E. Fee Obligation

FACT: "On or before January 1, 2026, and annually thereafter, a covered entity shall pay a fee, upon filing its disclosure, to the state board for the administration and implementation of this section." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(c)(2)(A). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

## F. GHG Verification

FACT: A covered entity's greenhouse-gas claims may be weighted by the state board "if those claims are verified by a third-party independent verifier," to the extent the report describes greenhouse gases or their voluntary mitigation. *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(b)(5). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

## G. Penalty Exposure

FACT: [penalty_summary] "The administrative penalties imposed on a reporting entity shall not exceed fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) in a reporting year." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(e)(2). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

FACT: "The state board shall adopt regulations that authorize it to seek administrative penalties from a covered entity that fails to make the report required by this section publicly available on its internet website or publishes an inadequate or insufficient report." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(e)(2). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

## H. Section 38580 Exclusion (Scope Boundary)

FACT: "Section 38580 does not apply to a violation of this section." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(e)(1). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

*Analytical inference:* Section 38580 of the California Health and Safety Code (the California Global Warming Solutions Act general penalty provision) is expressly excluded; enforcement instead runs through the administrative penalty process in Section 38533(e)(2) alone.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the January 1, 2026 first report, biennial thereafter, and the annual fee obligation from the same date). Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Section 38533, subdivisions (a) through (e), beyond the insurance-entity definitional exclusion (Section 12), which does not use the word "except" or "exempt" in the enacted text itself. Scope limits: CAPTURED above (Part H, the Section 38580 non-application clause).

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 8.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of the export date: this statute regulates entity-level financial risk disclosure, not products or services the workspace sells.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

## Report Filing and Public Posting

FACT: "On or before January 1, 2026, and biennially thereafter, a covered entity shall make available to the public, on its own internet website, a copy of the report required by this section." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(c)(1). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

*No content for this section as of the export date beyond the above: the enacted text does not establish a CARB registration portal or submission database for the reports themselves -- the public-website posting IS the filing mechanism as written. CARB's implementing regulations may add a separate submission requirement.*

## Fee Payment

FACT: "On or before January 1, 2026, and annually thereafter, a covered entity shall pay a fee, upon filing its disclosure, to the state board for the administration and implementation of this section." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(c)(2)(A). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

GAP: Specific fee amount and payment mechanism not available from primary sources as of the date of this brief.

## Reporting Content Requirements Summary

*Operational implication:* The report includes: (1) climate-related financial risk disclosure per TCFD June 2017 or successor/equivalent; (2) measures adopted to reduce and adapt to disclosed risks; (3) where incomplete, a detailed explanation of gaps and a description of steps to prepare complete disclosures; (4) where GHG data is included, optionally supported by third-party independent verification.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

## 1. Climate-Risk Data Collection and Assessment Infrastructure

*Operational implication:* The TCFD framework requires identification and assessment of physical risks (acute and chronic) and transition risks (policy, technology, market, reputational) across the workspace's operations, plus a governance structure demonstrating board and management-level oversight.

GAP: Specific cost figure for implementing a TCFD-aligned risk assessment framework not available from primary sources as of the date of this brief.

## 2. GHG Emissions Data System

*Operational implication:* Building or procuring a GHG accounting system capable of producing defensible, methodology-consistent Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions data is a prerequisite for a complete TCFD disclosure.

## 3. Public Website Publication System

FACT: "On or before January 1, 2026, and biennially thereafter, a covered entity shall make available to the public, on its own internet website, a copy of the report required by this section." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(c)(1). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

## 4. Third-Party Verification Engagement (Conditional)

*Operational implication:* Workspaces intending to include GHG metrics should scope a verification engagement as part of the preparation timeline ahead of the January 1, 2026 deadline.

## 5. Fee Payment Infrastructure

*Operational implication:* The workspace will need an internal process for identifying the annual fee obligation, tracking CARB's fee schedule publication, and routing the payment through finance.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

## Insurance-Entity Exemption

FACT: "'Covered entity' does not include a business entity that is subject to regulation by the Department of Insurance, or that is in the business of insurance in any other state." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(a)(4). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether a group entity that includes an insurance-regulated subsidiary but whose primary operations are freight forwarding qualifies for the insurance-entity exemption (in whole or in part) requires counsel review.

## Equivalent-Reporting Safe Harbor

FACT: "Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a covered entity satisfies the requirements of paragraph (1) if it prepares a publicly accessible biennial report that includes climate-related financial risk disclosure information by any of the following methods: (A) Pursuant to a law, regulation, or listing requirement issued by any regulated exchange, national government, or other governmental entity, including a law or regulation issued by the United States government, incorporating disclosure requirements consistent with clause (i) of subparagraph (A) of paragraph (1), including the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards, as issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board. (B) Voluntarily using a framework that meets the requirements of clause (i) of subparagraph (A) of paragraph (1) or the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards, as issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(b)(4). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

## Consolidation Safe Harbor

FACT: "If a subsidiary of a parent company qualifies as a covered entity pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (a), the subsidiary is not required to prepare a separate climate-related financial risk report." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(b)(2). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

*Analytical inference:* This provision only applies where the parent is also preparing a report; it does not exempt a covered-entity subsidiary from compliance where the parent is not itself a covered entity or is not producing a report.

## Section 38580 Exclusion

FACT: "Section 38580 does not apply to a violation of this section." *Source: SB 261, Chapter 383, Health and Safety Code Section 38533(e)(1). https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202320240SB261

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section as of the export date beyond the related-instrument note: California SB 253 (the Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act, enacted the same legislative cycle) imposes Scope 1, 2, and 3 GHG reporting obligations on a different, higher revenue threshold population and directly intersects with SB 261's GHG content and verification provisions; SB 253's own enacted text is not in this item's captured pool, so no FACT claim is grounded from it here (see Section 15's candidate-source listing).*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- October 7, 2023: SB 261 approved by the Governor and filed with the Secretary of State; Chapter 383 enacted.
- January 1, 2026: first biennial climate-related financial risk report due; the covered entity prepares the report, makes it publicly available on its own website, and pays the fee to CARB.
- January 1, 2028: second biennial report due, and biennially thereafter.

*Pending, no sourced date: CARB penalty regulations; CARB fee schedule; climate reporting organization contract award.*

*Sources: SB 261, Chapter 383, California Health and Safety Code Section 38533.*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyses Commission Regulation (EU) No 100/2014 of 5 February 2014, which replaces
in full the Annex to Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 -- the list of aircraft operators that performed an
aviation activity under the EU Emissions Trading System (Directive 2003/87/EC) on or after 1 January
2006, together with the Member State administering each operator's compliance obligations under the
scheme.

**Convention notes:** The Regulation's own enacting text is two short Articles; its overwhelming
substantive content is the replaced Annex itself (a per-operator lookup table of administering Member
States), captured in full in this item's pool (225,938 characters) but not itself a source of
additional generalizable obligations beyond the replacement fact captured below -- an operator's own
row in that table is a lookup result, not a separately-stated compliance duty. Workspace-anchored,
generic role language is used throughout.

FACT: "COMMISSION REGULATION (EU) No 100/2014 of 5 February 2014 amending Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 on the list of aircraft operators that performed an aviation activity listed in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on or after 1 January 2006 specifying the administering Member State for each aircraft operator" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 100/2014, title, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32014R0100. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0100.

FACT: "6.2.2014 EN Official Journal of the European Union L 37/1" *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 100/2014, Official Journal heading, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32014R0100. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0100.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Having regard to Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 October 2003 establishing a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Community and amending Council Directive 96/61/EC ( 1 ) , and in particular Article 18a(3)(b) thereof," *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 100/2014, citations, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32014R0100. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0100.

Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 maintains the list that tells each aircraft operator within scope of the
EU aviation emissions-trading rules which Member State administers its compliance obligations. This
Regulation replaces that entire list (via a new Annex) to reflect an updated set of aircraft operators
and administering Member States.

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 5 February 2014." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 100/2014, signature block, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32014R0100. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0100.

*Operational implication:* Aircraft operators subject to the EU Emissions Trading Scheme for aviation
should check the replaced Annex to confirm which Member State now administers their compliance
obligations, since this Regulation replaces the entire prior list rather than amending individual
entries.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "The inclusion of an aircraft operator in the Union’s emissions trading scheme is dependent upon the performance of an aviation activity as set out in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC and is not dependent on the inclusion in the list of aircraft operators established by the Commission on the basis of Article 18a(3) of that Directive." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 100/2014, recital 4, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32014R0100. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0100.

*Analytical inference:* An aircraft operator's substantive ETS obligations run from performing an
aviation activity under Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC, not from this Regulation's own administering-
Member-State list; the list is an administrative allocation mechanism, not the source of the underlying
compliance obligation. A workspace whose clients operate aircraft under the EU ETS should treat this
Regulation as confirming WHICH Member State administers a given operator, not WHETHER that operator is
in scope.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "In establishing the updated list of the aircraft operators to include aircraft operators which performed an aviation activity listed in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC in 2013, account has been taken of the fleet list declarations provided to the Commission by aircraft operators and service companies. However, a number of management or service companies and aircraft registration markings appear in the updated list instead of aircraft operators due to a lack of information provided." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 100/2014, recital 5, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32014R0100. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0100.

*Analytical inference:* The recital's own correction rationale (management/service-company names and
aircraft registration markings previously appearing in place of the actual operator) signals that an
operator whose compliance role is administered through a service company or leasing structure should
independently confirm its own correct listing under the replaced Annex, rather than assuming a prior
listing was accurate.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**Requirement 1: Binding, directly applicable effect (final provisions).** FACT: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 100/2014, final provisions, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32014R0100. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0100.

**Requirement 2: Annex replacement (Article 1).** FACT: "The Annex to Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 is replaced by the Annex to this Regulation." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 100/2014, Article 1, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32014R0100. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0100.

**Requirement 3: Entry into force (Article 2).** FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 100/2014, Article 2, EUR-Lex, CELEX:32014R0100. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0100.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Regulation. No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Regulation. No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Regulation.

Obligations surveyed: 3; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 3.
Shortfall: the 225,938-character captured pool is almost entirely the replaced Annex itself (a per-operator administering-Member-State lookup table), which the Regulation's own two-Article enacting text (Article 1 replacing the Annex, Article 2 entry into force) does not further subdivide into additional generalizable obligations; the individual Annex rows are lookup results, not separately stated compliance duties, so K remains under 5 despite the large raw capture size.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Regulation creates no registration or reporting obligation beyond the Annex replacement itself (Section 8); whether a specific aircraft operator's own reporting cadence under Directive 2003/87/EC changes as a result of a different administering Member State is a fact-specific question outside this item's captured pool.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 5 February 2014 | Commission Regulation (EU) No 100/2014 done at Brussels | In force |
| 6 February 2014 | Published in the Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 37/1) | In force |
| 9 February 2014 | Regulation entered into force (third day following OJ publication, per Article 2) | In force |

# 15. Sources

| # | Title | Issuing Body | Type | URL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Commission Regulation (EU) No 100/2014 of 5 February 2014 amending Regulation (EC) No 748/2009 on the list of aircraft operators that performed an aviation activity listed in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC | European Commission | Tier 1 - Binding law (Official Journal) | https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0100 |

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks EU Commission Proposal COM(2023)441 (procedure 2023/0266(COD)), a proposed Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the accounting of greenhouse gas emissions of transport services, for a freight-forwarding workspace operating air (primary), road (secondary), and ocean (tertiary) modes.

**Convention note.** COM(2023)441 is a legislative proposal, not yet an adopted regulation. All provisions described below are proposed requirements subject to change through the EU ordinary legislative procedure (co-decision, Parliament and Council). No provision is binding law until formally adopted and published in the Official Journal.

**Source coverage note.** The primary EUR-Lex source URL originally supplied returned a "Page Not Found" error and yielded no recoverable text. The secondary EUR-Lex CELEX source returned the full EUR-Lex landing page including substantial explanatory memorandum text; all FACT claims in this brief are span-grounded to that source. The eumonitor.eu and umweltbundesamt.de captures returned interface/navigation content only and yielded no groundable substantive claims; recorded as non-contributing.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: [effective_date] "Strasbourg, 11.7.2023 COM(2023) 441 final 2023/0266(COD) Proposal for a REGULATION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL on the accounting of greenhouse gas emissions of transport services" *Source: EUR-Lex landing page for 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

FACT: The proposal's stated objective is that "transparent information on emissions of transport services empowers customers to make well-informed choices and influences business decisions of entities organising and providing these services on the market." *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

FACT: "there is currently no universally accepted framework for greenhouse gas emissions accounting of transport services" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

FACT: "I t is estimated that almost 600,000 entities in the EU transport sector measure their greenhouse gas emissions (2020), but only 21,660 of these do it at the disaggregated level needed to produce greenhouse gas emissions data of transport services. This is only 1.2% of approximately 1.8 million entities performing transport operations on their own" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

*Analytical inference:* The proposal explicitly identifies "transport service organisers, including operators" as the category of entities that "do not systematically calculate their greenhouse gas emissions" and whose behaviour the regulation is designed to change. A freight forwarder organising multi-modal shipments on behalf of shippers is, in the proposal's framing, precisely a "transport service organiser." If adopted, this regulation would represent the first binding EU-level obligation to calculate and communicate emissions at the transport-service level for that class of entity.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the workspace, acting as freight forwarder rather than carrier or operator of record, is classified as a "transport service organiser" or a "transport service user" under the proposed regulation's operative definitions requires legal review of the proposal's full operative text, which is not reproduced in the available source content.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING -- Begin internal baseline assessment now, before the regulation is adopted.**

FACT: "easure their emissions in some way, but only 35% (9 out of 26) of those that measure do it at transport service lev" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

*Operational implication:* For a freight forwarder whose clients increasingly request emissions data at the shipment level, a baseline assessment of current data availability (carrier-level emission factors, fuel consumption data per flight or leg, load factor assumptions) identifies the gap between current data infrastructure and likely regulatory requirements before the compliance clock starts.

**MONITORING -- Review ISO 14083:2023 alignment.**

FACT: "ed this new standard ISO 14083 :2023 in March 2023 . S ubsequently , CEN   transposed   it   as" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

*Operational implication:* ISO 14083:2023 is the technical standard the proposal explicitly builds upon. Workspaces that adopt ISO 14083-aligned emissions accounting before the regulation is finalised will face lower compliance transition costs.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "transport service organisers, including operators, do not systematically calculate their greenhouse gas emissions" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

*Analytical inference:* A freight forwarder organising multi-modal shipments on behalf of cargo principals (selecting carriers, booking capacity, consolidating shipments) performs the function of a "transport service organiser" in the plain meaning of that term as used in the proposal. If the final regulation follows the proposal's intent, the workspace's organiser role places it within the regulated population, not merely as a downstream data recipient.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* The precise placement of a freight forwarder in the compliance chain (obligated reporting entity, pass-through recipient of carrier-generated data, or both depending on transaction structure) requires legal review of the proposal's operative articles, which are not reproduced in the available source content.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of the export date: COM(2023)441 is a legislative proposal under procedure 2023/0266(COD); no adopted regulation text or authoritative implementing guidance has been published. Analysis of operative articles is not possible from the available source content, which contains the explanatory memorandum but not the full operative text.*

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: [primary_deadline] "Strasbourg, 11.7.2023 COM(2023) 441 final 2023/0266(COD) Proposal for a REGULATION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL on the accounting of greenhouse gas emissions of transport services" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

*Analytical inference:* Under the ordinary legislative procedure, the European Parliament and Council each produce positions, and a trilogue negotiation typically follows; for transport-sector regulations of comparable scope this process has historically taken 18 to 36 months from proposal publication. This is an inference from institutional process norms, not a sourced date.

GAP: The regulation's adoption date and Official Journal publication date are not available from primary sources as of the date of generation.

GAP: Entry into force and any compliance deadline are not available from primary sources as of the date of generation: COM(2023)441 remains a legislative proposal under procedure 2023/0266(COD), not yet adopted.

**Re-check window:** re-assess this brief when the European Parliament's rapporteur publishes their report or the Council adopts its general approach, whichever occurs first.

# 7. Threshold Questions

## Question 1: What entities are obligated?

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether a freight forwarder is classified as organiser, user, or both, and what specific obligation attaches to each classification, requires legal review of the operative text, which is not reproduced in the available source content.

## Question 2: Which transport modes are in scope?

FACT: [jurisdictional_scope] "It sets out a common regulatory framework for greenhouse gas emissions accounting of transport services across the entire multimodal transport chain" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

*Analytical inference:* All three modes in the workspace's priority stack (air, road, ocean) appear to be within scope. Mode-specific carve-outs or phase-in timelines are not recoverable from the available source content.

## Question 3: What is the calculation methodology?

FACT: "selecting an emissions calculation method and default data based on what is more beneficial for an individual enti ty. This creat es conditions for greenwashing" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

## Question 4: Do SME exemptions or reduced obligations apply?

FACT: "The l ow uptake of greenhouse gas emissions accounting is mainly observed among micro-, small- and medium- sized enterprises (SME s ) 7 , which represent the vast majority of entities operating i n the EU transport market" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

*Analytical inference:* This framing suggests the proposal's authors were aware of SME capacity constraints and that the final regulation may include differentiated obligations or transition periods for smaller entities.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether any SME threshold exemption applies to the workspace requires legal review of the operative articles and the workspace's corporate classification.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*No adopted operative text is available for this section: the proposal is in the legislative procedure under 2023/0266(COD), and the available source content is the explanatory memorandum only. The following are drawn from the explanatory memorandum's stated policy intent, not binding operative requirements.*

## A. Stated Intent -- Transport-Service-Level Emissions Calculation

FACT: The explanatory memorandum states that "only the latter type of information is relevant to effectively support and influence transport service users" decisions, identifying this as the level at which emissions data must be generated. *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

*Operational implication:* For the workspace, this means the proposed standard is not satisfied by company-level or vehicle-level emissions reporting; the data unit would be the individual transport service -- a specific shipment or leg.

## B. Stated Intent -- Greenwashing Prevention

FACT: "selecting an emissions calculation method and default data based on what is more beneficial for an individual enti ty. This creat es conditions for greenwashing" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

*Operational implication:* Workspaces that currently use emissions figures from carrier marketing materials or self-selected methodologies face the highest restatement risk when a mandatory harmonised methodology enters force.

## C. Stated Intent -- Harmonised Methodology

FACT: "emissions should be quantified based on a scientifically sound, detailed and harmonised methodological approach" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

## D. Stated Scope Boundary

FACT: The explanatory memorandum states that "consequences   are   out of scope of the proposed initiative." (referring to air pollutant and noise emissions and their subsequent health and environmental impact, which the proposal treats as separate from its greenhouse-gas accounting objective). *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

## E. Penalty Provisions

GAP: Penalty and enforcement provisions are not available from primary sources as of the date of generation: the available source content is the explanatory memorandum only, and the operative articles that would set out sanctions are not reproduced in it.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Sections A through D above (the proposal has no adopted timeline of its own; see Section 6, GAP). Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Sections A through D above. Scope limits: CAPTURED above (Part D, the explanatory memorandum's own "out of scope" statement regarding non-GHG pollutant and noise impacts).

Obligations surveyed: 4; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 4.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of the export date: the workspace does not sell regulated products in scope of this proposal; the proposal targets service-level accounting obligations on transport-sector entities, not product-level compliance.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The operative articles governing registration of obligated entities, reporting periodicity, and submission formats are not reproduced in the available source content; what the explanatory memorandum does state is the evidential base for the proposal's reporting architecture.

FACT: "The b enefits and added value of emissions accounting are demonstrated by the results of existing emissions monitoring and reporting schemes in the EU and beyond" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

*Analytical inference:* The reporting architecture will likely require transport service organisers and operators to calculate and communicate emissions per service unit (shipment or leg) to their clients or to a competent authority, in a format aligned with ISO 14083:2023. Whether this is a client-facing disclosure obligation, a regulator-filing obligation, or both is not determinable from the available source content.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

The following gaps are identified from the explanatory memorandum's problem framing, not from operative articles.

**Gap 1 -- Shipment-level emissions calculation capability.**

FACT: "only 21,660 of these do it at the disaggregated level needed to produce greenhouse gas emissions data of transport services. This is only 1.2% of approximately 1.8 million entities performing transport operations on their own" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

*Operational implication:* For workspaces operating without a shipment-level emissions calculation system, the gap between current state and the regulation's intended unit of account is the fundamental infrastructure challenge: per-leg emissions calculation using actual or default emission factors per ISO 14083:2023, aggregated per transport service for each client shipment.

**Gap 2 -- Carrier data integration.**

*Analytical inference:* ISO 14083:2023 prioritises actual fuel consumption data over default values. The workspace will need to build or buy data feeds from carrier partners, or negotiate data access clauses in carrier contracts, to meet an actual-data standard.

**Gap 3 -- Client disclosure infrastructure.**

*Analytical inference:* If the regulation imposes a disclosure obligation toward transport service users (shippers), the workspace will need a mechanism to produce per-shipment emissions certificates or data outputs aligned with the harmonised methodology.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*No content for this section as of the export date: no operative exemptions are recoverable from the available source content, which contains only the explanatory memorandum, not the operative articles.*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "The b enefits and added value of emissions accounting are demonstrated by the results of existing emissions monitoring and reporting schemes in the EU and beyond" -- specifically, the proposal identifies two EU-funded research projects as foundational to the proposal's methodology: Carbon Footprint of Freight Transport (COFRET) under FP7, and Logistics Emissions Accounting and Reduction Network (LEARN) under Horizon 2020. *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

FACT: "ed this new standard ISO 14083 :2023 in March 2023 . S ubsequently , CEN   transposed   it   as" *Source: EUR-Lex 52023PC0441, European Commission, 11 July 2023. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52023PC0441

*Analytical inference:* ISO 14083:2023 and the Global Logistics Emissions Council (GLEC) Framework represent the current best-available alternative methodology for workspaces that wish to calculate and disclose transport emissions ahead of regulatory adoption. Adopting ISO 14083 now provides a defensible, internationally recognised basis for client emissions disclosures while the EU regulation is finalised.

*Industry interpretation:* Smart Freight Centre (the GLEC framework custodian) and CEN-CENELEC (active on EN ISO 14083 standardisation) are the primary institutional actors advancing the technical underpinning of this regulation in the pre-adoption period.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- March 2023: ISO 14083:2023 published, the technical standard the proposal builds upon.
- 11 July 2023: COM(2023)441 published by the European Commission, opening the ordinary legislative procedure under reference 2023/0266(COD).

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This brief analyses the GLEC Framework v3 (2023 edition, revised and updated), published by Smart Freight Centre (SFC) as the third version of the Global Logistics Emissions Council Framework for Logistics Emissions Accounting and Reporting. The brief applies the framework's requirements, methods, and implications to workspaces operating in freight forwarding, logistics service provision, and supply chain roles spanning air-primary, road-secondary, and ocean-tertiary transport modes.

**Convention notes:**
- The GLEC Framework v3 is a **voluntary industry standard**, not binding legislation. All obligations described below are framework requirements for conformance claims; none are legally mandatory under statute. The distinction between "conformance requirements" and "legal obligations" is maintained throughout.
- The Framework is co-aligned with ISO 14083:2023, which is a published international standard. References to ISO 14083 chapters are drawn from the Framework text, which incorporates and references ISO 14083 provisions throughout.
- "The workspace" refers generically to the freight forwarding or logistics service operation described in the workspace profile. No individual, company, or product is named.
- Dates of source publication: GLEC Framework v3.0, revised and updated (2023).

*Source: Global Logistics Emissions Council Framework for Logistics Emissions Accounting and Reporting, v3.0 edition, revised and updated, Smart Freight Centre, 2023. https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3_UPDATED_13_12_23.pdf

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

### What the Framework Is

The GLEC Framework v3 is a voluntary methodology standard for the calculation and reporting of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions arising from freight transport chains and logistics hub operations. It was first published in 2016; the third version integrates the provisions of ISO 14083:2023: *Greenhouse gases: Quantification and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions arising from transport chain operations*: which was published in 2023 following a development process that began in 2019.

FACT: "The GLEC Framework v3 guides and supports companies in implementing transparency on the efficiency of their supply chains and logistics. It offers an easy-to-use approach to an ISO 14083-compliant calculation of GHG emissions from transport, covering the transport itself as well as logistics hubs and the emissions from the energy supply to them both." *Source: GLEC Framework v3.0, Smart Freight Centre, 2023, p. 2. https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3_UPDATED_13_12_23.pdf

FACT: "Following its publication, we have integrated the provisions of ISO 14083:2023 back into the GLEC Framework. The outcome, GLEC Framework v3, is now in front of you." *Source: GLEC Framework v3.0, Smart Freight Centre, 2023, p. 2. https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3_UPDATED_13_12_23.pdf

### Effective Date

FACT: The GLEC Framework v3.0 revised and updated edition was published in 2023. ISBN 978-90-833629-0-8. This is the current operative version.

No compliance deadline: the source presents this as a voluntary standard with no mandated adoption date as of the export date. The Framework does not impose a statutory compliance deadline on any entity. See penalty_summary below for the full gap statement.

### Jurisdictional Scope

FACT: "It covers transport operations from national to international levels, anywhere in the world." *Source: GLEC Framework v3.0, Smart Freight Centre, 2023, Section 1 Chapter 1. https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3_UPDATED_13_12_23.pdf

The Framework is globally applicable and is not restricted to any jurisdiction, regulatory zone, or trade bloc. It is, however, the recommended methodology for CDP reporting and SBTi target-setting, both of which carry their own program-specific requirements (see Registration and Reporting Obligations).

### Penalty Summary

No penalty: the source presents this as a voluntary standard / non-binding framework with no enforcement mechanism as of the export date. The Framework contains no fines, sanctions, or enforcement provisions. Non-adoption does not trigger any regulatory consequence under the Framework itself. *Source: GLEC Framework v3.0, Smart Freight Centre, 2023. https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3_UPDATED_13_12_23.pdf

*Operational implication:* While no direct penalty exists under the Framework, non-adoption carries indirect commercial risk: the Framework is the recommended method for logistics emission reporting to CDP and SBTi, and CDP questionnaire compliance and SBTi transport target-setting both reference GLEC/ISO 14083 methodology. Workspaces that cannot demonstrate GLEC-conformant reporting may face disadvantage in client procurement processes that reference CDP scores or SBTi alignment. *Source: GLEC Framework v3.0, Smart Freight Centre, 2023, Section 2 Chapter 1 and Chapter 3. https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3_UPDATED_13_12_23.pdf

### Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Covering the entire transport chain, the Framework works for carriers, logistics service providers (LSPs) and shippers as well as other end-users of emissions information, such as governments, investors and green freight programs." *Source: GLEC Framework v3.0, Smart Freight Centre, 2023, Introduction. https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3_UPDATED_13_12_23.pdf

FACT: "The GLEC Framework aligns with ISO 14083 and is recognized by the Greenhouse Gas Protocol. It is the recommended method for reporting logistics emissions to the Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP) and for setting targets in line with the Science-Based Targets initiative (SBTi)." *Source: GLEC Framework v3.0, Smart Freight Centre, 2023, Introduction. https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3_UPDATED_13_12_23.pdf

*Operational implication:* For workspaces operating as freight forwarders, LSPs, or as purchasers of transport services across air, road, and ocean modes, the Framework defines both how the workspace calculates its own Scope 1/2/3 emissions and what emission data it can credibly demand from subcontracted carriers and pass to shipper clients. Inability to produce or receive GLEC-conformant emission data constitutes a gap in the data the workspace can report to CDP or provide to clients setting SBTi targets.

**Additional grounded provisions:**
- FACT: "Leading multinationals have committed to implementing the GLEC Framework through joining the SFC community. 150+" *Source: GLEC Framework v3.0, Smart Freight Centre, 2023, https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3_UPDATED_13_12_23.pdf*
